<!-- end proof-16 -->
<!-- lemma-12: body_md -->
\label{l.chart_hamiltonian_expansion}
Fix $L\geqslant1$. Under the couplings described above, we have
\begin{align}
    &H_{N+M}^{x,q}\left((S_{r_N(\tau)}\sigma,\tau),\alpha\right)+\widetilde V_N^{x,y,q}(\sigma,\alpha)\notag\\
    &\qquad\mathrel{\hstretch{1.8}{\approx}}\widetilde H_N^{x,q}(r_N(\tau);\sigma,\alpha)+\widetilde V_N^{x,y,q}(\sigma,\alpha)+\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}\sum_{j\in\mathsf M_s}\tau_j\mathsf X^q_{N,j}(\sigma,\alpha)-\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}\vartheta^s|\tau^{(s)}|^2,
    \label{e.chart_H_decomposition}
\end{align}
uniformly over $x,y,q$ and $(\sigma,\tau,\alpha)\in\Sigma_N\times\{|\tau|\leqslant L+1\}\times\mathfrak U$.
<!-- end lemma-12 -->
<!-- proof-17: body_md -->
Write $\widetilde\sigma:=S_{r_N(\tau)}\sigma$ and $\rho:=(\widetilde\sigma,\tau)$, and recall from~\eqref{e.r_N_close_to_one} that $|r_N(\tau)-\vec{\mathbf{1}}|\leqslant CN^{-1}$ on the range of $\tau$ considered. We go through the terms of $H_{N+M}^{x,q}(\rho,\alpha)$ in~\eqref{e.perturbed_enriched_H} and~\eqref{e.enriched_H}, at size $N+M$. The term $\widetilde V_N^{x,y,q}$ is the same on both sides of~\eqref{e.chart_H_decomposition}; since it is not independent of the other fields, we must also keep track of its cross-covariances with the terms that we modify.

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{Interaction field.}\quad By~\eqref{e.interaction_decomposition},
\begin{equation*}
    \sqrt{2t}H_{N+M}(\rho)=\sqrt{2t}\widetilde H_N(\widetilde\sigma)+\sqrt{2t}\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}\sum_{j\in\mathsf M_s}\tau_j\widetilde{\mathsf Z}_{N,j}(\widetilde\sigma)+\sqrt{2t}\widetilde D_N(\widetilde\sigma,\tau).
\end{equation*}
The first term is the interaction part of $\widetilde H_N^{x,q}(r_N(\tau);\sigma,\alpha)$ in~\eqref{e.radially_evaluated_H}. The last two terms are independent of all the other fields. By~\eqref{e.D_covariance_residual} and~\eqref{e.overlap_split}, the variance of $\widetilde D_N(\widetilde\sigma,\tau)$ is bounded by $(N+M)\sup|D^2\xi|\,|\mathsf b_N(\tau,\tau)|^2\leqslant C_LN^{-1}$, so that $\widetilde D_N(\widetilde\sigma,\tau)\stackrel{0,N^{-1}}{\mathrel{\hstretch{1.8}{\approx}}}0$. By~\eqref{e.D_MN_explicit}, \eqref{e.overlap_dilation}, and the Lipschitz continuity of $\nabla\xi$, the covariance of $\widetilde{\mathsf Z}_{N,j}(\widetilde\sigma)$ and $\widetilde{\mathsf Z}_{N,j}(\widetilde\sigma')$ is
\begin{equation*}
    \partial_s\xi\left(\Big(\tfrac{N}{N+M}\sqrt{r^u_N(\tau)r^u_N(\tau')}\,R_{N,u}(\sigma,\sigma')\Big)_{u\in\mathscr{S}}\right)=\partial_s\xi\left(R_N(\sigma,\sigma')\right)+O(N^{-1}),
\end{equation*}
uniformly over the range considered, and the same holds after multiplication by $\tau_j\tau'_j$. Comparing with~\eqref{e.Z_Nj_covariance}, we obtain
\begin{equation*}
    \sqrt{2t}\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}\sum_{j\in\mathsf M_s}\tau_j\widetilde{\mathsf Z}_{N,j}(\widetilde\sigma)+\sqrt{2t}\widetilde D_N(\widetilde\sigma,\tau)\stackrel{0,N^{-1}}{\mathrel{\hstretch{1.8}{\approx}}}\sqrt{2t}\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}\sum_{j\in\mathsf M_s}\tau_j\mathsf Z_{N,j}(\sigma),
\end{equation*}
and both sides are independent of all the other fields.

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{Self-overlap corrections.}\quad Since $\rho\in\Sigma_{N+M}$, the interaction correction in $H^{x,q}_{N+M}$ is $-(N+M)t\xi(\lambda)$. On the other hand, by~\eqref{e.overlap_dilation} and~\eqref{e.radial_factor}, $R_{N,s}(\widetilde\sigma,\widetilde\sigma)=r_N^s(\tau)\lambda_s$, so that $\mathsf a_N(\widetilde\sigma,\widetilde\sigma)=\lambda-(|\tau^{(s)}|^2/(N+M))_{s\in\mathscr{S}}$. The interaction correction in $\widetilde H_N^{x,q}(r_N(\tau);\sigma,\alpha)$ is therefore
\begin{align*}
    -Nt\widetilde\xi_N\left(R_N(\widetilde\sigma,\widetilde\sigma)\right)
    &=-(N+M)t\xi\left(\lambda-\big(\tfrac{|\tau^{(s)}|^2}{N+M}\big)_{s\in\mathscr{S}}\right)\\
    &=-(N+M)t\xi(\lambda)+t\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}\partial_s\xi(\lambda)|\tau^{(s)}|^2+O_L(N^{-1}),
\end{align*}
by Taylor's formula. Similarly, the cascade correction at size $N+M$ is $-\sum_sq^s(1)(N_s+M_s)$, while that in $\widetilde H_N^{x,q}(r_N(\tau);\sigma,\alpha)$ is $-\sum_sq^s(1)|\widetilde\sigma^{(s)}|^2=-\sum_sq^s(1)(N_s+M_s-|\tau^{(s)}|^2)$. Taking the difference of the two sides and recalling~\eqref{e.prelimit_vartheta_def}, the deterministic corrections account for the term $-\sum_s\vartheta^s|\tau^{(s)}|^2$ in~\eqref{e.chart_H_decomposition}, up to an error $O_L(N^{-1})$.

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{Cascade and external fields.}\quad By~\eqref{e.cascade_decomposition}, $\sqrt2W_{N+M}^q(\rho,\alpha)=\sqrt2W_N^q(\widetilde\sigma,\alpha)+\sqrt2\sum_s\sum_{j\in\mathsf M_s}\tau_jw_j^{q^s}(\alpha)$, where the first term is the cascade part of $\widetilde H_N^{x,q}(r_N(\tau);\sigma,\alpha)$ and the second is the cascade part of $\sum_j\tau_j\mathsf X^q_{N,j}$. The external field decomposes in the same way, producing the terms $h^s\tau_j$ in $\mathsf X^q_{N,j}$. These decompositions are exact.

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{Perturbation field.}\quad It remains to compare $\eta_{N+M}H^x_{N+M}(\rho,\alpha)$ with $\eta_NH^x_N(\widetilde\sigma,\alpha)$, which is the perturbation part of $\widetilde H_N^{x,q}(r_N(\tau);\sigma,\alpha)$. Both are independent of all the fields considered so far, but not of $\widetilde V_N^{x,y,q}$, which contains the term $2\eta_N^2\sum_sy^s\partial_{r^s}H_N^x(S_r\sigma,\alpha)|_{r=\vec{\mathbf{1}}}$. By~\eqref{e.overlap_perturbation_covariance}, \eqref{e.overlap_perturbation_cross_covariance}, and Lemma~\ref{l.comput_cov_radial}, all the relevant covariances are obtained by evaluating and differentiating the kernels $\mathsf C_{\mathsf h}$ at overlaps that differ from $R_N(\sigma,\sigma')$ by $O_L(N^{-1})$, by~\eqref{e.full_and_bulk_overlap_bound} and~\eqref{e.overlap_dilation}, with prefactors $(N+M)\eta_{N+M}^2$, $(N(N+M))^{1/2}\eta_{N+M}\eta_N$, or $N\eta_N^2$, which differ from one another by $O(N|\eta_{N+M}-\eta_N|+\eta_N^2)$. Using~\eqref{e.ch_perturbation_lipschitz_summability} to sum over $\mathsf h$, we find that replacing $\eta_{N+M}H^x_{N+M}(\rho,\alpha)$ by $\eta_NH^x_N(\widetilde\sigma,\alpha)$ changes the variance by $O(N|\eta_{N+M}-\eta_N|+\eta_N^2)$, and the cross-covariance with $\widetilde V_N^{x,y,q}$ by $O(\eta_N(N|\eta_{N+M}-\eta_N|+\eta_N^2))$. Both quantities vanish as $N\to\infty$, by~\eqref{e.eta_N_def}. The means are zero.

Collecting the four steps, the means of the two sides of~\eqref{e.chart_H_decomposition} differ by $O_L(N^{-1})$ and their covariances by $o(1)$, uniformly over the stated range. This is~\eqref{e.chart_H_decomposition}.
<!-- end proof-17 -->
<!-- lemma-13: body_md -->
\label{l.radial_first_order_expansion}
Fix $L\geqslant1$. We have
\begin{align}
    \widetilde H_N^{x,q}(r_N(\tau);\sigma,\alpha)+\widetilde V_N^{x,y,q}(\sigma,\alpha)\stackrel{N^{-1},N^{-1}}{\mathrel{\hstretch{1.8}{\approx}}}\widetilde H_N^{x,y,q}(\sigma,\alpha)+\frac12\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}\left(M_s-|\tau^{(s)}|^2\right)\widetilde{\mathcal E}_{N,s}^{x,q}(\sigma,\alpha)
    \label{e.radial_first_order}
\end{align}
uniformly over $x,y,q$ and $(\sigma,\tau,\alpha)\in\Sigma_N\times\{|\tau|\leqslant L+1\}\times\mathfrak U$. The relation remains valid, with the same rates, if a Gaussian field independent of $\widetilde H_N$, $W^q_N$, and $H^x_N$ is added to both sides.
<!-- end lemma-13 -->
<!-- proof-18: body_md -->
Set $\delta_s(\tau):=r_N^s(\tau)-1=(M_s-|\tau^{(s)}|^2)/N_s$, so that $|\delta_s(\tau)|\leqslant C_LN^{-1}$ by~\eqref{e.r_N_close_to_one}. Taylor's formula in the radial variable gives
\begin{align*}
    \widetilde H_N^{x,q}(r_N(\tau);\sigma,\alpha)={}&\widetilde H_N^{x,q}(\sigma,\alpha)+\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}\delta_s(\tau)\,\partial_{r^s}\widetilde H^{x,q}_N(r;\sigma,\alpha)\big|_{r=\vec{\mathbf{1}}}+\boldsymbol{\varepsilon}_N(\sigma,\tau,\alpha),\\
    \boldsymbol{\varepsilon}_N(\sigma,\tau,\alpha):={}&\sum_{s,u\in\mathscr{S}}\delta_s(\tau)\delta_u(\tau)\int_0^1(1-\mathsf v)\,\partial_{r^s}\partial_{r^u}\widetilde H_N^{x,q}(\vec{\mathbf{1}}+\mathsf v\delta(\tau);\sigma,\alpha)\,\mathrm{d}\mathsf v.
\end{align*}
By the definition~\eqref{e.radial_generic_perturbation} of $\widetilde{\mathcal E}^{x,q}_{N,s}$, the first-order term is $\frac12\sum_s(M_s-|\tau^{(s)}|^2)\widetilde{\mathcal E}^{x,q}_{N,s}(\sigma,\alpha)$. By~\eqref{e.second_radial_bound} and the bound on $\delta(\tau)$, the remainder satisfies $\boldsymbol{\varepsilon}_N\stackrel{N^{-1},N^{-3}}{\mathrel{\hstretch{1.8}{\approx}}}0$. The field on the right-hand side of~\eqref{e.radial_first_order} has variance at most $CN$, by~\eqref{e.radial_energy_covariance_bound} and the covariance formula of $\widetilde H^{x,q}_N$; the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality therefore bounds its covariance with $\boldsymbol{\varepsilon}_N$ by $C_LN^{-1}$. This proves~\eqref{e.radial_first_order}. A field independent of $\widetilde H_N$, $W^q_N$, and $H^x_N$ is independent of $\boldsymbol{\varepsilon}_N$, which gives the last assertion.
<!-- end proof-18 -->
<!-- lemma-14: body_md -->
\label{l.symmetric_block_radial_covariance}
Fix $L\geqslant1$, and write $\rho:=(S_{r_N(\tau)}\sigma,\tau)$. Under the couplings above, we have
\begin{align}
    H_{N+M}^{x,y,q}(\rho,\alpha)=H_{N+M}^{x,q}(\rho,\alpha)+V_{N+M}^{x,y,q}(\rho,\alpha)
    &\mathrel{\hstretch{1.8}{\approx}} H_{N+M}^{x,q}(\rho,\alpha)+\widetilde V_N^{x,y,q}(\sigma,\alpha)
    \label{e.replace_V_NM}
\end{align}
uniformly over $x,y,q$ and $(\sigma,\tau,\alpha)\in\Sigma_N\times\{|\tau|\leqslant L+1\}\times\mathfrak U$, and
\begin{equation}
    H_N^{x,y,q}(\sigma,\alpha)=H_N^{x,q}(\sigma,\alpha)+V_N^{x,y,q}(\sigma,\alpha)\mathrel{\hstretch{1.8}{\approx}} H_N^{x,q}(\sigma,\alpha)+\widetilde V_N^{x,y,q}(\sigma,\alpha)
    \label{e.replace_V_N}
\end{equation}
uniformly over $x,y,q$ and $(\sigma,\alpha)\in\Sigma_N\times\mathfrak U$.
<!-- end lemma-14 -->
<!-- proof-19: body_md -->
We first replace $\eta_{N+M}$ by $\eta_N$ in $V^{x,y,q}_{N+M}$. By~\eqref{e.full_radial_energy_covariance_bound} at size $N+M$, the field $V^{x,y,q}_{N+M}/\eta_{N+M}$ has mean and covariance of order $N$, and its covariance with $H^{x,q}_{N+M}$ is of order $N$ as well. Multiplying it by $\eta_N$ instead of $\eta_{N+M}$ therefore changes the mean, the variance, and the covariance with $H^{x,q}_{N+M}$ of the left-hand side of~\eqref{e.replace_V_NM} by at most $CN|\eta_{N+M}-\eta_N|$, which vanishes by~\eqref{e.eta_N_def}.

Both sides of~\eqref{e.replace_V_NM} and~\eqref{e.replace_V_N} are now of the form $\mathsf H+2\eta_N\sum_sy^s\mathsf D_s$, where $\mathsf H$ is a Hamiltonian and $\mathsf D_s$ is a radial derivative. It therefore suffices to show that, in each of the two comparisons, the means of the two radial derivatives, their covariances with the Hamiltonian $\mathsf H$ and with the corresponding Hamiltonian evaluated at another point, and their mutual covariances, differ by $O_L(1)$; multiplication by $2\eta_N$ (once for the cross terms, twice for the covariances of the radial derivatives) then gives errors of order $\eta_N$ and $\eta_N^2$.

Consider~\eqref{e.replace_V_NM}. The means of the radial derivatives are obtained by differentiating the deterministic terms in~\eqref{e.enriched_H}, at sizes $N+M$ and $N$, as in~\eqref{e.mean_perturbed_H}. For species $s$, the derivative $2\partial_{r^s}$ of the interaction correction is $-2(N+M)t\lambda_s\partial_s\xi(\lambda)$ for the $(N+M)$-spin system and $-2Nt\lambda_s\partial_s\widetilde\xi_N(\lambda)=-2Nt\lambda_s\partial_s\xi(\frac{N}{N+M}\lambda)$ for the bulk system; these differ by $O(1)$. The derivatives of the cascade corrections are $-2q^s(1)(N_s+M_s)$ and $-2q^s(1)N_s$; and the derivatives of the external-field terms are $h^s\sum_{i\in I_{N+M,s}}\rho_i$ and $h^s\sum_{i\in I_{N,s}}\sigma_i$, whose difference is $h^s((\sqrt{r^s_N(\tau)}-1)\sum_{i\in I_{N,s}}\sigma_i+\sum_{j\in\mathsf M_s}\tau_j)=O_L(1)$, as in the proof of Lemma~\ref{l.fixed_block_increment_bound}. The covariances are obtained by differentiating covariance kernels. For instance, by~\eqref{e.def_H_N} and~\eqref{e.overlap_dilation}, and with $\rho'=(S_{r_N(\tau')}\sigma',\tau')$,
\begin{equation*}
    \operatorname{Cov}\left(2\partial_{r^s}H_{N+M}(S_r\rho)\big|_{r=\vec{\mathbf{1}}},H_{N+M}(\rho')\right)=(N+M)R_{N+M,s}(\rho,\rho')\,\partial_s\xi\left(R_{N+M}(\rho,\rho')\right),
\end{equation*}
while, by~\eqref{e.interaction_decomposition}, \eqref{e.tH=}, and the independence of $\widetilde{\mathsf Z}_{N,j}$ and $\widetilde D_N$ from $\widetilde H_N$,
\begin{equation*}
    \operatorname{Cov}\left(2\partial_{r^s}\widetilde H_{N}(S_r\sigma)\big|_{r=\vec{\mathbf{1}}},H_{N+M}(\rho')\right)=N\sqrt{r^s_N(\tau')}R_{N,s}(\sigma,\sigma')\,\partial_s\xi\left(\tfrac{N}{N+M}R_N(\sigma,S_{r_N(\tau')}\sigma')\right).
\end{equation*}
By~\eqref{e.full_and_bulk_overlap_bound} and~\eqref{e.r_N_close_to_one}, the overlaps and radii appearing in these two expressions differ by $O_L(N^{-1})$, and the prefactors differ by $M$; since $\xi$ is smooth, the two expressions differ by $O_L(1)$. The same argument applies to the covariance of the radial derivatives with $H_{N+M}(\rho)$ itself, to the cascade field through~\eqref{e.cascade_decomposition} and~\eqref{e.WNq_covariance}, to the perturbation field through~\eqref{e.overlap_perturbation_cross_covariance} and~\eqref{e.ch_perturbation_lipschitz_summability}, in which case the kernels $\mathsf C_{\mathsf h}$ are differentiated at most twice and the bound is $O_L(\Lambda_{\mathsf h})$ before summation, and to the covariances between two radial derivatives, which involve one more derivative of the kernels. This proves~\eqref{e.replace_V_NM}.

For~\eqref{e.replace_V_N}, the cascade, external-field, and perturbation parts of $V_N^{x,y,q}$ and $\widetilde V_N^{x,y,q}$ coincide, and the only difference lies in the interaction part, where $H_N$ is replaced by $\widetilde H_N$ and $\xi$ by $\widetilde\xi_N$. Under the coupling~\eqref{e.coupling_H_tildeH}, we have $\operatorname{Cov}(\partial_{r^s}\widetilde H_N(S_r\sigma),H_N(\sigma'))=\operatorname{Cov}(\partial_{r^s}\widetilde H_N(S_r\sigma),\widetilde H_N(\sigma'))$, and the kernels $\xi$ and $\widetilde\xi_N$, together with their derivatives of order at most three, differ by $O(N^{-1})$ uniformly on the overlap domain $[-1,1]^\mathscr{S}$. The differences of means and covariances are therefore $O(1)$ again, and the conclusion follows as above.
<!-- end proof-19 -->
<!-- proposition-6: body_md -->
\label{p.radial_insertion_harmless}
Let $L\geqslant1$. Uniformly over $x,y,q$, we have
\begin{gather}
    \mathbb{E}\log Z^{x,y,q}_{N+M,L}-\mathbb{E}\log Z_N^{x,y,q}\mathrel{\hstretch{1.8}{\approx}} A^{\mathrm{rad}}_{N,L}(x,y,q),\label{e.radial_insertion_cutoff_increment_negligible}
    \\
    \mathbb{E}\left\langle f\right\rangle_{N+M,L}^{x,y,q}
    \mathrel{\hstretch{1.8}{\approx}}\mathbb{E}\left\langle f\right\rangle^{x,y,q,\mathrm{ch}}_{N+M,L,\widetilde V},
    \label{e.radial_insertion_observable_negligible}
\end{gather}
for every bounded measurable function $f$ of finitely many replicas of $(\tau,\alpha)$. Consequently, the increment with cutoff is asymptotically a lower bound for the true increment:
\begin{equation}
    \lim_{N\to\infty}\sup_{x,y,q}
    \left(A_{N,L}^{\mathrm{rad}}(x,y,q)-A_N(x,y,q)\right)_+=0.
    \label{e.one_sided_increment}
\end{equation}
<!-- end proposition-6 -->
<!-- proof-20: body_md -->
We apply Lemma~\ref{l.gaussian_comparison_covariance_norm} on the space $\Sigma_N\times\{|\tau|\leqslant L+1\}\times\mathfrak U$, with the finite measure $\chi_L(\tau)p_N^{\mathrm{ch}}(\tau)\mathrm{d}\tau\,P_N(\mathrm{d}\sigma)\mathfrak{R}(\mathrm{d}\alpha)$ normalized to a probability measure (the normalization cancels in the differences of logarithms and does not affect the brackets), to the two fields in~\eqref{e.replace_V_NM}. The partition functions are $Z^{x,y,q}_{N+M,L}$ and $Z^{x,y,q,\mathrm{ch}}_{N+M,L,\widetilde V}$, by~\eqref{e.truncated_true_partition} and~\eqref{e.radially_inserted_full_partition_L}, so that $\mathbb{E}\log Z^{x,y,q}_{N+M,L}\mathrel{\hstretch{1.8}{\approx}}\mathbb{E}\log Z^{x,y,q,\mathrm{ch}}_{N+M,L,\widetilde V}$ and~\eqref{e.radial_insertion_observable_negligible} holds. Applying the same lemma on $\Sigma_N\times\mathfrak U$ to the two fields in~\eqref{e.replace_V_N} gives $\mathbb{E}\log Z^{x,y,q}_N\mathrel{\hstretch{1.8}{\approx}}\mathbb{E}\log Z^{x,y,q}_{N,\widetilde V}$. Combining the two estimates on partition functions proves~\eqref{e.radial_insertion_cutoff_increment_negligible}. Finally, by~\eqref{e.full_partition_dominates_cutoff}, we have $A_N(x,y,q)\geqslant\mathbb{E}\log Z^{x,y,q}_{N+M,L}-\mathbb{E}\log Z^{x,y,q}_N$, so that $(A^{\mathrm{rad}}_{N,L}-A_N)_+$ is bounded by the absolute value of the difference between the two sides of~\eqref{e.radial_insertion_cutoff_increment_negligible}, which tends to zero uniformly over $x,y,q$. This proves~\eqref{e.one_sided_increment}.
<!-- end proof-20 -->
<!-- lemma-15: body_md -->
\label{l.bulk_true_comparison}
There exists a constant $C<\infty$ such that, for every sufficiently large $N$,
\begin{equation}
    \varepsilon_N(Q):=\sup_{x,y,q}\left|\widetilde F_N^{x,y}(t,q)-\overline F_{N+M}^{x,y}(t,q)\right|\leqslant\frac{C}{N}.
    \label{e.bulk_true_comparison}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-15 -->
<!-- proof-21: body_md -->
We first compare the bulk system with the $N$-spin system. Under the coupling~\eqref{e.coupling_H_tildeH}, the fields $H_N^{x,q}+\widetilde V_N^{x,y,q}$ and $\widetilde H_N^{x,q}+\widetilde V^{x,y,q}_N$ differ by $\sqrt{2tM}\,\widetilde Y_N(\sigma)$, whose covariance $2tM\theta_N(R_N(\sigma,\sigma'))$ is bounded by~\eqref{e.cavity_reaction_kernel_limit}, and by the deterministic term $-Nt(\xi(\lambda)-\widetilde\xi_N(\lambda))=-tM\theta_N(\lambda)$, which is bounded as well. Lemma~\ref{l.gaussian_comparison_covariance_norm} therefore gives
\begin{equation*}
    \sup_{x,y,q}\left|\mathbb{E}\log Z_N^{\mathord{\sim},x,y,q}-\mathbb{E}\log Z_{N,\widetilde V}^{x,y,q}\right|\leqslant C.
\end{equation*}
By~\eqref{e.replace_V_N} and Lemma~\ref{l.gaussian_comparison_covariance_norm}, we also have $\sup_{x,y,q}|\mathbb{E}\log Z_{N,\widetilde V}^{x,y,q}-\mathbb{E}\log Z_N^{x,y,q}|\leqslant C$ for all sufficiently large $N$. Dividing by $N$ and recalling~\eqref{e.ZNx_def} and~\eqref{e.ZcircMN_def}, we obtain $\sup_{x,y,q}|\widetilde F_N^{x,y}(t,q)-\overline F_N^{x,y}(t,q)|\leqslant C/N$. Next, by~\eqref{e.ASS_increment_def},
\begin{equation*}
    \widetilde F_N^{x,y}(t,q)-\frac{N+M}{N}\overline F_{N+M}^{x,y}(t,q)=\widetilde F_N^{x,y}(t,q)-\overline F_N^{x,y}(t,q)+\frac1N A_N(x,y,q),
\end{equation*}
so that Lemma~\ref{l.fixed_block_increment_bound} gives $\sup_{x,y,q}|\widetilde F_N^{x,y}(t,q)-\frac{N+M}{N}\overline F_{N+M}^{x,y}(t,q)|\leqslant C/N$. It remains to observe that $\overline F^{x,y}_{N+M}(t,q)$ is bounded uniformly over $x,y,q$ and $N$, so that replacing $\frac{N+M}N\overline F^{x,y}_{N+M}$ by $\overline F^{x,y}_{N+M}$ costs at most $CM/N$. Indeed, Jensen's inequality and the self-overlap correction in~\eqref{e.enriched_H} give
\begin{equation*}
    -t\xi(\lambda)\leqslant\frac1N\mathbb{E}\log Z_N(t,0)\leqslant\frac1N\log\int\exp\left(\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}h^s\sum_{i\in I_{N,s}}\sigma_i\right)P_N(\mathrm{d}\sigma)\leqslant\max_{s\in\mathscr{S}}|h^s|,
\end{equation*}
the Lipschitz estimate~\eqref{e.F_N_Lipschitz} extends this bound to $\overline F_N(t,q)$ for $q$ in the bounded set $Q$, and~\eqref{e.full_radial_free_energy_cost}--\eqref{e.GG_free_energy_cost} extend it to $\overline F_N^{x,y}(t,q)$.
<!-- end proof-21 -->
<!-- lemma-16: body_md -->
\label{l.integrated_convex_derivative_random}
Let $0<\delta<1/2$. Let $\mathcal F$ be a random differentiable convex function on $[0,3]$, and set $f(u):=\mathbb{E}\mathcal F(u)$. Assume that $f$ is finite and differentiable on $[0,3]$ and that, for some $K<\infty$,
\begin{equation}
    \sup_{u\in[0,3]}|f'(u)|\leqslant K.
    \label{e.random_convex_derivative_l1_hypothesis}
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
    \int_1^2\mathbb{E}\left|\mathcal F'(u)-f'(u)\right|\,\mathrm{d} u\leqslant\frac3\delta\int_0^3\mathbb{E}\left|\mathcal F(u)-f(u)\right|\,\mathrm{d} u+2K\delta.
    \label{e.random_integrated_convex_derivative_bound}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-16 -->
<!-- proof-22: body_md -->
Set $A(u):=\mathcal F(u)-f(u)$. For every differentiable convex function $g:[0,3]\to\mathbb{R}$ and every $u\in[1,2]$, we have
\begin{equation*}
    \frac{g(u)-g(u-\delta)}{\delta}\leqslant g'(u)\leqslant\frac{g(u+\delta)-g(u)}{\delta}.
\end{equation*}
Using the upper difference quotient for $\mathcal F$ and the lower one for $f$, and then the other way around, we obtain
\begin{align*}
    \mathcal F'(u)-f'(u)
    &\leqslant\frac{f(u+\delta)-2f(u)+f(u-\delta)+A(u+\delta)-A(u)}{\delta},\\
    \mathcal F'(u)-f'(u)
    &\geqslant\frac{-f(u+\delta)+2f(u)-f(u-\delta)+A(u)-A(u-\delta)}{\delta}.
\end{align*}
Since $f$ is convex, $f(u+\delta)-2f(u)+f(u-\delta)\geqslant0$, and therefore
\begin{align*}
    \left|\mathcal F'(u)-f'(u)\right|
    \leqslant\frac{f(u+\delta)-2f(u)+f(u-\delta)}{\delta}
    +\frac{|A(u-\delta)|+|A(u)|+|A(u+\delta)|}{\delta}.
\end{align*}
We integrate over $u\in[1,2]$ and take expectations. The contribution of the second term is at most $\frac3\delta\int_0^3\mathbb{E}|A(u)|\mathrm{d} u$. For the first term, we write
\begin{align*}
    \int_1^2\left(f(u+\delta)-2f(u)+f(u-\delta)\right)\mathrm{d} u=\int_0^\delta\left(\int_{2-\delta+v}^{2+v}f'(w)\,\mathrm{d} w-\int_{1-\delta+v}^{1+v}f'(w)\,\mathrm{d} w\right)\mathrm{d} v
    \leqslant2K\delta^2,
\end{align*}
by the fundamental theorem of calculus and~\eqref{e.random_convex_derivative_l1_hypothesis}. This proves~\eqref{e.random_integrated_convex_derivative_bound}.
<!-- end proof-22 -->
<!-- lemma-17: body_md -->
\label{l.fixed_tilt_uniform_bounds}
Fix $L\geqslant1$. There exists $C_L<\infty$ such that, for every $N$, $x$, $y\in[0,3]^{\mathscr{S}}$, $q$, $\mathsf{t}\in[0,1]$, and $s\in\mathscr{S}$,
\begin{equation}
    \mathbb{E}\left\langle|\widetilde{\mathcal E}_{N,s}^{x,q}|^4\right\rangle_N^{\mathord{\sim},x,y,q}
    +\mathbb{E}\left\langle|\widetilde{\mathcal E}_{N,s}^{x,q}|^4\right\rangle_{N,\mathsf{t},L}
    +\mathbb{E}\left\langle R_\mathsf{t}^2\right\rangle^{\otimes}_{N,L}\leqslant C_L.
    \label{e.cavity_tilt_moment_bounds}
\end{equation}
In particular, $\sup_N\sup_{x,y,q}\max_{s\in\mathscr{S}}|e_N^s|<\infty$ and $\sup_N\sup_{x,y,q}\operatorname{Rad}_{N,L}(x,y,q)\leqslant C_L$.
<!-- end lemma-17 -->
<!-- proof-23: body_md -->
We first prove a general estimate. Let $\mu$ be a finite measure on a space $\mathbb X$, let $\mathsf G$ be a centered Gaussian field on $\mathbb X$ and $m$ a bounded function, and let $\left\langle\cdot\right\rangle$ be the Gibbs bracket associated with the measure $e^{\mathsf G(\mathsf z)+m(\mathsf z)}\mu(\mathrm{d}\mathsf z)$. Let $X$ be a Gaussian field on $\mathbb X$, jointly Gaussian with $\mathsf G$, and let $A<\infty$ be such that
\begin{equation*}
    \sup_{\mathsf z\in\mathbb X}\left(|\mathbb{E} X(\mathsf z)|+\operatorname{Var}X(\mathsf z)\right)\leqslant A
    \qquad\text{and}\qquad
    \sup_{\mathsf z,\mathsf z'\in\mathbb X}\left|\operatorname{Cov}\left(X(\mathsf z),\mathsf G(\mathsf z')\right)\right|\leqslant A.
\end{equation*}
We claim that, for every $\lambda\in\mathbb{R}$,
\begin{equation}
    \mathbb{E}\left\langle e^{\lambda X}\right\rangle\leqslant\exp\left(3A|\lambda|+A\lambda^2/2\right).
    \label{e.tilted_exponential_moment}
\end{equation}
To see this, fix $\mathsf z\in\mathbb X$, write $X(\mathsf z)=\mathbb{E} X(\mathsf z)+X^\circ(\mathsf z)$, and set $C_{\mathsf z}(\mathsf z'):=\operatorname{Cov}(X(\mathsf z),\mathsf G(\mathsf z'))$. The Cameron--Martin formula gives, for every nonnegative measurable functional $\Phi$ of the field $\mathsf G$,
\begin{equation*}
    \mathbb{E}\left[e^{\lambda X^\circ(\mathsf z)}\Phi(\mathsf G)\right]
    =e^{\lambda^2\operatorname{Var}(X(\mathsf z))/2}\,\mathbb{E}\left[\Phi(\mathsf G+\lambda C_{\mathsf z})\right].
\end{equation*}
We apply this identity to the normalized Gibbs density at $\mathsf z$, namely $\Phi(\mathsf G):=e^{\mathsf G(\mathsf z)+m(\mathsf z)}/\int e^{\mathsf G+m}\mathrm{d}\mu$. Since $|C_{\mathsf z}|\leqslant A$, replacing $\mathsf G$ by $\mathsf G+\lambda C_{\mathsf z}$ multiplies the numerator and the denominator of $\Phi$ by factors in $[e^{-A|\lambda|},e^{A|\lambda|}]$, so that $\Phi(\mathsf G+\lambda C_{\mathsf z})\leqslant e^{2A|\lambda|}\Phi(\mathsf G)$. Hence
\begin{equation*}
    \mathbb{E}\left\langle e^{\lambda X}\right\rangle=\int_{\mathbb X}\mathbb{E}\left[e^{\lambda X(\mathsf z)}\Phi(\mathsf G)\right]\mu(\mathrm{d}\mathsf z)\leqslant e^{A|\lambda|+A\lambda^2/2+2A|\lambda|}\int_{\mathbb X}\mathbb{E}\left[\Phi(\mathsf G)\right]\mu(\mathrm{d}\mathsf z),
\end{equation*}
and the last integral equals $1$. This proves~\eqref{e.tilted_exponential_moment}. Since $|u|^4\leqslant24(e^u+e^{-u})$ and $|u|^8\leqslant8!\,(e^u+e^{-u})$, we deduce that
\begin{equation}
    \mathbb{E}\left\langle|X|^4\right\rangle\leqslant48\exp(3A+A/2)
    \qquad\text{and}\qquad
    \mathbb{E}\left\langle|X|^8\right\rangle\leqslant2\cdot8!\exp(3A+A/2).
    \label{e.tilted_polynomial_moments}
\end{equation}

We apply this estimate first to the bulk bracket $\left\langle\cdot\right\rangle_N^{\mathord{\sim},x,y,q}$, with $\mathbb X:=\Sigma_N\times\mathfrak U$, $\mu:=P_N\otimes\mathfrak{R}$, and $\mathsf G$ the centered part of $\widetilde H_N^{x,y,q}$, and with $X:=\widetilde{\mathcal E}^{x,q}_{N,s}$. The mean and the variance of $X$ are bounded by~\eqref{e.radial_energy_covariance_bound}. For the cross-covariances, we note that the covariance of $\widetilde{\mathcal E}^{x,q}_{N,s}(\sigma,\alpha)$ with $\widetilde H_N^{x,q}(\sigma',\alpha')$ is $2/N_s$ times a first radial derivative of a covariance kernel of order $N$, hence is bounded by~\eqref{e.second_radial_bound}, and that its covariance with $\widetilde V_N^{x,y,q}(\sigma',\alpha')=\eta_N\sum_uy^uN_u\widetilde{\mathcal E}^{x,q}_{N,u}(\sigma',\alpha')$ is $O(\eta_N)$ by~\eqref{e.radial_energy_covariance_bound}. The hypotheses therefore hold with a constant $A=C$ independent of $L$, and~\eqref{e.tilted_polynomial_moments} gives the bound on the first term in~\eqref{e.cavity_tilt_moment_bounds}, together with
\begin{equation}
    \mathbb{E}\left\langle|\widetilde{\mathcal E}_{N,s}^{x,q}|^8\right\rangle_N^{\mathord{\sim},x,y,q}\leqslant C.
    \label{e.bulk_eighth_moment}
\end{equation}
Since $e^s_N=\mathbb{E}\left\langle\widetilde{\mathcal E}^{x,q}_{N,s}\right\rangle_N^{\mathord{\sim},x,y,q}$ by~\eqref{e.e^N_s=}, Jensen's inequality gives $|e^s_N|\leqslant C$, which is the first assertion after~\eqref{e.cavity_tilt_moment_bounds}.

We next apply the estimate to the product bracket $\left\langle\cdot\right\rangle^{\otimes}_{N,L}$, with
\begin{equation*}
    \mathbb X:=\Sigma_N\times\{|\tau|\leqslant L+1\}\times\mathfrak U,
    \qquad
    \mu:=\chi_L(\tau)\,\boldsymbol{\gamma}_M(\mathrm{d}\tau)\,P_N(\mathrm{d}\sigma)\,\mathfrak{R}(\mathrm{d}\alpha),
\end{equation*}
the same field $\mathsf G$, and $X:=W_\mathsf{t}$. By~\eqref{e.cavity_tilt_W}, on the set $\mathbb X$, the field $W_\mathsf{t}$ is a linear combination of $(\widetilde{\mathcal E}^{x,q}_{N,u})_{u\in\mathscr{S}}$ and $(\mathsf X^q_{N,j})_{j\in[M]}$ with coefficients bounded by $C_L$, plus a deterministic term bounded by $C_L$; here we use $|\tau|\leqslant L+1$, the bound $|e^s_N|\leqslant C$ just proved, and the boundedness of the coefficients $\vartheta^s$ in~\eqref{e.prelimit_vartheta_def} for $q$ in the bounded set $Q$ of~\eqref{e.xyqbR_uniform}. By~\eqref{e.cavity_field_def}, the fields $\mathsf X^q_{N,j}$ have mean $h^s$ and variance bounded by $C$, and they are independent of $\widetilde H_N^{x,y,q}$ and of $(\widetilde{\mathcal E}^{x,q}_{N,u})_u$. Together with the bounds of the previous paragraph, this shows that the hypotheses hold with $A=C_L$, so that~\eqref{e.tilted_exponential_moment} gives
\begin{equation}
    \mathbb{E}\left\langle e^{\lambda W_\mathsf{t}}\right\rangle^{\otimes}_{N,L}\leqslant C_L\qquad\text{for every }\lambda\in[-4,4].
    \label{e.W_exponential_moments}
\end{equation}
We now bound the second moment of the density~\eqref{e.cavity_tilt_density}. By the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality, $1=(\left\langle e^{W_\mathsf{t}/2}e^{-W_\mathsf{t}/2}\right\rangle^{\otimes}_{N,L})^2\leqslant\left\langle e^{W_\mathsf{t}}\right\rangle^{\otimes}_{N,L}\left\langle e^{-W_\mathsf{t}}\right\rangle^{\otimes}_{N,L}$, and by Jensen's inequality, $(\left\langle e^{-W_\mathsf{t}}\right\rangle^{\otimes}_{N,L})^2\leqslant\left\langle e^{-2W_\mathsf{t}}\right\rangle^{\otimes}_{N,L}$. Hence
\begin{align*}
    \mathbb{E}\left\langle R_\mathsf{t}^2\right\rangle^{\otimes}_{N,L}
    =\mathbb{E}\Bigg[\frac{\left\langle e^{2W_\mathsf{t}}\right\rangle^{\otimes}_{N,L}}{\big(\left\langle e^{W_\mathsf{t}}\right\rangle^{\otimes}_{N,L}\big)^2}\Bigg]
    &\leqslant\mathbb{E}\left[\left\langle e^{2W_\mathsf{t}}\right\rangle^{\otimes}_{N,L}\,\left\langle e^{-2W_\mathsf{t}}\right\rangle^{\otimes}_{N,L}\right]\\
    &\leqslant\left(\mathbb{E}\left\langle e^{4W_\mathsf{t}}\right\rangle^{\otimes}_{N,L}\right)^{1/2}\left(\mathbb{E}\left\langle e^{-4W_\mathsf{t}}\right\rangle^{\otimes}_{N,L}\right)^{1/2}\leqslant C_L,
\end{align*}
where we used the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality for $\mathbb{E}$, Jensen's inequality for the brackets, and the bound~\eqref{e.W_exponential_moments}. This is the bound on the third term in~\eqref{e.cavity_tilt_moment_bounds}.

For the second term, since $\widetilde{\mathcal E}^{x,q}_{N,s}$ does not depend on $\tau$, the change of density~\eqref{e.cavity_tilt_change_of_density}, the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality, and~\eqref{e.bulk_eighth_moment} give
\begin{equation*}
    \mathbb{E}\left\langle|\widetilde{\mathcal E}_{N,s}^{x,q}|^4\right\rangle_{N,\mathsf{t},L}
    =\mathbb{E}\left\langle|\widetilde{\mathcal E}_{N,s}^{x,q}|^4R_\mathsf{t}\right\rangle^{\otimes}_{N,L}
    \leqslant\left(\mathbb{E}\left\langle|\widetilde{\mathcal E}_{N,s}^{x,q}|^8\right\rangle_N^{\mathord{\sim},x,y,q}\right)^{1/2}\left(\mathbb{E}\left\langle R_\mathsf{t}^2\right\rangle^{\otimes}_{N,L}\right)^{1/2}\leqslant C_L.
\end{equation*}
Finally, by Jensen's inequality and $|e_N^s|\leqslant C$, we have $\mathbb{E}\left\langle|\widetilde{\mathcal E}^{x,q}_{N,s}-e^s_N|\right\rangle_{N,\mathsf{t},L}\leqslant C_L$, and the bound on $\operatorname{Rad}_{N,L}$ follows from its definition~\eqref{e.radial_error_def}.
<!-- end proof-23 -->
<!-- lemma-18: body_md -->
\label{l.radial_self_average}
For every $L\geqslant1$, we have
\begin{equation*}
    \lim_{N\to\infty}\sup_{x,q}\int_{[1,2]^{\mathscr{S}}}\operatorname{Rad}_{N,L}(x,y,q)\,\mathrm{d} y=0.
\end{equation*}
<!-- end lemma-18 -->
<!-- proof-24: body_md -->
Fix $L\geqslant1$, $N$, $x$, and $q$, and write $E_s:=\widetilde{\mathcal E}_{N,s}^{x,q}$ and $\left\langle\cdot\right\rangle_0:=\left\langle\cdot\right\rangle_N^{\mathord{\sim},x,y,q}$ for brevity. The constants $C$ below may depend on $L$ but not on $N,x,y,q,\mathsf{t}$. Recall from~\eqref{e.e^N_s=} that $e_N^s=\mathbb{E}\left\langle E_s\right\rangle_0$ depends on $y$. The proof has two steps: we first show that $E_s$ concentrates around $e^s_N$ under the bulk measure for most values of $y$, and we then transfer this concentration to the interpolating measures through the density $R_\mathsf{t}$.

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{Step 1: Concentration under the bulk measure.}\par
Define
\begin{equation*}
    \mathcal F(y):=\frac1N\log Z_N^{\mathord{\sim},x,y,q},
    \qquad
    f(y):=\mathbb{E}\mathcal F(y),
\end{equation*}
where $Z_N^{\mathord{\sim},x,y,q}$ is the bulk partition function in~\eqref{e.ZcircMN_def}. By~\eqref{e.radial_generic_perturbation}, the dependence of $\widetilde H_N^{x,y,q}$ on $y$ is through the affine term $\eta_N\sum_sy^sN_sE_s$. Hence, using $N_s=\lambda_sN$,
\begin{gather*}
    \partial_{y^s}\mathcal F(y)=\eta_N\lambda_s\left\langle E_s\right\rangle_0,\qquad 
    \partial_{y^s}f(y)=\eta_N\lambda_s\mathbb{E}\left\langle E_s\right\rangle_0=\eta_N\lambda_se^s_N,\\
    \partial_{y^s}^2f(y)=\eta_N^2\lambda_s^2N\,\mathbb{E}\left\langle\left(E_s-\left\langle E_s\right\rangle_0\right)^2\right\rangle_0.
\end{gather*}
In particular, $\mathcal F$ and $f$ are convex in each coordinate of $y$. Since $|e^s_N|\leqslant C$ by Lemma~\ref{l.fixed_tilt_uniform_bounds}, we have $\sup_{y\in[0,3]^{\mathscr{S}}}|\partial_{y^s}f(y)|\leqslant C\eta_N$. Moreover, the Hamiltonian $\widetilde H_N^{x,y,q}$ is of the form~\eqref{e.linear_cascade_hamiltonian}, see Remark~\ref{r.linear_form_hamiltonians}, and its variance is at most $CN$ uniformly over $x,y,q$, by~\eqref{e.covariance_perturbed_H} and~\eqref{e.radial_energy_covariance_bound}. Lemma~\ref{l.cascade_concentration}, which controls the fluctuations coming from the Gaussian fields and from the cascade, gives
\begin{equation*}
    \sup_{y\in[0,3]^{\mathscr{S}}}\mathbb{E}\left|\mathcal F(y)-f(y)\right|\leqslant CN^{-1/2}.
\end{equation*}
Set $\delta_N:=(N^{-1/2}/\eta_N)^{1/2}$, which is smaller than $1/2$ for all sufficiently large $N$ and tends to zero, by~\eqref{e.eta_N_def}. Fix $s\in\mathscr{S}$ and the coordinates $y^u$, $u\ne s$. Applying Lemma~\ref{l.integrated_convex_derivative_random} to $\mathcal F$ and $f$ as functions of $u=y^s$, with $K=C\eta_N$ and $\delta=\delta_N$, gives
\begin{align*}
    \eta_N\lambda_s\int_1^2\mathbb{E}\left|\left\langle E_s\right\rangle_0-e^s_N\right|\,\mathrm{d} y^s
    &\leqslant\frac{3}{\delta_N}\int_0^3\mathbb{E}|\mathcal F-f|\,\mathrm{d} y^s+2C\eta_N\delta_N\\
    &\leqslant C\left(\frac{N^{-1/2}}{\delta_N}+\eta_N\delta_N\right)=2C\eta_N\left(\frac{N^{-1/2}}{\eta_N}\right)^{1/2}.
\end{align*}
Dividing by $\eta_N\lambda_s$, we obtain
\begin{equation*}
    \int_1^2\mathbb{E}\left|\left\langle E_s\right\rangle_0-e^s_N\right|\,\mathrm{d} y^s\leqslant C\left(\frac{N^{-1/2}}{\eta_N}\right)^{1/2}.
\end{equation*}
Next, integrating the formula for $\partial^2_{y^s}f$ over $y^s\in[1,2]$ and using the bound on $\partial_{y^s}f$ gives
\begin{equation*}
    \int_1^2\mathbb{E}\left\langle\left(E_s-\left\langle E_s\right\rangle_0\right)^2\right\rangle_0\,\mathrm{d} y^s\leqslant\frac{2C\eta_N}{\eta_N^2\lambda_s^2N}=\frac{C}{N\eta_N}.
\end{equation*}
Combining the last two displays with the triangle inequality and the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality, in the form
\begin{equation*}
    \mathbb{E}\left\langle|E_s-e^s_N|\right\rangle_0\leqslant\left(\mathbb{E}\left\langle(E_s-\left\langle E_s\right\rangle_0)^2\right\rangle_0\right)^{1/2}+\mathbb{E}\left|\left\langle E_s\right\rangle_0-e^s_N\right|,
\end{equation*}
and using Jensen's inequality for the concave function $u\mapsto u^{1/2}$ after an integration over $y^s\in[1,2]$, we get
\begin{equation*}
    \int_1^2\mathbb{E}\left\langle\left|E_s-e^s_N\right|\right\rangle_0\,\mathrm{d} y^s\leqslant\varepsilon_N:=C\left((N\eta_N)^{-1/2}+(N^{-1/2}/\eta_N)^{1/2}\right),
\end{equation*}
and $\varepsilon_N\to0$ by~\eqref{e.eta_N_def}. Integrating over the remaining coordinates of $y\in[1,2]^{\mathscr{S}}$ and summing over $s$, we conclude that
\begin{equation}
    \sup_{x,q}\int_{[1,2]^{\mathscr{S}}}a_N(y)\,\mathrm{d} y\leqslant|\mathscr{S}|\varepsilon_N,
    \qquad\text{where}\qquad
    a_N(y):=\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}\mathbb{E}\left\langle\left|E_s-e^s_N\right|\right\rangle_0.
    \label{e.bulk_radial_self_averaging}
\end{equation}

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{Step 2: Transfer to the interpolating measures.}\par
Fix $\mathsf{t}\in[0,1]$. Since $E_s$ does not depend on $\tau$, its averages under $\left\langle\cdot\right\rangle^{\otimes}_{N,L}$ coincide with those under $\left\langle\cdot\right\rangle_0$. By the change of density~\eqref{e.cavity_tilt_change_of_density}, the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality, and the bound on $\mathbb{E}\left\langle R_\mathsf{t}^2\right\rangle^{\otimes}_{N,L}$ in Lemma~\ref{l.fixed_tilt_uniform_bounds},
\begin{align*}
    \mathbb{E}\left\langle|E_s-e^s_N|\right\rangle_{N,\mathsf{t},L}
    =\mathbb{E}\left\langle|E_s-e^s_N|R_\mathsf{t}\right\rangle^{\otimes}_{N,L}
    &\leqslant\left(\mathbb{E}\left\langle|E_s-e^s_N|^2\right\rangle_0\right)^{1/2}\left(\mathbb{E}\left\langle R_\mathsf{t}^2\right\rangle^{\otimes}_{N,L}\right)^{1/2}\\
    &\leqslant C\left(\mathbb{E}\left\langle|E_s-e^s_N|^2\right\rangle_0\right)^{1/2}.
\end{align*}
By H\"older's inequality, $\mathbb{E}\left\langle X^2\right\rangle_0\leqslant(\mathbb{E}\left\langle|X|\right\rangle_0)^{2/3}(\mathbb{E}\left\langle|X|^4\right\rangle_0)^{1/3}$ for every random variable $X$, and for $X:=E_s-e^s_N$ the fourth moment is bounded by Lemma~\ref{l.fixed_tilt_uniform_bounds} and $|e^s_N|\leqslant C$. Hence
\begin{equation*}
    \mathbb{E}\left\langle|E_s-e^s_N|\right\rangle_{N,\mathsf{t},L}\leqslant C\left(\mathbb{E}\left\langle|E_s-e^s_N|\right\rangle_0\right)^{1/3}\leqslant C\,a_N(y)^{1/3}.
\end{equation*}
Summing over $s$ and integrating over $\mathsf{t}\in[0,1]$, we obtain from the definition~\eqref{e.radial_error_def} that
\begin{equation*}
    \operatorname{Rad}_{N,L}(x,y,q)\leqslant C\,a_N(y)^{1/3}.
\end{equation*}
Integrating over $y\in[1,2]^{\mathscr{S}}$, using Jensen's inequality for the concave function $u\mapsto u^{1/3}$, and then~\eqref{e.bulk_radial_self_averaging}, we conclude that
\begin{equation*}
    \sup_{x,q}\int_{[1,2]^{\mathscr{S}}}\operatorname{Rad}_{N,L}(x,y,q)\,\mathrm{d} y\leqslant C\left(|\mathscr{S}|\varepsilon_N\right)^{1/3}\xrightarrow[N\to\infty]{}0.
\end{equation*}
This completes the proof.
<!-- end proof-24 -->
<!-- proposition-7: body_md -->
\label{p.chart_to_gaussian}
Fix $L\geqslant1$ and a bounded continuous function $f$ of finitely many replicas of $(\tau,\alpha)$. There exist constants $C_L,C_{f,L}<\infty$ and sequences $(\varepsilon_{N,L})_N$ and $(\varepsilon_{N,f,L})_N$ of nonnegative numbers converging to zero, all independent of $x,y,q$, such that
\begin{gather}
    \Big|\mathbb{E}\log Z^{x,y,q,\mathrm{ch}}_{N+M,L,\widetilde V}
    -\mathbb{E}\log Z^{x,y,q,\boldsymbol{\gamma}}_{N,L,\mathsf X,b_N}-\frac12\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}M_se^s_N\Big|
    \leqslant C_L\operatorname{Rad}_{N,L}(x,y,q)+\varepsilon_{N,L},
    \label{e.partition_chart_to_gaussian}
    \\
    \left|\mathbb{E}\left\langle f\right\rangle^{x,y,q,\mathrm{ch}}_{N+M,L,\widetilde V}-\mathbb{E}\left\langle f\right\rangle^{x,y,q,\boldsymbol{\gamma}}_{N,L,\mathsf X,b_N}\right|
    \leqslant C_{f,L}\operatorname{Rad}_{N,L}(x,y,q)+\varepsilon_{N,f,L}.
    \label{e.normalized_chart_to_gaussian}
\end{gather}
<!-- end proposition-7 -->
<!-- proof-25: body_md -->
We take $N$ large enough that $\{|\tau|\leqslant L+1\}\subseteq\mathcal B_N$, and we suppose that $f$ depends on $n$ replicas.

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{Step 1: Replacement of $p_N^{\mathrm{ch}}(\tau)\mathrm{d}\tau$ by $\boldsymbol{\gamma}_M(\mathrm{d}\tau)$.}\par
For a finite measure $\nu$ on $\mathbb{R}^M$, set
\begin{equation*}
    Z_N[\nu]:=\iiint\chi_L(\tau)e^{H_{N+M}^{x,q}((S_{r_N(\tau)}\sigma,\tau),\alpha)+\widetilde V_N^{x,y,q}(\sigma,\alpha)}\,\nu(\mathrm{d}\tau)\,P_N(\mathrm{d}\sigma)\,\mathfrak{R}(\mathrm{d}\alpha),
\end{equation*}
and let $\left\langle\cdot\right\rangle_{N,\nu}$ be the associated Gibbs bracket. With $\nu=p^{\mathrm{ch}}_N(\tau)\mathrm{d}\tau$, we recover $Z^{x,y,q,\mathrm{ch}}_{N+M,L,\widetilde V}$ and $\left\langle\cdot\right\rangle^{x,y,q,\mathrm{ch}}_{N+M,L,\widetilde V}$ from~\eqref{e.radially_inserted_full_partition_L}. Set
\begin{equation*}
    \delta_{N,L}:=\sup_{|\tau|\leqslant L+1}\left|\log\frac{p_N^{\mathrm{ch}}(\tau)}{(2\pi)^{-M/2}e^{-|\tau|^2/2}}\right|,
\end{equation*}
which tends to zero as $N\to\infty$ by Lemma~\ref{l.block_disintegration} and~\eqref{e.radial_factor}. On the support of $\chi_L$, the two densities are within a factor $e^{\pm\delta_{N,L}}$ of each other, so that $Z_N[p^{\mathrm{ch}}_N\mathrm{d}\tau]$ and $Z_N[\boldsymbol{\gamma}_M]$ are within a factor $e^{\pm\delta_{N,L}}$ of each other, and the Radon--Nikodym derivative of the one-replica Gibbs measure $\left\langle\cdot\right\rangle_{N,p^{\mathrm{ch}}_N\mathrm{d}\tau}$ with respect to $\left\langle\cdot\right\rangle_{N,\boldsymbol{\gamma}_M}$ takes values in $[e^{-2\delta_{N,L}},e^{2\delta_{N,L}}]$. Taking the $n$-fold product, we obtain
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
    \left|\mathbb{E}\log Z_N[p^{\mathrm{ch}}_N\mathrm{d}\tau]-\mathbb{E}\log Z_N[\boldsymbol{\gamma}_M]\right|&\leqslant\delta_{N,L}\qquad\text{and}\\
    \left|\mathbb{E}\left\langle f\right\rangle_{N,p^{\mathrm{ch}}_N\mathrm{d}\tau}-\mathbb{E}\left\langle f\right\rangle_{N,\boldsymbol{\gamma}_M}\right|&\leqslant\|f\|_\infty\left(e^{2n\delta_{N,L}}-1\right).
\end{aligned}
\label{e.chart_density_replacement}
\end{equation}

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{Step 2: Expansion of the Hamiltonian.}\par
By Lemma~\ref{l.chart_hamiltonian_expansion}, then by Lemma~\ref{l.radial_first_order_expansion} applied with the cavity field $\sum_j\tau_j\mathsf X^q_{N,j}$ added to both sides, which is allowed since this field is independent of $\widetilde H_N$, $W^q_N$, and $H^x_N$, and finally by the first identity in~\eqref{e.radial_interpolation_endpoints}, we have
\begin{equation*}
    H_{N+M}^{x,q}\left((S_{r_N(\tau)}\sigma,\tau),\alpha\right)+\widetilde V_N^{x,y,q}(\sigma,\alpha)\mathrel{\hstretch{1.8}{\approx}}\mathcal H_{N,1}(\sigma,\tau,\alpha)+\frac12\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}M_se^s_N,
\end{equation*}
uniformly over $x,y,q$ and $(\sigma,\tau,\alpha)\in\Sigma_N\times\{|\tau|\leqslant L+1\}\times\mathfrak U$. For $\mathsf{t}\in[0,1]$, let
\begin{equation*}
    \mathcal Z_N(\mathsf{t}):=\iiint\chi_L(\tau)e^{\mathcal H_{N,\mathsf{t}}(\sigma,\tau,\alpha)}\boldsymbol{\gamma}_M(\mathrm{d}\tau)\,P_N(\mathrm{d}\sigma)\,\mathfrak{R}(\mathrm{d}\alpha),
\end{equation*}
whose Gibbs bracket is $\left\langle\cdot\right\rangle_{N,\mathsf{t},L}$. Since the constant $\frac12\sum_sM_se^s_N$ is deterministic and bounded, Lemma~\ref{l.gaussian_comparison_covariance_norm} gives sequences $\varepsilon'_{N,L},\varepsilon'_{N,f,L}\to0$, independent of $x,y,q$, such that
\begin{equation}
    \Big|\mathbb{E}\log Z_N[\boldsymbol{\gamma}_M]-\mathbb{E}\log\mathcal Z_N(1)-\frac12\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}M_se^s_N\Big|\leqslant\varepsilon'_{N,L}
    \qquad\text{and}\qquad
    \left|\mathbb{E}\left\langle f\right\rangle_{N,\boldsymbol{\gamma}_M}-\mathbb{E}\left\langle f\right\rangle_{N,1,L}\right|\leqslant\varepsilon'_{N,f,L}.
    \label{e.chart_field_comparison}
\end{equation}

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{Step 3: Interpolation in $\mathsf{t}$.}\par
Differentiating in $\mathsf{t}$ and using~\eqref{e.interpolating_hamiltonian}, we find
\begin{equation*}
    \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d} \mathsf{t}}\mathbb{E}\log\mathcal Z_N(\mathsf{t})=\frac12\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}\mathbb{E}\left\langle\left(M_s-|\tau^{(s)}|^2\right)\left(\widetilde{\mathcal E}_{N,s}^{x,q}-e_N^s\right)\right\rangle_{N,\mathsf{t},L}.
\end{equation*}
Since $|M_s-|\tau^{(s)}|^2|\leqslant M_s+(L+1)^2$ on the support of $\chi_L$, we obtain from~\eqref{e.radial_error_def} that
\begin{equation}
    \left|\mathbb{E}\log\mathcal Z_N(1)-\mathbb{E}\log\mathcal Z_N(0)\right|\leqslant C_L\operatorname{Rad}_{N,L}(x,y,q).
    \label{e.radial_interpolation_partition_bound}
\end{equation}
Similarly, writing $z^\ell=(\sigma^\ell,\tau^\ell,\alpha^\ell)$ for the replicas,
\begin{align*}
    \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d} \mathsf{t}}\mathbb{E}\left\langle f\right\rangle_{N,\mathsf{t},L}=\frac12\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}\mathbb{E}\Bigg\langle f\Bigg(&\sum_{\ell=1}^n\left(M_s-|\tau^{\ell,(s)}|^2\right)\left(\widetilde{\mathcal E}_{N,s}^{x,q}(\sigma^\ell,\alpha^\ell)-e_N^s\right)\\
    &-n\left(M_s-|\tau^{n+1,(s)}|^2\right)\left(\widetilde{\mathcal E}_{N,s}^{x,q}(\sigma^{n+1},\alpha^{n+1})-e_N^s\right)\Bigg)\Bigg\rangle_{N,\mathsf{t},L},
\end{align*}
and since the replicas are exchangeable,
\begin{equation}
    \left|\mathbb{E}\left\langle f\right\rangle_{N,1,L}-\mathbb{E}\left\langle f\right\rangle_{N,0,L}\right|\leqslant C_{f,L}\operatorname{Rad}_{N,L}(x,y,q).
    \label{e.radial_interpolation_replica_bound}
\end{equation}

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{Step 4: Conclusion.}\par
By the second identity in~\eqref{e.radial_interpolation_endpoints}, we have $\mathcal Z_N(0)=Z^{x,y,q,\boldsymbol{\gamma}}_{N,L,\mathsf X,b_N}$ and $\left\langle\cdot\right\rangle_{N,0,L}=\left\langle\cdot\right\rangle^{x,y,q,\boldsymbol{\gamma}}_{N,L,\mathsf X,b_N}$. Combining~\eqref{e.chart_density_replacement}, \eqref{e.chart_field_comparison}, \eqref{e.radial_interpolation_partition_bound}, and~\eqref{e.radial_interpolation_replica_bound} proves~\eqref{e.partition_chart_to_gaussian} and~\eqref{e.normalized_chart_to_gaussian}, with $\varepsilon_{N,L}:=\delta_{N,L}+\varepsilon'_{N,L}$ and $\varepsilon_{N,f,L}:=\|f\|_\infty(e^{2n\delta_{N,L}}-1)+\varepsilon'_{N,f,L}$.
<!-- end proof-25 -->
<!-- lemma-19: body_md -->
\label{l.diagonal_compensation}
Let $L\geqslant1$, $e\in\mathbb{R}^{\mathscr{S}}$, and $\pi,\pi'\in\mathcal Q_\infty^{\mathscr{S}}$. Then
\begin{equation}
    \left|\mathcal D_{M,L}\left(\pi,b(\pi,e)\right)-\mathcal D_{M,L}\left(\pi',b(\pi',e)\right)\right|\leqslant M(L+1)^2\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}|\pi^s-\pi'^s|_{L^1},
    \label{e.diagonal_compensation_partition}
\end{equation}
and, for every $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and every bounded measurable function $f$ of $n$ replicas of $(\tau,\alpha)$, there is a constant $C_n<\infty$, depending only on $n$, such that
\begin{equation}
    \left|\mathbb{E}\left\langle f\right\rangle^{\pi,\mathfrak{R}}_{M,L,b(\pi,e)}-\mathbb{E}\left\langle f\right\rangle^{\pi',\mathfrak{R}}_{M,L,b(\pi',e)}\right|\leqslant C_n\|f\|_\infty M(L+1)^2\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}|\pi^s-\pi'^s|_{L^1}.
    \label{e.diagonal_compensation_observable}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-19 -->
<!-- proof-26: body_md -->
For $\mathsf{t}\in[0,1]$, set $u_\mathsf{t}:=(1-\mathsf{t})\pi+\mathsf{t}\pi'\in\mathcal Q_\infty^{\mathscr{S}}$ and $b_\mathsf{t}:=b(u_\mathsf{t},e)$, so that $(u_0,b_0)=(\pi,b(\pi,e))$ and $(u_1,b_1)=(\pi',b(\pi',e))$, and realize the cascade fields jointly as $w^{u_\mathsf{t}^s}_j:=\sqrt{1-\mathsf{t}}\,w^{\pi^s}_j+\sqrt{\mathsf{t}}\,w^{\pi'^s}_j$, with independent fields $w^{\pi^s}_j$ and $w^{\pi'^s}_j$. The covariance of the field $\sqrt2w^{u_\mathsf{t}^s}_j(\alpha)\tau_j$ is $2u_\mathsf{t}^s(\alpha\wedge\alpha')\tau_j\tau'_j$, whose derivative in $\mathsf{t}$ is $2(\pi'^s-\pi^s)(\alpha\wedge\alpha')\tau_j\tau'_j$. Gaussian integration by parts, as in the proof of Lemma~\ref{l.gaussian_comparison_covariance_norm}, together with the derivative $\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}\mathsf{t}}b_\mathsf{t}^s=2(\pi'^s(1)-\pi^s(1))$ of the quadratic coefficient, gives
\begin{align*}
    \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}\mathsf{t}}\mathbb{E}\log Z_{M,L,b_\mathsf{t}}^{u_\mathsf{t},\mathfrak{R}}={}&\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}\sum_{j\in\mathsf M_s}\left(\pi'^s(1)-\pi^s(1)\right)\mathbb{E}\left\langle\tau_j^2\right\rangle^{u_\mathsf{t},\mathfrak{R}}_{M,L,b_\mathsf{t}}-\frac12\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}\sum_{j\in\mathsf M_s}\frac{\mathrm{d} b^s_\mathsf{t}}{\mathrm{d}\mathsf{t}}\,\mathbb{E}\left\langle\tau_j^2\right\rangle^{u_\mathsf{t},\mathfrak{R}}_{M,L,b_\mathsf{t}}\\
    &-\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}\sum_{j\in\mathsf M_s}\mathbb{E}\left\langle\tau_j\tau_j'\left(\pi'^s-\pi^s\right)(\alpha\wedge\alpha')\right\rangle_{M,L,b_\mathsf{t}}^{u_\mathsf{t},\mathfrak{R}}.
\end{align*}
The first term is the diagonal term of the integration by parts, the second one comes from the derivative of the quadratic coefficient, and the two cancel exactly, since $\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}\mathsf{t}}b^s_\mathsf{t}=2(\pi'^s(1)-\pi^s(1))$. This cancellation is the point of the parametrization~\eqref{e.b_pi_e_def}. On the support of $\chi_L$, we have $|\tau_j\tau'_j|\leqslant(L+1)^2$. Moreover, integrating out the cavity coordinates, the bracket $\left\langle\cdot\right\rangle^{u_\mathsf{t},\mathfrak{R}}_{M,L,b_\mathsf{t}}$ tilts the cascade by the factor $\exp(\mathbf g(w^{u_\mathsf{t}}(\alpha)))$, where $w^{u_\mathsf{t}}=(w^{u_\mathsf{t}^s}_j)_{j\in[M]}$ and
\begin{equation*}
    \mathbf g(w):=\log\int\chi_L(\tau)\exp\Big(\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}\sum_{j\in\mathsf M_s}\left((\sqrt2w_j+h^{s})\tau_j-\tfrac12(b^s_\mathsf{t}-1)\tau_j^2\right)\Big)\boldsymbol{\gamma}_M(\mathrm{d}\tau)
\end{equation*}
is a Lipschitz function on $\mathbb{R}^M$, since its gradient is $\sqrt2$ times a Gibbs average of $\tau$ restricted to $\{|\tau|\leqslant L+1\}$. By the invariance~\eqref{e.invariance_cascade}, the overlap $\alpha\wedge\alpha'$ is therefore uniformly distributed on $[0,1]$ under this bracket, so that the remaining sum is bounded in absolute value by $(L+1)^2\sum_sM_s|\pi'^s-\pi^s|_{L^1}\leqslant M(L+1)^2\sum_s|\pi^s-\pi'^s|_{L^1}$. Integrating over $\mathsf{t}\in[0,1]$, and recalling that the additive constant in~\eqref{e.direct_canonical} is $\frac12\sum_sM_se^s$ at both endpoints, proves~\eqref{e.diagonal_compensation_partition}. The same interpolation applied to $\mathbb{E}\left\langle f\right\rangle^{u_\mathsf{t},\mathfrak{R}}_{M,L,b_\mathsf{t}}$ produces, as in the proof of Lemma~\ref{l.gaussian_comparison_covariance_norm}, a finite sum of Gibbs averages of $f$ multiplied by the terms $(\pi'^s-\pi^s)(\alpha^\ell\wedge\alpha^{\ell'})\tau^\ell_j\tau^{\ell'}_j$ for $\ell,\ell'\leqslant n+2$, again with an exact cancellation of the diagonal terms; the overlaps $\alpha^\ell\wedge\alpha^{\ell'}$ with $\ell\ne\ell'$ are uniformly distributed by the same invariance, and~\eqref{e.diagonal_compensation_observable} follows.
<!-- end proof-26 -->
<!-- lemma-20: body_md -->
\label{l.canonical_normalization_identity}
Let $\pi\in\mathcal Q_\infty^{\mathscr{S}}$ and let $b$ be admissible for $\pi$. The function $b\mapsto\mathcal D_M(\pi,b)$ is convex on the set of admissible $b$, with
\begin{gather}
    \partial_{b^s}\mathcal D_M(\pi,b)
    =\frac{M_s}{2}-\frac12\mathbb{E}\left\langle |\tau^{(s)}|^2\right\rangle^{\pi,\mathfrak{R}}_{M,b},
    \qquad s\in\mathscr{S},
    \label{e.direct_canonical_derivative}
\end{gather}
and $\mathcal D_M(\pi,b)\geqslant -M\psi(\pi)$. Moreover, if
\begin{equation}
    \mathbb{E}\left\langle|\tau^{(s)}|^2\right\rangle^{\pi,\mathfrak{R}}_{M,b}=M_s\qquad\text{for every }s\in\mathscr{S},
    \label{e.block_normalization_condition}
\end{equation}
then $b=b_\pi$ and $\mathcal D_M(\pi,b)=-M\psi(\pi)$; if in addition $\pi=q+t\nabla\xi(p)$ for some $p\in\mathcal Q_{\infty,\leqslant\lambda}^{\mathscr{S}}$, then
\begin{align}
    \mathcal P_{M,t,q}(p,b)=-M\mathscr{P}_{t,q}(p).
    \label{e.canonical_equals_Parisi}
\end{align}
<!-- end lemma-20 -->
<!-- proof-27: body_md -->
By~\eqref{e.canonical_additivity} and part~\eqref{i.multiplier_minimizer} of Lemma~\ref{l.multiplier}, the function $b\mapsto\mathcal D_M(\pi,b)$ is a sum over $s\in\mathscr{S}$ of strictly convex functions of $b^s$, hence it is convex. For each $s\in\mathscr{S}$, the function $b^s\mapsto\log Z^{\pi,\mathfrak{R}}_{M,b}$ is almost surely convex on the admissible set, with derivative $-\frac12\left\langle|\tau^{(s)}|^2\right\rangle^{\pi,\mathfrak{R}}_{M,b}$, and the monotone convergence argument of Step~5 of the proof of Lemma~\ref{l.scalar_initial_continuous_derivative}, which applies verbatim to the block with $M$ coordinates, shows that $b^s\mapsto\mathbb{E}\log Z^{\pi,\mathfrak{R}}_{M,b}$ is differentiable with derivative $-\frac12\mathbb{E}\left\langle|\tau^{(s)}|^2\right\rangle^{\pi,\mathfrak{R}}_{M,b}$; together with~\eqref{e.direct_canonical}, this gives~\eqref{e.direct_canonical_derivative}. The lower bound is~\eqref{e.canonical_infimum}. Under~\eqref{e.block_normalization_condition}, the derivatives in~\eqref{e.direct_canonical_derivative} vanish, so that $b$ is a critical point of the convex function $b\mapsto\mathcal D_M(\pi,b)$, hence a minimizer. By~\eqref{e.canonical_additivity} and the uniqueness of the minimizer in Lemma~\ref{l.scalar_initial_continuous_derivative}, we get $b=b_\pi$ and $\mathcal D_M(\pi,b)=-M\psi(\pi)$. Finally, if $\pi=q+t\nabla\xi(p)$, then~\eqref{e.canonical_ASS_functional}, \eqref{e.reaction_value}, and~\eqref{e.spherical_Parisi_functional} give
\begin{equation*}
    \mathcal P_{M,t,q}(p,b)=-M\psi\left(q+t\nabla\xi(p)\right)+tM\int_0^1\theta(p(r))\,\mathrm{d} r=-M\mathscr{P}_{t,q}(p). \qedhere
\end{equation*}
<!-- end proof-27 -->
<!-- lemma-21: body_md -->
\label{l.derivative_initial}
Let $\pi\in\mathcal Q_\infty^{\mathscr{S}}$, and let $b_\pi$ be as in~\eqref{e.b_pi_def}. For every $\kappa\in\mathcal Q_\infty^{\mathscr{S}}$, we have
\begin{align}
    \left\langle\kappa,\partial_q\psi(\pi)\right\rangle_{L^2}
    =\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}\mathbb{E}\left\langle\kappa^s(\alpha\wedge\alpha')
    \widetilde R_{M,s}(\tau,\tau')\right\rangle^{\pi,\mathfrak{R}}_{M,b_\pi}.
    \label{e.derivative_initial_formula_block}
\end{align}
<!-- end lemma-21 -->
<!-- proof-28: body_md -->
Write $b:=b_\pi$, $\overline\kappa:=\max_{s\in\mathscr{S}}\kappa^s(1)$, and $\pi_\varepsilon:=\pi+\varepsilon\kappa\in\mathcal Q_\infty^{\mathscr{S}}$ for $\varepsilon\geqslant0$, and fix $\varepsilon_0\in(0,1]$ such that $4\varepsilon_0\mathcal K(\kappa^s)\leqslant1$ for every $s\in\mathscr{S}$. Since $\mathcal K$ is linear, and since $b^s-2\mathcal K(\pi^s)=\ell_{h^s}(\pi^s)\geqslant1$ by~\eqref{e.b_a_def} and~\eqref{e.uniform_gap}, we have $b^s-2\mathcal K(\pi^s_\varepsilon)=\ell_{h^s}(\pi^s)-2\varepsilon\mathcal K(\kappa^s)\geqslant\frac12$ for every $\varepsilon\in[0,\varepsilon_0]$ and $s\in\mathscr{S}$; in particular, $b$ is admissible for $\pi_\varepsilon$. We compute the derivative of $\varepsilon\mapsto\mathcal D_M(\pi_\varepsilon,b)$ at $\varepsilon=0$ in two ways: from the explicit formula, and by Gaussian integration by parts. Since the covariance of the block without cutoff is unbounded, the integration by parts is performed with a cutoff, which is then removed.

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{Step 1: The explicit formula.}\par
Recall the function $\widehat J_a$ from Step~1 of the proof of Proposition~\ref{l.psi_spherical_smooth}. By~\eqref{e.canonical_additivity} and~\eqref{e.b_a_def},
\begin{equation*}
    \mathcal D_M(\pi_\varepsilon,b)=\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}M_s\,\widehat J_{h^s}\left(\pi^s_\varepsilon,\ell_{h^s}(\pi^s)-2\varepsilon\mathcal K(\kappa^s)\right).
\end{equation*}
By Step~2 of that proof, applied to the segment from $\pi^s$ to $\pi^s+\kappa^s$, the function $(\varepsilon,\ell)\mapsto\widehat J_{h^s}(\pi^s_\varepsilon,\ell)$ is differentiable in $\varepsilon$, and its derivative, given by~\eqref{e.J_hat_s_derivative}, is jointly continuous on $[0,1]\times(0,\infty)$. It is also differentiable in $\ell$, with $\partial_\ell\widehat J_{h^s}(\pi^s_\varepsilon,\ell)=\frac12(1-S_{h^s}(\pi^s_\varepsilon,\ell))$ by~\eqref{e.D_b_derivative_explicit}, and this derivative is jointly continuous as well, by the dominated convergence argument given at the end of that step. We can therefore apply the chain rule. Since $S_{h^s}(\pi^s,\ell_{h^s}(\pi^s))=1$, the derivative in $\ell$ does not contribute at $\varepsilon=0$, and by~\eqref{e.J_hat_s_derivative}, \eqref{e.zeta_explicit}, \eqref{e.derivative_psi_lambda}, and $M_s=\lambda_sM$, we obtain
\begin{equation}
    \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}\varepsilon}\mathcal D_M(\pi_\varepsilon,b)\Big|_{\varepsilon=0}=-\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}M_s\int_0^1\kappa^s(u)\zeta_{h^s,\pi^s}(u)\,\mathrm{d} u=-M\left\langle\kappa,\partial_q\psi(\pi)\right\rangle_{L^2}.
    \label{e.derivative_initial_explicit}
\end{equation}
Moreover, by~\eqref{e.direct_canonical_derivative}, \eqref{e.canonical_additivity}, and~\eqref{e.D_b_derivative_explicit},
\begin{equation}
    \mathbb{E}\left\langle|\tau^{(s)}|^2\right\rangle^{\pi_\varepsilon,\mathfrak{R}}_{M,b}=M_sS_{h^s}\left(\pi^s_\varepsilon,b^s-2\mathcal K(\pi^s_\varepsilon)\right),
    \qquad s\in\mathscr{S},
    \label{e.derivative_initial_second_moment}
\end{equation}
which is a continuous function of $\varepsilon\in[0,\varepsilon_0]$, by the joint continuity just mentioned, and is therefore bounded on this interval.

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{Step 2: Integration by parts with a cutoff.}\par
Conditionally on $\mathfrak{R}$, let $(w_j^{\kappa^s})_{s\in\mathscr{S},j\in\mathsf M_s}$ be independent Gaussian fields with covariances $\kappa^s(\alpha\wedge\alpha')$, independent of the fields $(w_j^{\pi^s})_{s\in\mathscr{S},j\in\mathsf M_s}$, and realize the fields of the block with path $\pi_\varepsilon$ as $w_j^{\pi^s_\varepsilon}:=w_j^{\pi^s}+\sqrt\varepsilon\,w_j^{\kappa^s}$. The exponent in~\eqref{e.U_pi_b_def} then reads
\begin{equation*}
    U_\varepsilon:=U_{\pi_\varepsilon,b}=U_{\pi,b}+\sqrt\varepsilon\,\mathsf v,
    \qquad
    \mathsf v(\tau,\alpha):=\sqrt2\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}\sum_{j\in\mathsf M_s}w_j^{\kappa^s}(\alpha)\tau_j.
\end{equation*}
For $L\in[1,\infty]$ and $\varepsilon\in[0,\varepsilon_0]$, let $Z_{L,\varepsilon}$ and $\left\langle\cdot\right\rangle_{L,\varepsilon}$ be defined as in~\eqref{e.canonical_cutoff_partition_def}, with the exponent $U_\varepsilon$ and with $\chi_L$ replaced by the indicator function of $\{|\tau|\leqslant L\}$, so that $Z_{\infty,\varepsilon}=Z^{\pi_\varepsilon,\mathfrak{R}}_{M,b}$ and $\left\langle\cdot\right\rangle_{\infty,\varepsilon}=\left\langle\cdot\right\rangle^{\pi_\varepsilon,\mathfrak{R}}_{M,b}$. We set
\begin{equation*}
    X_{L,\varepsilon}:=\left\langle|\tau|^2\right\rangle_{L,\varepsilon},
    \qquad
    D_{L,\varepsilon}:=\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}\kappa^s(1)\left\langle|\tau^{(s)}|^2\right\rangle_{L,\varepsilon},
    \qquad
    Y_{L,\varepsilon}:=\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}\left\langle\kappa^s(\alpha\wedge\alpha')\sum_{j\in\mathsf M_s}\tau_j\tau_j'\right\rangle_{L,\varepsilon},
\end{equation*}
and $\Phi_L(\varepsilon):=\mathbb{E} D_{L,\varepsilon}-\mathbb{E} Y_{L,\varepsilon}$. Since $0\leqslant\kappa^s\leqslant\overline\kappa$, the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality, the independence of the replicas under the bracket, and Jensen's inequality give
\begin{equation}
    0\leqslant D_{L,\varepsilon}\leqslant\overline\kappa X_{L,\varepsilon}
    \qquad\text{and}\qquad
    |Y_{L,\varepsilon}|\leqslant\overline\kappa\left\langle|\tau|\,|\tau'|\right\rangle_{L,\varepsilon}\leqslant\overline\kappa X_{L,\varepsilon}.
    \label{e.derivative_initial_domination}
\end{equation}
By~\eqref{e.derivative_initial_second_moment}, the random variable $X_{\infty,\varepsilon}$ is integrable, so that $\Phi_\infty(\varepsilon)$ is well defined. Let $L<\infty$. The covariance $2\pi^s_\varepsilon(\alpha\wedge\alpha')\tau_j\tau_j'$ of the field $\sqrt2w_j^{\pi^s_\varepsilon}(\alpha)\tau_j$ is bounded on $\{|\tau|\leqslant L\}$, and its derivative in $\varepsilon$ is $2\kappa^s(\alpha\wedge\alpha')\tau_j\tau_j'$. The function $\varepsilon\mapsto\mathbb{E}\log Z_{L,\varepsilon}$ is continuous on $[0,\varepsilon_0]$, and Gaussian integration by parts, as in the proofs of Lemmas~\ref{l.gaussian_comparison_covariance_norm} and~\ref{l.diagonal_compensation}, shows that it is differentiable on $(0,\varepsilon_0]$ with derivative $\Phi_L(\varepsilon)$, the term $\mathbb{E} D_{L,\varepsilon}$ coming from the diagonal of the covariance. Since $|\Phi_L|\leqslant2\overline\kappa L^2$, we obtain
\begin{equation}
    \mathbb{E}\log Z_{L,\varepsilon}-\mathbb{E}\log Z_{L,0}=\int_0^\varepsilon\Phi_L(\varepsilon')\,\mathrm{d}\varepsilon',
    \qquad\varepsilon\in[0,\varepsilon_0].
    \label{e.derivative_initial_cutoff}
\end{equation}

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{Step 3: Removal of the cutoff.}\par
Fix $\varepsilon\in[0,\varepsilon_0]$. Almost surely, $Z_{\infty,\varepsilon}$ and $X_{\infty,\varepsilon}$ are finite, by Lemma~\ref{l.remove_cutoffs} below and~\eqref{e.derivative_initial_second_moment}. For $L<\infty$, the average $X_{\infty,\varepsilon}$ is a convex combination of $X_{L,\varepsilon}\leqslant L^2$ and of an average of $|\tau|^2$ over $\{|\tau|>L\}$, which is at least $L^2$; hence $X_{L,\varepsilon}\leqslant X_{\infty,\varepsilon}$. By dominated convergence with respect to the measure $e^{U_\varepsilon}\boldsymbol{\gamma}_M\otimes\mathfrak{R}$ and its tensor square, we have $D_{L,\varepsilon}\to D_{\infty,\varepsilon}$ and $Y_{L,\varepsilon}\to Y_{\infty,\varepsilon}$ almost surely as $L\to\infty$, and by~\eqref{e.derivative_initial_domination}, these random variables are bounded by $\overline\kappa X_{\infty,\varepsilon}$, which is integrable. Hence $\Phi_L(\varepsilon)\to\Phi_\infty(\varepsilon)$ as $L\to\infty$, with $|\Phi_L(\varepsilon)|\leqslant2\overline\kappa\,\mathbb{E} X_{\infty,\varepsilon}$, and the right-hand side is bounded uniformly over $\varepsilon\in[0,\varepsilon_0]$ by Step~1. Moreover, $\mathbb{E}\log Z_{L,\varepsilon}\to\mathbb{E}\log Z_{\infty,\varepsilon}$ by monotone convergence, as in the proof of Lemma~\ref{l.remove_cutoffs}, whose lower bound on the partition function uses only the unit ball. Letting $L\to\infty$ in~\eqref{e.derivative_initial_cutoff}, we obtain, by dominated convergence,
\begin{equation}
    \mathbb{E}\log Z^{\pi_\varepsilon,\mathfrak{R}}_{M,b}-\mathbb{E}\log Z^{\pi,\mathfrak{R}}_{M,b}=\int_0^\varepsilon\Phi_\infty(\varepsilon')\,\mathrm{d}\varepsilon',
    \qquad\varepsilon\in[0,\varepsilon_0].
    \label{e.derivative_initial_integrated}
\end{equation}

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{Step 4: Continuity at $\varepsilon=0$.}\par
We show that $\Phi_\infty(\varepsilon)\to\Phi_\infty(0)$ as $\varepsilon\to0$. The term $\mathbb{E} D_{\infty,\varepsilon}$ is a continuous function of $\varepsilon$, by~\eqref{e.derivative_initial_second_moment}. For the other term, we use that $e^{\sqrt\varepsilon\mathsf v}\leqslant1+e^{\sqrt{\varepsilon_0}\mathsf v}$, so that $e^{U_\varepsilon}\leqslant e^{U_0}+e^{U_{\varepsilon_0}}$ for every $\varepsilon\in[0,\varepsilon_0]$. Almost surely, the function $(1+|\tau|^2)(e^{U_0}+e^{U_{\varepsilon_0}})$ is integrable with respect to $\boldsymbol{\gamma}_M\otimes\mathfrak{R}$, since $Z_{\infty,\varepsilon}$ and $X_{\infty,\varepsilon}$ are finite for $\varepsilon\in\{0,\varepsilon_0\}$. By dominated convergence, applied to the numerators and to the denominators of the brackets, we have $X_{\infty,\varepsilon}\to X_{\infty,0}$ and $Y_{\infty,\varepsilon}\to Y_{\infty,0}$ almost surely as $\varepsilon\to0$. Moreover, $\mathbb{E} X_{\infty,\varepsilon}\to\mathbb{E} X_{\infty,0}$ by~\eqref{e.derivative_initial_second_moment}. Since $\overline\kappa X_{\infty,\varepsilon}\pm Y_{\infty,\varepsilon}\geqslant0$ by~\eqref{e.derivative_initial_domination}, Fatou's lemma gives
\begin{equation*}
    \overline\kappa\,\mathbb{E} X_{\infty,0}\pm\mathbb{E} Y_{\infty,0}\leqslant\liminf_{\varepsilon\to0}\left(\overline\kappa\,\mathbb{E} X_{\infty,\varepsilon}\pm\mathbb{E} Y_{\infty,\varepsilon}\right)=\overline\kappa\,\mathbb{E} X_{\infty,0}+\liminf_{\varepsilon\to0}\left(\pm\mathbb{E} Y_{\infty,\varepsilon}\right),
\end{equation*}
that is, $\mathbb{E} Y_{\infty,\varepsilon}\to\mathbb{E} Y_{\infty,0}$.

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{Step 5: Conclusion.}\par
By~\eqref{e.derivative_initial_integrated} and Step~4, the function $\varepsilon\mapsto\mathbb{E}\log Z^{\pi_\varepsilon,\mathfrak{R}}_{M,b}$ is differentiable at $\varepsilon=0$, with derivative $\Phi_\infty(0)$. By~\eqref{e.direct_canonical}, we thus have
\begin{align*}
    \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}\varepsilon}\mathcal D_M(\pi_\varepsilon,b_\pi)\Big|_{\varepsilon=0}
    ={}&\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}\kappa^s(1)\left(\mathbb{E}\left\langle|\tau^{(s)}|^2\right\rangle^{\pi,\mathfrak{R}}_{M,b_\pi}-M_s\right)-\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}\mathbb{E}\left\langle\kappa^s(\alpha\wedge\alpha')\sum_{j\in\mathsf M_s}\tau_j\tau_j'\right\rangle^{\pi,\mathfrak{R}}_{M,b_\pi},
\end{align*}
where the terms $\kappa^s(1)$ come from the diagonal of the covariance and from the last term in~\eqref{e.direct_canonical}. Since $b_\pi$ minimizes $b\mapsto\mathcal D_M(\pi,b)$, the first sum vanishes by~\eqref{e.direct_canonical_derivative}. Comparing with~\eqref{e.derivative_initial_explicit}, dividing by $-M$, and using~\eqref{e.cavity_overlap_def} gives~\eqref{e.derivative_initial_formula_block}.
<!-- end proof-28 -->
<!-- lemma-22: body_md -->
\label{l.linear_rpc_quadratic_gain}
Let $\pi\in\mathcal Q_\infty^{\mathscr{S}}$, and for $\tau\in\mathbb{R}^M$, set $W_M^\pi(\tau,\alpha):=\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}\sum_{j\in\mathsf M_s}\tau_jw_j^{\pi^s}(\alpha)$. We have
\begin{equation*}
    \mathbb{E}\log\int\exp\left(\sqrt2W_M^\pi(\tau,\alpha)\right)\mathfrak{R}(\mathrm{d}\alpha)
    =\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}\mathcal K(\pi^s)|\tau^{(s)}|^2.
\end{equation*}
<!-- end lemma-22 -->
<!-- proof-29: body_md -->
For fixed $\tau$, the field $\sqrt2W_M^\pi(\tau,\cdot)$ is a centered Gaussian field on $\mathfrak U$ with covariance $c(\alpha\wedge\alpha')$, where $c(r):=2\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}|\tau^{(s)}|^2\pi^s(r)$ belongs to $\mathcal Q_\infty$. The result follows from~\eqref{e.cascade_gaussian_identity} and the definition of $\mathcal K$ in~\eqref{e.Krho_def}.
<!-- end proof-29 -->
<!-- lemma-23: body_md -->
\label{l.multispecies_nonadmissible_escape}
Let $\pi\in\mathcal Q_\infty^{\mathscr{S}}$ and $b\in\mathbb{R}^{\mathscr{S}}$. If $b$ is not admissible for $\pi$, then
\begin{equation*}
    \lim_{L\to\infty}\mathbb{E}\log Z^{\pi,\mathfrak{R}}_{M,L,b}=+\infty,\qquad\text{and equivalently}\qquad\lim_{L\to\infty}\mathcal D_{M,L}(\pi,b)=+\infty.
\end{equation*}
<!-- end lemma-23 -->
<!-- proof-30: body_md -->
Set $\Delta_s:=2\mathcal K(\pi^s)-b^s$. Since $b$ is not admissible, there is $s_*\in\mathscr{S}$ with $\Delta_{s_*}\geqslant0$. For $\tau\in\mathbb{R}^M$, let
\begin{equation*}
    v(\tau):=\log\int\exp\left(\sqrt2W_M^\pi(\tau,\alpha)\right)\mathfrak{R}(\mathrm{d}\alpha)
    \qquad\text{and}\qquad
    \Phi(\tau):=\frac12\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}\Delta_s|\tau^{(s)}|^2+\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}h^s\sum_{j\in\mathsf M_s}\tau_j,
\end{equation*}
where $W^\pi_M$ is as in Lemma~\ref{l.linear_rpc_quadratic_gain}. The random function $v$ is convex in $\tau$, and by Lemma~\ref{l.linear_rpc_quadratic_gain}, $\mathbb{E} v(\tau)=\sum_{s}\mathcal K(\pi^s)|\tau^{(s)}|^2$. By~\eqref{e.U_pi_b_def} and $\boldsymbol{\gamma}_M(\mathrm{d}\tau)=(2\pi)^{-M/2}e^{-|\tau|^2/2}\mathrm{d}\tau$, we can therefore write
\begin{equation*}
    Z^{\pi,\mathfrak{R}}_{M,L,b}=(2\pi)^{-M/2}\int\chi_L(\tau)\,e^{\Phi(\tau)}\,e^{v(\tau)-\mathbb{E} v(\tau)}\,\mathrm{d}\tau.
\end{equation*}
Let $\nu_L$ be the probability measure on $\mathbb{R}^M$ with density proportional to $\chi_Le^{\Phi}$, which is well defined since $\chi_L$ has compact support. Jensen's inequality with respect to $\nu_L$ gives
\begin{equation*}
    \log Z^{\pi,\mathfrak{R}}_{M,L,b}\geqslant-\frac M2\log(2\pi)+\log\int\chi_L(\tau)e^{\Phi(\tau)}\,\mathrm{d}\tau+\int\left(v-\mathbb{E} v\right)\mathrm{d}\nu_L.
\end{equation*}
The last term has zero expectation by Fubini's theorem; the required integrability follows from $\mathbb{E}|v(\tau)|\leqslant C(1+|\tau|^2)$, which is a consequence of the lower bound $v(\tau)\geqslant\sqrt2\int W^\pi_M(\tau,\alpha)\,\mathfrak{R}(\mathrm{d}\alpha)$ (Jensen's inequality) and of the upper bound $\mathbb{E} e^{v(\tau)}=\exp(\sum_s\pi^s(1)|\tau^{(s)}|^2)$. Hence
\begin{equation}
\label{e.escape_deterministic_lower_bound}
    \mathbb{E}\log Z^{\pi,\mathfrak{R}}_{M,L,b}\geqslant-\frac M2\log(2\pi)+\log\int\chi_L(\tau)\exp\Bigg(\frac12\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}\Delta_s|\tau^{(s)}|^2+\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}h^s\sum_{j\in\mathsf M_s}\tau_j\Bigg)\mathrm{d}\tau.
\end{equation}
It remains to check that this deterministic integral tends to infinity with $L$. Let $A_L$ be the set of $\tau\in\mathbb{R}^M$ such that $|\tau^{(s_*)}|\leqslant L/2$, $h^{s_*}\sum_{j\in\mathsf M_{s_*}}\tau_j\geqslant0$, and $|\tau^{(u)}|\leqslant1$ for every $u\ne s_*$. For $L\geqslant2|\mathscr{S}|$, every $\tau\in A_L$ satisfies $|\tau|^2\leqslant L^2/4+|\mathscr{S}|\leqslant L^2$, so $\chi_L=1$ on $A_L$ by~\eqref{e.chi_L_def}. On $A_L$, the term $\frac12\Delta_{s_*}|\tau^{(s_*)}|^2$ and the external-field term of the species $s_*$ are nonnegative, while the contributions of the other species are bounded from below by a constant $-C$ independent of $L$, since their coordinates lie in a fixed ball. By symmetry, the half-ball $\{\tau^{(s_*)}:|\tau^{(s_*)}|\leqslant L/2,\ h^{s_*}\sum_{j\in\mathsf M_{s_*}}\tau_j\geqslant0\}$ has volume at least $cL^{M_{s_*}}$ for some $c>0$ (if $h^{s_*}=0$, it is the whole ball). Restricting the integral in~\eqref{e.escape_deterministic_lower_bound} to $A_L$, we obtain
\begin{equation*}
    \mathbb{E}\log Z^{\pi,\mathfrak{R}}_{M,L,b}\geqslant-\frac M2\log(2\pi)-C+\log\left(cL^{M_{s_*}}\prod_{u\ne s_*}|\mathcal B_1(\mathbb{R}^{M_u})|\right)\xrightarrow[L\to\infty]{}+\infty,
\end{equation*}
where $|\mathcal B_1(\mathbb{R}^{M_u})|$ is the volume of the unit ball. The statement for $\mathcal D_{M,L}(\pi,b)$ follows from~\eqref{e.direct_canonical}, since the remaining terms do not depend on $L$.
<!-- end proof-30 -->
<!-- lemma-24: body_md -->
\label{l.finite_overlap_approx_spherical}
For every $L\geqslant1$ and $\varepsilon>0$, we have the following.
\begin{enumerate}
    \item \label{i.finite_approx_increment} There exist $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and a bounded continuous function $f_\varepsilon$ such that, uniformly over $x,y,q,b$,
    \begin{gather*}
        \mathbb{E}\log\frac{Z^{x,y,q,\boldsymbol{\gamma}}_{N,L,\mathsf X,b}}{Z_N^{\mathord{\sim},x,y,q}}
        \asymp_\varepsilon\mathbb{E}\left\langle f_\varepsilon\left(R_N^{\leqslant n},q(R_\alpha^{\leqslant n}),b\right)\right\rangle_N^{\mathord{\sim},x,y,q},
    \end{gather*}
    and, uniformly over $q\in Q$, $b\in B$, and $p\in\mathcal Q_{\infty,\leqslant\lambda}^{\mathscr{S}}$,
    \begin{gather*}
        \mathbb{E}\log Z^{q+t\nabla\xi(p),\mathfrak{R}}_{M,L,b}
        \asymp_\varepsilon\mathbb{E}\left\langle f_\varepsilon\left(p(R_\alpha^{\leqslant n}),q(R_\alpha^{\leqslant n}),b\right)\right\rangle_{\mathfrak{R}}.
    \end{gather*}

    \item \label{i.finite_approx_cavity_array} Let $m\geqslant1$ and let $G:(\mathbb{R}^{\mathscr{S}}\times[0,1])^{m\times m}\to\mathbb{R}$ be bounded and continuous. There exist $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and a bounded continuous function $f_\varepsilon^G$ such that, uniformly over $x,y,q,b$,
    \begin{equation*}
        \mathbb{E}\left\langle G\left(\left(\widetilde R_M(\tau^\ell,\tau^{\ell'}),R_\alpha^{\ell,\ell'}\right)_{\ell,\ell'\leqslant m}\right)\right\rangle^{x,y,q,\boldsymbol{\gamma}}_{N,L,\mathsf X,b}
        \asymp_\varepsilon\mathbb{E}\left\langle f_\varepsilon^G\left(R_N^{\leqslant n},R_\alpha^{\leqslant n},q(R_\alpha^{\leqslant n}),b\right)\right\rangle_N^{\mathord{\sim},x,y,q},
    \end{equation*}
    and, uniformly over $q\in Q$, $b\in B$, and $p\in\mathcal Q_{\infty,\leqslant\lambda}^{\mathscr{S}}$,
    \begin{equation*}
        \mathbb{E}\left\langle G\left(\left(\widetilde R_M(\tau^\ell,\tau^{\ell'}),R_\alpha^{\ell,\ell'}\right)_{\ell,\ell'\leqslant m}\right)\right\rangle^{q+t\nabla\xi(p),\mathfrak{R}}_{M,L,b}
        \asymp_\varepsilon\mathbb{E}\left\langle f_\varepsilon^G\left(p(R_\alpha^{\leqslant n}),R_\alpha^{\leqslant n},q(R_\alpha^{\leqslant n}),b\right)\right\rangle_{\mathfrak{R}}.
    \end{equation*}

    \item \label{i.finite_approx_reaction} For every $N\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\mathsf y_N$ be a centered Gaussian field on $\Sigma_N$, independent of the other Gaussian fields, with covariance $\mathbb{E}\mathsf y_N(\sigma)\mathsf y_N(\sigma')=\theta(R_N(\sigma,\sigma'))$. There exist $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and a bounded continuous function $f_\varepsilon^{\mathcal I}$ such that, uniformly over $x,y,q$,
    \begin{equation*}
        \mathbb{E}\log\left\langle\exp\left(\sqrt{2tM}\,\mathsf y_N(\sigma)-tM\theta(\lambda)\right)\right\rangle_N^{\mathord{\sim},x,y,q}
        \asymp_\varepsilon\mathbb{E}\left\langle f_\varepsilon^{\mathcal I}(R_N^{\leqslant n})\right\rangle_N^{\mathord{\sim},x,y,q},
    \end{equation*}
    and, uniformly over $p\in\mathcal Q_{\infty,\leqslant\lambda}^{\mathscr{S}}$,
    \begin{equation*}
        \mathcal I_{M,t}(p)\asymp_\varepsilon\mathbb{E}\left\langle f_\varepsilon^{\mathcal I}\left(p(R_\alpha^{\leqslant n})\right)\right\rangle_{\mathfrak{R}}.
    \end{equation*}
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-24 -->
<!-- proof-31: body_md -->
The quantities on the left-hand sides are of the form considered in~\cite[Lemmas~6.6 and~6.7]{chen2025free}, and the statements follow from~\cite[Proposition~4.4]{chen2025free} as explained there. We only indicate how the arguments of the approximating functions arise. In the Gaussian model, the covariance of the cavity fields between two bulk replicas is $2t\partial_s\xi(R_N^{\ell,\ell'})+2q^s(R_\alpha^{\ell,\ell'})$, while in the canonical block with path $q+t\nabla\xi(p)$ it is $2t\partial_s\xi(p(R_\alpha^{\ell,\ell'}))+2q^s(R_\alpha^{\ell,\ell'})$: these are the same continuous function of $(R^{\ell,\ell'}_N,q(R_\alpha^{\ell,\ell'}))$, respectively of $(p(R_\alpha^{\ell,\ell'}),q(R_\alpha^{\ell,\ell'}))$. Since $\nabla\xi$ is continuous, the dependence on the overlaps can be absorbed into the approximating functions, but the path $q$ need not be continuous, so $q(R^{\leqslant n}_\alpha)$ is kept as an argument. In part~\eqref{i.finite_approx_cavity_array}, the function $G$ depends explicitly on $R^{\ell,\ell'}_\alpha$, which therefore remains a separate argument; in general, it cannot be recovered from $q(R_\alpha^{\leqslant n})$ when $q$ is constant on an interval. Part~\eqref{i.finite_approx_reaction} is the same argument applied to the scalar covariance $\theta(R_N^{\ell,\ell'})$, respectively $\theta(p(R_\alpha^{\ell,\ell'}))$. Since $L$ is fixed, the cavity coordinates range over a compact set, and the boundedness of $Q$, $B$, and of the overlaps make the approximations uniform in the stated parameters.
<!-- end proof-31 -->
<!-- lemma-25: body_md -->
\label{l.true_cavity_radius_ui}
For every integer $k\geqslant1$, there exists a constant $C_k<\infty$, depending only on $k$, such that, for every $s\in\mathscr{S}$,
\begin{gather*}
    \sup_N\sup_{x,y,q}\mathbb{E}\left\langle|\tau^{(s)}|^{2k}\right\rangle_{N+M}^{x,y,q}\leqslant C_kM_s^k,
    \\
    \text{and consequently}\qquad
    \lim_{a\to\infty}\sup_N\sup_{x,y,q}\mathbb{E}\left\langle\frac{|\tau^{(s)}|^2}{M_s}\mathds{1}_{\{|\tau^{(s)}|^2>aM_s\}}\right\rangle_{N+M}^{x,y,q}=0.
\end{gather*}
<!-- end lemma-25 -->
<!-- proof-32: body_md -->
Let $(e_i)_{i\leqslant N+M}$ be the standard basis of $\mathbb{R}^{N+M}$. For each $s'\in\mathscr{S}$, let $\mathsf O_{N,s'}$ be the compact group of orthogonal transformations of $\mathbb{R}^{I_{N+M,s'}}$ which fix the vector $\sum_{i\in I_{N+M,s'}}e_i$, and let $\mathsf O_N:=\prod_{s'\in\mathscr{S}}\mathsf O_{N,s'}$ act on $\mathbb{R}^{N+M}$ blockwise. The reference measure $P_{N+M}$ is invariant under $\mathsf O_N$. Every $U\in\mathsf O_N$ preserves the species overlaps and the sums $\sum_{i\in I_{N+M,s'}}\rho_i$, and commutes with the dilations~$S_r$. By~\eqref{e.mean_perturbed_H} and~\eqref{e.covariance_perturbed_H}, the law of the field $(H_{N+M}^{x,y,q}(U\rho,\alpha))_{\rho,\alpha}$ is therefore the same as that of $(H_{N+M}^{x,y,q}(\rho,\alpha))_{\rho,\alpha}$. It follows that, for every bounded Borel function $F$ on $\Sigma_{N+M}$,
\begin{equation}
    \mathbb{E}\left\langle F(\rho)\right\rangle_{N+M}^{x,y,q}=\mathbb{E}\left\langle\int_{\mathsf O_N}F(U\rho)\,\mathrm{d} U\right\rangle_{N+M}^{x,y,q},
    \label{e.residual_rotation_average}
\end{equation}
where $\mathrm{d} U$ denotes the Haar probability measure. We are thus reduced to a deterministic estimate on the average over $\mathsf O_{N,s}$.

Set $n_s:=|I_{N+M,s}|=N_s+M_s$ and $\vec{\mathbf{1}}_s:=\sum_{i\in I_{N+M,s}}e_i$. Let $u\in\mathbb{R}^{I_{N+M,s}}$ with $|u|^2=n_s$, and write
\begin{equation*}
    u=m\vec{\mathbf{1}}_s+v,
    \qquad
    m:=\frac1{n_s}\sum_{i\in I_{N+M,s}}u_i,
    \qquad
    v\perp\vec{\mathbf{1}}_s,
\end{equation*}
so that $n_sm^2+|v|^2=n_s$; in particular, $|m|\leqslant1$ and $|v|^2=n_s(1-m^2)$. Every $U\in\mathsf O_{N,s}$ fixes $\vec{\mathbf{1}}_s$, so that $(Uu)_i=m+(Uv)_i$ for every $i\in I_{N+M,s}$. If $n_s=1$, then $\mathsf O_{N,s}$ is trivial, $v=0$, and $|(Uu)_i|=1$. Assume now that $n_s\geqslant2$, and fix $i\in I_{N+M,s}$. Under the Haar measure on $\mathsf O_{N,s}$, the vector $Uv$ is uniform on the sphere of radius $|v|$ in the hyperplane $\vec{\mathbf{1}}_s^\perp$, whose dimension is $d:=n_s-1$, and $(Uv)_i$ is the scalar product of $Uv$ with the orthogonal projection of $e_i$ onto $\vec{\mathbf{1}}_s^\perp$, which has squared norm $1-n_s^{-1}=d/n_s$. If $Z$ is uniform on the unit sphere of $\mathbb{R}^d$, then $\mathbb{E} Z_1^{2k}=(2k-1)!!\prod_{j=0}^{k-1}(d+2j)^{-1}$: writing $Z=g/|g|$ with $g$ a standard Gaussian vector in $\mathbb{R}^d$, and using the independence of $|g|$ and $g/|g|$, we get $\mathbb{E} g_1^{2k}=\mathbb{E}|g|^{2k}\,\mathbb{E} Z_1^{2k}$, with $\mathbb{E} g_1^{2k}=(2k-1)!!$ and $\mathbb{E}|g|^{2k}=\prod_{j=0}^{k-1}(d+2j)$. Hence
\begin{equation*}
    \int_{\mathsf O_{N,s}}(Uv)_i^{2k}\,\mathrm{d} U
    =(2k-1)!!\,\left(\frac{d}{n_s}\right)^k|v|^{2k}\prod_{j=0}^{k-1}\frac1{d+2j}
    =(2k-1)!!\,(1-m^2)^k\prod_{j=0}^{k-1}\frac{d}{d+2j}
    \leqslant(2k-1)!!,
\end{equation*}
and, since $|m+w|^{2k}\leqslant2^{2k-1}(m^{2k}+w^{2k})$ and $|m|\leqslant1$,
\begin{equation}
    \sup_N\ \sup_{u\in\mathbb{R}^{I_{N+M,s}}:\:|u|^2=n_s}\ \max_{i\in I_{N+M,s}}\int_{\mathsf O_{N,s}}|(Uu)_i|^{2k}\,\mathrm{d} U
    \leqslant2^{2k-1}\left(1+(2k-1)!!\right)=:C_k,
    \label{e.deterministic_orbit_moment_bound}
\end{equation}
which also covers the case $n_s=1$. Fix $j\in\mathsf M_s$, so that $N+j\in I_{N+M,s}$ by~\eqref{e.N_compatible_block}, and let $F(\rho):=\rho_{N+j}^{2k}=\tau_j^{2k}$, which is bounded on $\Sigma_{N+M}$. For $\rho\in\Sigma_{N+M}$, we have $|\rho^{(s)}|^2=n_s$, and $F(U\rho)$ depends only on the component of $U$ in $\mathsf O_{N,s}$, so that~\eqref{e.deterministic_orbit_moment_bound}, applied with $u:=\rho^{(s)}$ and $i:=N+j$, gives $\int_{\mathsf O_N}F(U\rho)\,\mathrm{d} U\leqslant C_k$. By~\eqref{e.residual_rotation_average}, we obtain $\mathbb{E}\left\langle\tau_j^{2k}\right\rangle_{N+M}^{x,y,q}\leqslant C_k$ for every $j\in\mathsf M_s$. By Jensen's inequality, $|\tau^{(s)}|^{2k}=(\sum_{j\in\mathsf M_s}\tau_j^2)^k\leqslant M_s^{k-1}\sum_{j\in\mathsf M_s}\tau_j^{2k}$, and summing the previous bound over $j\in\mathsf M_s$ gives the moment bound. The second assertion follows from the case $k=2$: since $u\mathds{1}_{\{u>a\}}\leqslant u^2/a$ for $u\geqslant0$, the quantity under the limit is at most $C_2/a$.
<!-- end proof-32 -->
<!-- lemma-26: body_md -->
\label{l.remove_cutoffs}
For every $n\in\mathbb{N}$, there exists $C_n<\infty$ such that the following holds.
\begin{enumerate}
    \item \label{i.remove_cutoff_true} For every bounded measurable function $f$ of $n$ replicas of $(\tau,\alpha)$, and every $L\geqslant1$,
    \begin{equation*}
        \sup_N\sup_{x,y,q}\left|\mathbb{E}\left\langle f\right\rangle_{N+M,L}^{x,y,q}-\mathbb{E}\left\langle f\right\rangle_{N+M}^{x,y,q}\right|\leqslant C_n\|f\|_\infty\frac{M}{L^2}.
    \end{equation*}
    \item \label{i.remove_cutoff_canonical} Let $\pi\in\mathcal Q_\infty^{\mathscr{S}}$ and let $b$ be admissible for $\pi$. The quantity $Z^{\pi,\mathfrak{R}}_{M,b}$ is almost surely finite with integrable logarithm, and for every bounded measurable function $f$ of $n$ replicas of $(\tau,\alpha)$,
    \begin{gather*}
        \lim_{L\to\infty}\left|\mathbb{E}\left\langle f\right\rangle^{\pi,\mathfrak{R}}_{M,L,b}-\mathbb{E}\left\langle f\right\rangle^{\pi,\mathfrak{R}}_{M,b}\right|=0
        \qquad\text{and}\qquad
        \lim_{L\to\infty}\mathcal D_{M,L}(\pi,b)=\mathcal D_M(\pi,b).
    \end{gather*}
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-26 -->
<!-- proof-33: body_md -->
We first record an estimate valid for both brackets. Let $\left\langle\cdot\right\rangle$ be a Gibbs bracket without cutoff, let $\mu$ be the corresponding one-replica Gibbs measure, and let $\left\langle\cdot\right\rangle_L$ be the bracket obtained by inserting the factor $\chi_L(\tau^\ell)$ for each replica $\ell\leqslant n$.
