Setting $c_L:=\left\langle\chi_L(\tau)\right\rangle\in(0,1]$ and $u_L:=1-c_L$, the bracket $\left\langle\cdot\right\rangle_L$ is the $n$-fold tensor power of the probability measure $\mu_L$ with density $\chi_L/c_L$ with respect to $\mu$. Since $0\leqslant\chi_L\leqslant1$, the measure $\mu-c_L\mu_L$ is nonnegative with total mass $u_L$, so that $\mu=c_L\mu_L+u_L\nu_L$ for some probability measure $\nu_L$ (when $u_L=0$, we have $\mu=\mu_L$). Expanding the $n$-fold tensor power of this decomposition, we find $\mu^{\otimes n}=c_L^n\mu_L^{\otimes n}+(1-c_L^n)\nu'$ for some probability measure $\nu'$. Hence, for every bounded measurable $f$ of $n$ replicas,
\begin{equation*}
    \left|\left\langle f\right\rangle-\left\langle f\right\rangle_L\right|=(1-c_L^n)\left|\nu'(f)-\left\langle f\right\rangle_L\right|\leqslant2\|f\|_\infty(1-c_L^n)\leqslant2n\|f\|_\infty u_L,
\end{equation*}
where we used that $1-c^n\leqslant n(1-c)$ for $c\in[0,1]$. Taking expectations, we obtain, with $C_n:=2n$,
\begin{equation}\label{e.|E<G>_L-E<G>|<}
    \left|\mathbb{E}\left\langle f\right\rangle_L-\mathbb{E}\left\langle f\right\rangle\right|\leqslant C_n\|f\|_\infty\,\mathbb{E} u_L.
\end{equation}

For part~\eqref{i.remove_cutoff_true}, we apply this to $\left\langle\cdot\right\rangle^{x,y,q}_{N+M}$. By~\eqref{e.chi_L_def}, Chebyshev's inequality, and~\eqref{e.true_block_second_moment},
\begin{align*}
    \mathbb{E} u_L
    \leqslant\mathbb{E}\left\langle\mathds{1}_{\{|\tau|>L\}}\right\rangle_{N+M}^{x,y,q}\leqslant\frac1{L^2}\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}\mathbb{E}\left\langle|\tau^{(s)}|^2\right\rangle_{N+M}^{x,y,q}=\frac{M}{L^2}.
\end{align*}

For part~\eqref{i.remove_cutoff_canonical}, we first verify the integrability statements. By~\eqref{e.canonical_additivity} and Lemma~\ref{l.scalar_initial_continuous_derivative}, the quantity $\mathbb{E}\log Z^{\pi,\mathfrak{R}}_{M,b}$ is finite when $b$ is admissible; in particular $Z^{\pi,\mathfrak{R}}_{M,b}<\infty$ almost surely. We also need a lower bound on $\log Z^{\pi,\mathfrak{R}}_{M,1,b}$. Let $\nu$ be the probability measure obtained by normalizing the restriction of $\boldsymbol{\gamma}_M$ to the unit ball $\mathcal B_1$ of $\mathbb{R}^M$. Since $\chi_1=1$ on $\mathcal B_1$, Jensen's inequality gives
\begin{align*}
    \log Z^{\pi,\mathfrak{R}}_{M,1,b}
    &\geqslant\log\boldsymbol{\gamma}_M(\mathcal B_1)+\iint_{\mathcal B_1\times\mathfrak U}U_{\pi,b}(\tau,\alpha)\,\nu(\mathrm{d}\tau)\,\mathfrak{R}(\mathrm{d}\alpha)\\
    &=\log\boldsymbol{\gamma}_M(\mathcal B_1)-\frac12\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}\sum_{j\in\mathsf M_s}(b^s-1)\int_{\mathcal B_1}\tau_j^2\,\nu(\mathrm{d}\tau),
\end{align*}
where the terms linear in $\tau$ vanish because $\nu$ is symmetric. Since $Z^{\pi,\mathfrak{R}}_{M,1,b}\leqslant Z^{\pi,\mathfrak{R}}_{M,L,b}\leqslant Z^{\pi,\mathfrak{R}}_{M,b}$, both $\log Z^{\pi,\mathfrak{R}}_{M,1,b}$ and $\log Z^{\pi,\mathfrak{R}}_{M,b}$ are integrable, and by the monotonicity in~\eqref{e.chi_L_def}, $\log Z^{\pi,\mathfrak{R}}_{M,L,b}$ increases to $\log Z^{\pi,\mathfrak{R}}_{M,b}$ as $L\to\infty$. Monotone convergence gives $\lim_{L\to\infty}\mathbb{E}\log Z^{\pi,\mathfrak{R}}_{M,L,b}=\mathbb{E}\log Z^{\pi,\mathfrak{R}}_{M,b}$, hence the convergence of $\mathcal D_{M,L}(\pi,b)$ by~\eqref{e.direct_canonical}. Finally, since $Z^{\pi,\mathfrak{R}}_{M,b}$ is almost surely finite, dominated convergence gives $u_L=1-\left\langle\chi_L(\tau)\right\rangle^{\pi,\mathfrak{R}}_{M,b}\to0$ almost surely, hence $\mathbb{E} u_L\to0$, and~\eqref{e.|E<G>_L-E<G>|<} concludes the proof.
<!-- end proof-33 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{t.spherical_cavity_lim}
Fix $t>0$ and $q\in\mathcal Q_\infty^{\mathscr{S}}$. Let $(N_k,x_k,y_k,q_k)_{k\geqslant1}$ be a sequence such that $N_k\in M\mathbb{N}$ tends to infinity, $x_k\in[0,3]^{\mathbb{N}^4}$, $y_k\in[0,3]^{\mathscr{S}}$, and $q_k\in\mathcal Q_\infty^{\mathscr{S}}$ satisfies
\begin{align}
    \sup_k|q_k|_{L^\infty}<\infty,\qquad \lim_{k\to\infty}q_k(r)=q(r)\quad\text{for a.e.\ }r\in[0,1],\qquad\lim_{k\to\infty}q_k(1)=q(1).
    \label{e.cavity_theorem_path_convergence}
\end{align}
Assume that
\begin{equation}
    \lim_{k\to\infty}\Delta_{N_k}(x_k,y_k,q_k)=0\qquad\text{and}\qquad \lim_{k\to\infty}\operatorname{Rad}_{N_k,L}(x_k,y_k,q_k)=0\quad\text{for every }L\in\mathbb{N}.
    \label{e.cavity_assumptions_delta}
\end{equation}
Then there exist a subsequence, which we still denote by $(N_k,x_k,y_k,q_k)_{k\geqslant1}$, a path $p\in\mathcal Q_{\infty,\leqslant\lambda}^{\mathscr{S}}$, and a vector $b\in\mathbb{R}^{\mathscr{S}}$ admissible for $\pi:=q+t\nabla\xi(p)$, such that the following holds.
\begin{enumerate}
    \item\label{i.cav_overlaps}
    \emph{Synchronization of the bulk overlaps.} For every $n\in\mathbb{N}$, the array $(R^{\leqslant n}_{N_k}, R^{\leqslant n}_\alpha)$ under $\mathbb{E}\left\langle\cdot\right\rangle_{N_k}^{\mathord{\sim},x_k,y_k,q_k}$ converges in law, as $k\to\infty$, to
    \begin{align}
        \left(\left(p(R^{\ell,\ell'}_\alpha),R^{\ell,\ell'}_\alpha\right)\mathds{1}_{\{\ell\neq\ell'\}}+\left(\lambda,1\right)\mathds{1}_{\{\ell=\ell'\}}\right)_{1\leqslant \ell,\ell'\leqslant n}
        \qquad\text{under $\mathbb{E}\left\langle\cdot\right\rangle_\mathfrak{R}$.}
        \label{e.overlap_limit_statement}
    \end{align}

    \item\label{i.cav_marginal}
    \emph{Convergence of the cavity coordinates.} For every $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and every continuous function $g:(\mathbb{R}^{\mathscr{S}}\times[0,1])^{n\times n}\to\mathbb{R}$ such that $|g((a^{\ell,\ell'},r^{\ell,\ell'})_{\ell,\ell'\leqslant n})|\leqslant C(1+\sum_{\ell,\ell'\leqslant n}|a^{\ell,\ell'}|^d)$ for some $C<\infty$ and $d\in\mathbb{N}$, we have, with $\tau$ as in~\eqref{e.tau=},
    \begin{align}
        \lim_{k\to\infty}
        \mathbb{E}\left\langle g\left(\left(\widetilde R_M(\tau^\ell,\tau^{\ell'}),\alpha^\ell\wedge\alpha^{\ell'}\right)_{\ell,\ell'\leqslant n}\right)\right\rangle_{N_k+M}^{x_k,y_k,q_k}
        =\mathbb{E}\left\langle g\left(\left(\widetilde R_M(\tau^\ell,\tau^{\ell'}),\alpha^\ell\wedge\alpha^{\ell'}\right)_{\ell,\ell'\leqslant n}\right)\right\rangle^{\pi,\mathfrak{R}}_{M,b}.
        \label{e.cavity_marginal_limit}
    \end{align}
    The arrays include their diagonal entries, so that~\eqref{e.cavity_marginal_limit} covers in particular the one-replica second moments $|\tau^{(s)}|^2=M\widetilde R_{M,s}(\tau,\tau)$.

    \item\label{i.cav_normalization}
    \emph{Spherical normalization.} The canonical block satisfies
    \begin{equation}
        \mathbb{E}\left\langle|\tau^{(s)}|^2\right\rangle^{\pi,\mathfrak{R}}_{M,b}=M_s\qquad\text{for every }s\in\mathscr{S},
        \label{e.cavity_canonical_normalization}
    \end{equation}
    and consequently $b=b_\pi$.

    \item\label{i.cav_increment}
    \emph{The cavity increment.} We have
    \begin{equation}
        \liminf_{k\to\infty}A_{N_k}(x_k,y_k,q_k)\geqslant\mathcal P_{M,t,q}(p,b)=-M\mathscr{P}_{t,q}(p).
        \label{e.cavity_increment_lower_bound}
    \end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- proof-34: body_md -->
Throughout the proof, we write $\vartheta_k^s:=q_k^s(1)+t\partial_s\xi(\lambda)$ for the coefficient in~\eqref{e.prelimit_vartheta_def} associated with $q_k$, and $\vartheta^s:=q^s(1)+t\partial_s\xi(\lambda)$; by~\eqref{e.cavity_theorem_path_convergence}, $\vartheta_k\to\vartheta$.

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{Part 1: Convergence of the overlap array and choice of $b$.}\par
The arrays $(R_{N_k}^{\ell,\ell'},R_\alpha^{\ell,\ell'})_{\ell,\ell'\geqslant1}$ are uniformly bounded. After passing to a subsequence, they converge in finite-dimensional distributions under $\mathbb{E}\left\langle\cdot\right\rangle_{N_k}^{\mathord{\sim},x_k,y_k,q_k}$ to an array $(R_\infty^{\ell,\ell'},R_{\alpha,\infty}^{\ell,\ell'})_{\ell,\ell'\geqslant1}$; we denote by $\mathbf{E}$ the expectation under the law of the limiting array. The diagonal is deterministic, since $R_{N_k}^{\ell,\ell}=\lambda$ by~\eqref{e.lambda_N_equals_lambda} and $R_\alpha^{\ell,\ell}=1$.

We next identify the off-diagonal entries. Since every term in~\eqref{e.Delta_MN_def} is nonnegative, the first limit in~\eqref{e.cavity_assumptions_delta} gives $\lim_{k\to\infty}\Delta_{N_k}^{x_k,y_k,q_k}(\mathbf{f}_j,n_j,\mathsf h_j)=0$ for every $j\in\mathbb{N}$. The linear span of the constants and of the monomials $\mathbf{f}_j$ is dense among the continuous functions of finitely many entries of the bounded overlap array, and, by polarization, the linear span of the constants and of the functions $(v,u)\mapsto\mathsf C_{\mathsf h}(v,u)$, $\mathsf h\in\mathbb{N}^4$, is dense among the continuous functions on the overlap domain. Passing to the limit in~\eqref{e.Delta_r_def}, we obtain
\begin{align*}
    \mathbf{E}\left[ \mathbf{f}(\cdots)\varphi\left(R_\infty^{1,n+1},R_{\alpha,\infty}^{1,n+1}\right)\right]
    =\frac1n\mathbf{E} \left[\mathbf{f}(\cdots)\right]\mathbf{E}\left[\varphi\left(R_\infty^{1,2},R_{\alpha,\infty}^{1,2}\right)\right]+\frac1n\sum_{\ell=2}^n\mathbf{E} \left[\mathbf{f}(\cdots)\varphi\left(R_\infty^{1,\ell},R_{\alpha,\infty}^{1,\ell}\right)\right]
\end{align*}
for every $n\geqslant2$, every bounded continuous function $\mathbf{f}$ of $((R^{\ell,\ell'}_\infty, R^{\ell,\ell'}_{\alpha,\infty}))_{\ell,\ell'\leqslant n}$, abbreviated as $\mathbf{f}(\cdots)$, and every bounded continuous function $\varphi$. In other words, the limiting array satisfies the Ghirlanda--Guerra identities. To identify it, set
\begin{equation*}
    T^{\ell,\ell'}:=\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}R_{\infty,s}^{\ell,\ell'}+R_{\alpha,\infty}^{\ell,\ell'},
\end{equation*}
where $R_{\infty,s}^{\ell,\ell'}$ is the $s$-component of $R_\infty^{\ell,\ell'}$. The entries of $R_\infty$ are nonnegative, by Talagrand's positivity principle applied to each species array, see~\cite[Theorem~2.16]{pan} and~\cite[Section~4]{pan.multi}, so that $T$ takes values in $[0,2]$. The synchronization theorem~\cite[Theorem~4]{pan.multi} gives a Lipschitz, coordinatewise nondecreasing function $\Psi=(\Psi_{\mathscr{S}},\Psi_\alpha):[0,2]\to\mathbb{R}_+^{\mathscr{S}}\times[0,1]$ such that
\begin{equation*}
    \left(R_\infty^{\ell,\ell'},R_{\alpha,\infty}^{\ell,\ell'}\right)=\Psi(T^{\ell,\ell'})\qquad\text{almost surely, for every }\ell,\ell'.
\end{equation*}
The scalar array $(T^{\ell,\ell'})_{\ell,\ell'\geqslant1}$ has diagonal $2$, because $\sum_s\lambda_s=1$. We identify the limiting array by inverting $\Psi_\alpha$. For $r\in[0,1)$, set
\begin{equation*}
    \boldsymbol{\kappa}(r):=\inf\left\{v\in[0,2]:\Psi_\alpha(v)>r\right\}.
\end{equation*}
Fix $\ell\ne\ell'$, and let $U:=R_{\alpha,\infty}^{\ell,\ell'}=\Psi_\alpha(T^{\ell,\ell'})$. By the invariance~\eqref{e.invariance_cascade}, the overlap $\alpha^\ell\wedge\alpha^{\ell'}$ is uniformly distributed on $[0,1]$ under $\mathbb{E}\left\langle\cdot\right\rangle^{\mathord{\sim},x_k,y_k,q_k}_{N_k}$ for every $k$, hence so is $U$. In particular, for every $r\in[0,1)$, the event $\{\Psi_\alpha(T^{\ell,\ell'})>r\}$ has probability $1-r>0$, so that the set in the definition of $\boldsymbol{\kappa}(r)$ is nonempty, and $\boldsymbol{\kappa}$ is a nondecreasing function from $[0,1)$ to $[0,2]$. It is right-continuous, since the sets $\{v\in[0,2]:\Psi_\alpha(v)>r'\}$ increase to $\{v\in[0,2]:\Psi_\alpha(v)>r\}$ as $r'\downarrow r$. Since $\Psi_\alpha$ is nondecreasing, each level set $\Psi_\alpha^{-1}(\{r\})$ is an interval, and the level sets containing more than one point have pairwise disjoint nonempty interiors; hence the set $E$ of those $r\in[0,1]$ for which $\Psi_\alpha^{-1}(\{r\})$ contains more than one point is countable. Let $r\in[0,1)\setminus E$ and $v\in[0,2]$ be such that $\Psi_\alpha(v)=r$. For $v'<v$, we have $\Psi_\alpha(v')\leqslant r$, while for $v'>v$, we have $\Psi_\alpha(v')\geqslant r$ and $\Psi_\alpha(v')\ne r$, since the level set of $r$ is reduced to $\{v\}$. The set in the definition of $\boldsymbol{\kappa}(r)$ is therefore $(v,2]$, which is nonempty, so that $v<2$ and $\boldsymbol{\kappa}(r)=v$. Since $U$ is uniformly distributed and $E\cup\{1\}$ is countable, we have $U\notin E\cup\{1\}$ almost surely, and applying the previous observation with $v=T^{\ell,\ell'}$ and $r=U$ gives
\begin{equation*}
    T^{\ell,\ell'}=\boldsymbol{\kappa}\left(R_{\alpha,\infty}^{\ell,\ell'}\right)\qquad\text{almost surely, for every }\ell\ne\ell'.
\end{equation*}
Set $p:=\Psi_{\mathscr{S}}\circ\boldsymbol{\kappa}$ on $[0,1)$. Since $\Psi_{\mathscr{S}}$ is continuous and coordinatewise nondecreasing, with nonnegative values, and since $\boldsymbol{\kappa}$ is nondecreasing and right-continuous, the path $p$ is nondecreasing, right-continuous, bounded, and nonnegative, so that $p\in\mathcal Q_\infty^{\mathscr{S}}$, with the endpoint convention~\eqref{e.continuous_endpoint_convention}. Applying $\Psi_{\mathscr{S}}$ to the previous display, we obtain
\begin{equation}
    R_\infty^{\ell,\ell'}=p(R_{\alpha,\infty}^{\ell,\ell'}),
    \qquad \ell\ne\ell'.
    \label{e.cavity_limit_synchronization}
\end{equation}
For every $s\in\mathscr{S}$, the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality gives $R_{N_k,s}^{\ell,\ell'}\leqslant\lambda_{s}$, so that $p^s\leqslant\lambda_s$ almost everywhere, and then everywhere on $[0,1]$ by right-continuity and the endpoint convention. Hence $p\in\mathcal Q_{\infty,\leqslant\lambda}^{\mathscr{S}}$. Finally, the invariance~\eqref{e.invariance_cascade} identifies the joint law of the cascade overlaps, and not only the law of one overlap: for every $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and every $k$, the array $R_\alpha^{\leqslant n}$ has the same law under $\mathbb{E}\left\langle\cdot\right\rangle^{\mathord{\sim},x_k,y_k,q_k}_{N_k}$ as under $\mathbb{E}\left\langle\cdot\right\rangle_\mathfrak{R}$, hence so does the limiting array $(R_{\alpha,\infty}^{\ell,\ell'})_{\ell,\ell'\leqslant n}$. By~\eqref{e.cavity_limit_synchronization} and the deterministic diagonal, the limiting array $(R_\infty^{\ell,\ell'},R_{\alpha,\infty}^{\ell,\ell'})_{\ell,\ell'\leqslant n}$ is almost surely the image of $(R_{\alpha,\infty}^{\ell,\ell'})_{\ell,\ell'\leqslant n}$ under the map which applies $p$ entrywise off the diagonal and puts $(\lambda,1)$ on the diagonal, so its law is that of the array in~\eqref{e.overlap_limit_statement}. This proves part~\eqref{i.cav_overlaps}.

We now prepare the passage to the limit in the Gaussian model, which requires two additional ingredients. The first is a modification of $p$ near $r=1$, which allows us to represent the diagonal value $\lambda$ of the limiting array by a cascade path. For $m\geqslant2$, define
\begin{equation*}
    p_m(r):=
    \begin{cases}
        p(r),&0\leqslant r<1-m^{-1},\\
        \lambda,&1-m^{-1}\leqslant r\leqslant1.
    \end{cases}
\end{equation*}
Since $p\leqslant\lambda$, we have $p_m\in\mathcal Q_{\infty,\leqslant\lambda}^{\mathscr{S}}$, $p_m(1)=\lambda$, and $|p_m-p|_{L^1}\leqslant m^{-1}|\lambda-p|_{L^\infty}\to0$. Since the off-diagonal overlaps $\alpha^\ell\wedge\alpha^{\ell'}$ are uniformly distributed on $[0,1]$ under $\mathbb{E}\left\langle\cdot\right\rangle_\mathfrak{R}$ while the diagonal ones equal $1$, we have, for every $n\in\mathbb{N}$,
\begin{equation}
    \left(p_m(R_\alpha^{\ell,\ell'}),R_\alpha^{\ell,\ell'}\right)_{\ell,\ell'\leqslant n}
    \xrightarrow[m\to\infty]{\mathrm{law}}
    \left(\left(p(R_\alpha^{\ell,\ell'}),R_\alpha^{\ell,\ell'}\right)\mathds{1}_{\{\ell\ne\ell'\}}+\left(\lambda,1\right)\mathds{1}_{\{\ell=\ell'\}}\right)_{\ell,\ell'\leqslant n}
    \qquad\text{under }\mathbb{E}\left\langle\cdot\right\rangle_\mathfrak{R}.
    \label{e.cavity_terminal_array_approximation}
\end{equation}
The second ingredient is the inclusion of the paths $q_k$ in the convergence of part~\eqref{i.cav_overlaps}. For $\ell\ne\ell'$, the overlap $R_\alpha^{\ell,\ell'}$ is uniformly distributed on $[0,1]$ both under $\mathbb{E}\left\langle\cdot\right\rangle_\mathfrak{R}$ and, by the invariance~\eqref{e.invariance_cascade}, under $\mathbb{E}\left\langle\cdot\right\rangle_{N_k}^{\mathord{\sim},x_k,y_k,q_k}$. The uniform bound on the $q_k$ and the almost everywhere convergence in~\eqref{e.cavity_theorem_path_convergence} therefore give $\lim_k\mathbb{E}\left\langle|q_k(R_\alpha^{\ell,\ell'})-q(R_\alpha^{\ell,\ell'})|\right\rangle=0$ under both measures, while for $\ell=\ell'$ we use $q_k(1)\to q(1)$. Since $q$ has at most countably many discontinuities and the off-diagonal overlaps are uniform, the continuous mapping theorem applied to the convergence of part~\eqref{i.cav_overlaps} shows that, with
\begin{equation*}
    R_p^{\ell,\ell'}:=p(R_\alpha^{\ell,\ell'})\mathds{1}_{\{\ell\ne\ell'\}}+\lambda\mathds{1}_{\{\ell=\ell'\}},
\end{equation*}
we have, for every $n\in\mathbb{N}$,
\begin{equation}
    \left(R_{N_k}^{\leqslant n},R_\alpha^{\leqslant n},q_k(R_\alpha^{\leqslant n})\right)\ \text{under }\mathbb{E}\left\langle\cdot\right\rangle_{N_k}^{\mathord{\sim},x_k,y_k,q_k}
    \xrightarrow[k\to\infty]{\mathrm{law}}
    \left(R_p^{\leqslant n},R_\alpha^{\leqslant n},q(R_\alpha^{\leqslant n})\right)\ \text{under }\mathbb{E}\left\langle\cdot\right\rangle_\mathfrak{R}.
    \label{e.cavity_joint_array_convergence}
\end{equation}

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{Choice of $b$.}\par
By Lemma~\ref{l.fixed_tilt_uniform_bounds}, the vectors $e_{N_k}$ in~\eqref{e.e^N_s=}, computed with the parameters $(x_k,y_k,q_k)$, are bounded. Passing to a further subsequence, we may assume that $e_{N_k}\to e\in\mathbb{R}^{\mathscr{S}}$. By~\eqref{e.b_prelimit_def}, the vectors $b_{N_k}=\vec{\mathbf{1}}+e_{N_k}+2\vartheta_k$ then converge:
\begin{equation}
    \lim_{k\to\infty}b_{N_k}=\overline b:=\vec{\mathbf{1}}+e+2\vartheta.
    \label{e.cavity_prelimit_b_convergence}
\end{equation}
The vector $\overline b$ is the natural limit of the quadratic coefficients in the Gaussian model, whose cavity fields have the deterministic variance $2\vartheta^s$. In the canonical block with path $\pi=q+t\nabla\xi(p)$, however, the cascade fields have diagonal variance $\pi^s(1)=q^s(1)+t\partial_s\xi(p(1))$, which may be smaller than $\vartheta^s$ since $p(1)\leqslant\lambda$. We compensate for this difference in the quadratic coefficient, as explained in Subsection~\ref{s.diagonal_compensation}, and set
\begin{equation}
    \pi:=q+t\nabla\xi(p),
    \qquad
    \pi_m:=q+t\nabla\xi(p_m),
    \qquad
    b:=b(\pi,e)=\left(1+e^s+2\pi^s(1)\right)_{s\in\mathscr{S}},
    \label{e.cavity_b_def}
\end{equation}
with the notation~\eqref{e.b_pi_e_def}. By the nonnegativity of the coefficients in~\eqref{e.xi_power_series_def}, $\pi,\pi_m\in\mathcal Q_\infty^{\mathscr{S}}$, and by the Lipschitz continuity of $\nabla\xi$ on the overlap domain, $|\pi_m-\pi|_{L^1}\to0$ as $m\to\infty$. Moreover, $\pi_m(1)=q(1)+t\nabla\xi(\lambda)=\vartheta$, so that $\overline b=b(\pi_m,e)$ for every $m$. Lemma~\ref{l.diagonal_compensation} therefore gives, for every $L\geqslant1$ and every bounded continuous function $f$ of finitely many replicas of $(\tau,\alpha)$,
\begin{gather}
    \lim_{m\to\infty}\mathcal D_{M,L}(\pi_m,\overline b)=\mathcal D_{M,L}(\pi,b),
    \qquad
    \lim_{m\to\infty}\mathbb{E}\left\langle f\right\rangle_{M,L,\overline b}^{\pi_m,\mathfrak{R}}=\mathbb{E}\left\langle f\right\rangle_{M,L,b}^{\pi,\mathfrak{R}}.
    \label{e.cavity_compensated_path_continuity}
\end{gather}
This is the mechanism through which the diagonal value $\lambda$ of the limiting overlap array, which differs from $p(1)$, is transferred to the quadratic coefficient of the block. We also record that, by~\eqref{e.cavity_b_def},
\begin{equation}
    \frac12\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}M_se^s=\frac12\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}M_s(b^s-1)-\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}M_s\pi^s(1),
    \label{e.cavity_diagonal_compensation}
\end{equation}
which is the additive constant in the definition~\eqref{e.direct_canonical} of $\mathcal D_{M,L}(\pi,b)$.

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{Part 2: The limits at fixed cutoff.}\par
Fix $L\in\mathbb{N}$. We first consider the partition functions. By~\eqref{e.partition_chart_to_gaussian} and the second limit in~\eqref{e.cavity_assumptions_delta}, and after subtracting $\mathbb{E}\log Z^{\mathord{\sim},x_k,y_k,q_k}_{N_k}$ from both partition functions,
\begin{align}
    \lim_{k\to\infty}\Bigg(&\mathbb{E}\log\frac{Z^{x_k,y_k,q_k,\mathrm{ch}}_{N_k+M,L,\widetilde V}}{Z_{N_k}^{\mathord{\sim},x_k,y_k,q_k}}
    -\mathbb{E}\log\frac{Z^{x_k,y_k,q_k,\boldsymbol{\gamma}}_{N_k,L,\mathsf X,b_{N_k}}}{Z_{N_k}^{\mathord{\sim},x_k,y_k,q_k}}
    -\frac12\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}M_se_{N_k}^s
    \Bigg)=0.
    \label{e.cavity_chart_partition_reduction}
\end{align}
We compute the limit of the second term. Fix $\varepsilon>0$, and let $n$ and $f_\varepsilon$ be given by part~\eqref{i.finite_approx_increment} of Lemma~\ref{l.finite_overlap_approx_spherical}. For all sufficiently large $k$ and $m$, we have
\begin{align*}
    \mathbb{E}\log\frac{Z^{x_k,y_k,q_k,\boldsymbol{\gamma}}_{N_k,L,\mathsf X,b_{N_k}}}{Z_{N_k}^{\mathord{\sim},x_k,y_k,q_k}}
    &\stackrel{\text{L.\ref{l.finite_overlap_approx_spherical}\eqref{i.finite_approx_increment}}}{\asymp_\varepsilon}\mathbb{E}\left\langle f_\varepsilon\left(R_{N_k}^{\leqslant n},q_k(R_\alpha^{\leqslant n}),b_{N_k}\right)\right\rangle_{N_k}^{\mathord{\sim},x_k,y_k,q_k}\\
    &\stackrel{\eqref{e.cavity_joint_array_convergence},\eqref{e.cavity_prelimit_b_convergence}}{\asymp_\varepsilon}\mathbb{E}\left\langle f_\varepsilon\left(R_p^{\leqslant n},q(R_\alpha^{\leqslant n}),\overline b\right)\right\rangle_{\mathfrak{R}}\\
    &\stackrel{\eqref{e.cavity_terminal_array_approximation}}{\asymp_\varepsilon}\mathbb{E}\left\langle f_\varepsilon\left(p_m(R_\alpha^{\leqslant n}),q(R_\alpha^{\leqslant n}),\overline b\right)\right\rangle_{\mathfrak{R}}\stackrel{\text{L.\ref{l.finite_overlap_approx_spherical}\eqref{i.finite_approx_increment}}}{\asymp_\varepsilon}\mathbb{E}\log Z^{\pi_m,\mathfrak{R}}_{M,L,\overline b},
\end{align*}
where the second and third approximations use the continuity and boundedness of $f_\varepsilon$ together with the convergences in law. Letting $k\to\infty$, then $m\to\infty$ using the first limit in~\eqref{e.cavity_compensated_path_continuity} and the fact that the additive constant in~\eqref{e.direct_canonical} is the same for $(\pi_m,\overline b)$ and $(\pi,b)$, and finally $\varepsilon\downarrow0$, we obtain
\begin{equation*}
    \lim_{k\to\infty}
    \mathbb{E}\log\frac{Z^{x_k,y_k,q_k,\boldsymbol{\gamma}}_{N_k,L,\mathsf X,b_{N_k}}}{Z_{N_k}^{\mathord{\sim},x_k,y_k,q_k}}
    =\mathbb{E}\log Z^{\pi,\mathfrak{R}}_{M,L,b}.
\end{equation*}
Moreover, $\lim_ke_{N_k}=e$, so that, by~\eqref{e.cavity_diagonal_compensation} and the definition~\eqref{e.direct_canonical}, we conclude from~\eqref{e.cavity_chart_partition_reduction} that
\begin{equation}
    \lim_{k\to\infty}
    \mathbb{E}\log\frac{Z^{x_k,y_k,q_k,\mathrm{ch}}_{N_k+M,L,\widetilde V}}{Z_{N_k}^{\mathord{\sim},x_k,y_k,q_k}}
    =\mathcal D_{M,L}(\pi,b).
    \label{e.cavity_direct_term_limit}
\end{equation}

We next identify the reaction term. Under the coupling~\eqref{e.coupling_H_tildeH}, and by~\eqref{e.theta_N_def}, the Hamiltonians in~\eqref{e.radially_inserted_N_partition} and~\eqref{e.ZcircMN_def} satisfy $H_N^{x,q}+\widetilde V_N^{x,y,q}=\widetilde H^{x,y,q}_N+\sqrt{2tM}\,\widetilde Y_N-tM\theta_N(\lambda)$, so that
\begin{equation*}
    \mathbb{E}\log\frac{Z^{x,y,q}_{N,\widetilde V}}{Z_N^{\mathord{\sim},x,y,q}}
    =\mathbb{E}\log\left\langle\exp\left(\sqrt{2tM}\,\widetilde Y_N(\sigma)-tM\theta_N(\lambda)\right)\right\rangle_N^{\mathord{\sim},x,y,q}.
\end{equation*}
Let $\mathsf y_N$ be the field in part~\eqref{i.finite_approx_reaction} of Lemma~\ref{l.finite_overlap_approx_spherical}. Conditionally on the fields entering $\widetilde H^{x,y,q}_N$, the bracket $\left\langle\cdot\right\rangle^{\mathord{\sim},x,y,q}_N$ is a probability measure, and the fields $\widetilde Y_N$ and $\mathsf y_N$ are independent of it, with covariances $\theta_N(R_N(\sigma,\sigma'))$ and $\theta(R_N(\sigma,\sigma'))$. By~\eqref{e.cavity_reaction_kernel_limit} and Lemma~\ref{l.gaussian_comparison_covariance_norm},
\begin{align*}
    \lim_{N\to\infty}\sup_{x,y,q}\Bigg|{}&\mathbb{E}\log\left\langle\exp\left(\sqrt{2tM}\,\widetilde Y_N(\sigma)-tM\theta_N(\lambda)\right)\right\rangle_N^{\mathord{\sim},x,y,q}\\
    &-\mathbb{E}\log\left\langle\exp\left(\sqrt{2tM}\,\mathsf y_N(\sigma)-tM\theta(\lambda)\right)\right\rangle_N^{\mathord{\sim},x,y,q}\Bigg|=0.
\end{align*}
It therefore suffices to compute the limit of
\begin{equation*}
    B_k:=\mathbb{E}\log\left\langle\exp\left(\sqrt{2tM}\,\mathsf y_{N_k}(\sigma)-tM\theta(\lambda)\right)\right\rangle_{N_k}^{\mathord{\sim},x_k,y_k,q_k}.
\end{equation*}
Fix $\varepsilon>0$, and let $n$ and $f_\varepsilon^{\mathcal I}$ be given by part~\eqref{i.finite_approx_reaction} of Lemma~\ref{l.finite_overlap_approx_spherical}. For all sufficiently large $k$ and $m$,
\begin{align*}
    B_k&\stackrel{\text{L.\ref{l.finite_overlap_approx_spherical}\eqref{i.finite_approx_reaction}}}{\asymp_\varepsilon}\mathbb{E}\left\langle f_\varepsilon^{\mathcal I}(R_{N_k}^{\leqslant n})\right\rangle_{N_k}^{\mathord{\sim},x_k,y_k,q_k}\stackrel{\eqref{e.cavity_joint_array_convergence}}{\asymp_\varepsilon}\mathbb{E}\left\langle f_\varepsilon^{\mathcal I}(R_p^{\leqslant n})\right\rangle_{\mathfrak{R}}\\
    &\stackrel{\eqref{e.cavity_terminal_array_approximation}}{\asymp_\varepsilon}\mathbb{E}\left\langle f_\varepsilon^{\mathcal I}\left(p_m(R_\alpha^{\leqslant n})\right)\right\rangle_{\mathfrak{R}}\stackrel{\text{L.\ref{l.finite_overlap_approx_spherical}\eqref{i.finite_approx_reaction}}}{\asymp_\varepsilon}\mathcal I_{M,t}(p_m).
\end{align*}
By~\eqref{e.reaction_value}, the continuity of $\theta$, and the $L^1$ convergence of $p_m$ to $p$, we have $\lim_{m\to\infty}\mathcal I_{M,t}(p_m)=\mathcal I_{M,t}(p)$. Letting $k\to\infty$, then $m\to\infty$, and finally $\varepsilon\downarrow0$, we obtain
\begin{equation}
    \lim_{k\to\infty}
    \mathbb{E}\log\frac{Z^{x_k,y_k,q_k}_{N_k,\widetilde V}}{Z_{N_k}^{\mathord{\sim},x_k,y_k,q_k}}
    =\mathcal I_{M,t}(p).
    \label{e.cavity_reaction_term_limit}
\end{equation}

We finally consider the Gibbs averages, still at fixed cutoff $L$. Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let $g:(\mathbb{R}^{\mathscr{S}}\times[0,1])^{n\times n}\to\mathbb{R}$ be bounded and continuous, and write $G:=g((\widetilde R_M(\tau^\ell,\tau^{\ell'}),\alpha^\ell\wedge\alpha^{\ell'})_{\ell,\ell'\leqslant n})$, a bounded continuous function of $n$ replicas. By~\eqref{e.radial_insertion_observable_negligible}, \eqref{e.normalized_chart_to_gaussian}, and the second limit in~\eqref{e.cavity_assumptions_delta},
\begin{equation}
    \lim_{k\to\infty}\left(\mathbb{E}\left\langle G\right\rangle_{N_k+M,L}^{x_k,y_k,q_k}
    -\mathbb{E}\left\langle G\right\rangle_{N_k,L,\mathsf X,b_{N_k}}^{x_k,y_k,q_k,\boldsymbol{\gamma}}\right)=0.
    \label{e.cavity_observable_gaussian_reduction}
\end{equation}
Fix $\varepsilon>0$, and let $n'$ and $f_\varepsilon^G$ be given by part~\eqref{i.finite_approx_cavity_array} of Lemma~\ref{l.finite_overlap_approx_spherical}, applied with $m=n$ replicas of the cavity coordinates and $n'$ replicas of the bulk. For all sufficiently large $k$ and $m$,
\begin{align*}
    \mathbb{E}\left\langle G\right\rangle_{N_k,L,\mathsf X,b_{N_k}}^{x_k,y_k,q_k,\boldsymbol{\gamma}}
    &\stackrel{\text{L.\ref{l.finite_overlap_approx_spherical}\eqref{i.finite_approx_cavity_array}}}{\asymp_\varepsilon}\mathbb{E}\left\langle f_\varepsilon^G\left(R_{N_k}^{\leqslant n'},R_\alpha^{\leqslant n'},q_k(R_\alpha^{\leqslant n'}),b_{N_k}\right)\right\rangle_{N_k}^{\mathord{\sim},x_k,y_k,q_k}
    \\
    &\stackrel{\eqref{e.cavity_joint_array_convergence},\eqref{e.cavity_prelimit_b_convergence}}{\asymp_\varepsilon}\mathbb{E}\left\langle f_\varepsilon^G\left(R_p^{\leqslant n'},R_\alpha^{\leqslant n'},q(R_\alpha^{\leqslant n'}),\overline b\right)\right\rangle_{\mathfrak{R}}
    \\
    &\stackrel{\eqref{e.cavity_terminal_array_approximation}}{\asymp_\varepsilon}\mathbb{E}\left\langle f_\varepsilon^G\left(p_m(R_\alpha^{\leqslant n'}),R_\alpha^{\leqslant n'},q(R_\alpha^{\leqslant n'}),\overline b\right)\right\rangle_{\mathfrak{R}}
    \\
    &\stackrel{\text{L.\ref{l.finite_overlap_approx_spherical}\eqref{i.finite_approx_cavity_array}}}{\asymp_\varepsilon}\mathbb{E}\left\langle G\right\rangle_{M,L,\overline b}^{\pi_m,\mathfrak{R}}.
\end{align*}
Letting $k\to\infty$, then $m\to\infty$ using the second limit in~\eqref{e.cavity_compensated_path_continuity}, and finally $\varepsilon\downarrow0$, and combining with~\eqref{e.cavity_observable_gaussian_reduction}, we get
\begin{equation}
    \lim_{k\to\infty}\mathbb{E}\left\langle G\right\rangle_{N_k+M,L}^{x_k,y_k,q_k}
    =\mathbb{E}\left\langle G\right\rangle_{M,L,b}^{\pi,\mathfrak{R}}.
    \label{e.cavity_observable_fixed_cutoff_limit}
\end{equation}

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{Part 3: Admissibility of $b$.}\par
By~\eqref{e.radial_cutoff_increment_def}, the increment $A_{N,L}^{\mathrm{rad}}(x,y,q)$ is the difference of the two quantities whose limits are identified in~\eqref{e.cavity_direct_term_limit} and~\eqref{e.cavity_reaction_term_limit}. The one-sided comparison~\eqref{e.one_sided_increment} of Proposition~\ref{p.radial_insertion_harmless} therefore yields
\begin{equation}
    \liminf_{k\to\infty}A_{N_k}(x_k,y_k,q_k)
    \geqslant\mathcal D_{M,L}(\pi,b)-\mathcal I_{M,t}(p)
    \qquad\text{for every }L\in\mathbb{N}.
    \label{e.cavity_fixed_cutoff_increment_bound}
\end{equation}
By Lemma~\ref{l.fixed_block_increment_bound}, the left-hand side is finite, so that $\sup_{L\geqslant1}\mathcal D_{M,L}(\pi,b)<+\infty$. Lemma~\ref{l.multispecies_nonadmissible_escape} then shows that $b$ is admissible for $\pi$. This is what makes the untruncated block $\left\langle\cdot\right\rangle^{\pi,\mathfrak{R}}_{M,b}$ well defined, by Lemma~\ref{l.remove_cutoffs}.

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{Part 4: Removal of the cutoff.}\par
Since $b$ is admissible for $\pi$, Lemma~\ref{l.remove_cutoffs} allows us to let $L\to\infty$ on both sides of~\eqref{e.cavity_observable_fixed_cutoff_limit}, uniformly in $k$ on the left. This proves~\eqref{e.cavity_marginal_limit} for bounded continuous $g$.

We now remove the boundedness assumption on $g$. By hypothesis, there are $C<\infty$ and $d\in\mathbb{N}$ such that $|g((a^{\ell,\ell'},r^{\ell,\ell'})_{\ell,\ell'\leqslant n})|\leqslant C(1+\sum_{\ell,\ell'\leqslant n}|a^{\ell,\ell'}|^d)$. By the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality, $|\widetilde R_{M,s}(\tau^\ell,\tau^{\ell'})|\leqslant M^{-1}|\tau^{\ell,(s)}|\,|\tau^{\ell',(s)}|$, and the Gibbs average over the replicas of a product of functions of $\tau^\ell$ and $\tau^{\ell'}$ is bounded by the average of the square of either function, by the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality and the exchangeability of the replicas. Together with Jensen's inequality, the moment bounds of Lemma~\ref{l.true_cavity_radius_ui}, applied with an integer $k\geqslant d(1+\delta)$, therefore imply that, for every $\delta>0$,
\begin{equation}
    \sup_k\mathbb{E}\left\langle|G|^{1+\delta}\right\rangle_{N_k+M}^{x_k,y_k,q_k}<+\infty.
    \label{e.cavity_polynomial_uniform_integrability}
\end{equation}
For $C'>0$, the function $|g|^{1+\delta}\wedge C'$ is bounded and continuous, so the bounded case and~\eqref{e.cavity_polynomial_uniform_integrability} give
\begin{equation*}
    \mathbb{E}\left\langle |G|^{1+\delta}\wedge C'\right\rangle_{M,b}^{\pi,\mathfrak{R}}
    =\lim_{k\to\infty}\mathbb{E}\left\langle |G|^{1+\delta}\wedge C'\right\rangle_{N_k+M}^{x_k,y_k,q_k}
    \leqslant\sup_k\mathbb{E}\left\langle|G|^{1+\delta}\right\rangle_{N_k+M}^{x_k,y_k,q_k},
\end{equation*}
and monotone convergence as $C'\to\infty$ shows that $\mathbb{E}\left\langle |G|^{1+\delta}\right\rangle_{M,b}^{\pi,\mathfrak{R}}$ is finite. Let $T_{C'}(u):=(-C')\vee(u\wedge C')$. The bounded case gives~\eqref{e.cavity_marginal_limit} with $g$ replaced by $T_{C'}\circ g$, and since $|u-T_{C'}(u)|\leqslant|u|\mathds{1}_{\{|u|>C'\}}\leqslant C'^{-\delta}|u|^{1+\delta}$, we have
\begin{gather*}
    \sup_k\mathbb{E}\left\langle|G-T_{C'}(G)|\right\rangle_{N_k+M}^{x_k,y_k,q_k}
    \leqslant C'^{-\delta}\sup_k\mathbb{E}\left\langle|G|^{1+\delta}\right\rangle_{N_k+M}^{x_k,y_k,q_k},\\
    \mathbb{E}\left\langle|G-T_{C'}(G)|\right\rangle_{M,b}^{\pi,\mathfrak{R}}
    \leqslant C'^{-\delta}\mathbb{E}\left\langle|G|^{1+\delta}\right\rangle_{M,b}^{\pi,\mathfrak{R}}.
\end{gather*}
Both right-hand sides tend to zero as $C'\to\infty$, which proves~\eqref{e.cavity_marginal_limit} for every $g$ in the statement, and completes the proof of assertion~\eqref{i.cav_marginal}.

We next prove the normalization~\eqref{e.cavity_canonical_normalization}. Fix $s\in\mathscr{S}$, and let $g((a^{11},r^{11})):=Ma_s^{11}$, which is a continuous function of the array of one replica with growth of degree $d=1$, and satisfies $g((\widetilde R_M(\tau,\tau),\alpha\wedge\alpha))=M\widetilde R_{M,s}(\tau,\tau)=|\tau^{(s)}|^2$. Applying~\eqref{e.cavity_marginal_limit} with $n=1$ and this function $g$, and using~\eqref{e.true_block_second_moment}, we get
\begin{equation*}
    \mathbb{E}\left\langle|\tau^{(s)}|^2\right\rangle_{M,b}^{\pi,\mathfrak{R}}
    =\lim_{k\to\infty}\mathbb{E}\left\langle|\tau^{(s)}|^2\right\rangle_{N_k+M}^{x_k,y_k,q_k}
    =M_s,
\end{equation*}
which is~\eqref{e.cavity_canonical_normalization}. The uniform moment bounds of Lemma~\ref{l.true_cavity_radius_ui} enter here through~\eqref{e.cavity_polynomial_uniform_integrability}: the identity~\eqref{e.true_block_second_moment} alone would not allow the second moment to pass to the limit. Lemma~\ref{l.canonical_normalization_identity} now gives $b=b_\pi$, which completes the proof of assertion~\eqref{i.cav_normalization}.

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{Part 5: The cavity increment.}\par
Since $b$ is admissible for $\pi$, Lemma~\ref{l.remove_cutoffs} gives $\lim_{L\to\infty}\mathcal D_{M,L}(\pi,b)=\mathcal D_M(\pi,b)$. Letting $L\to\infty$ in~\eqref{e.cavity_fixed_cutoff_increment_bound} and recalling~\eqref{e.canonical_ASS_functional}, we obtain
\begin{equation}
    \liminf_{k\to\infty}A_{N_k}(x_k,y_k,q_k)
    \geqslant\mathcal D_M(\pi,b)-\mathcal I_{M,t}(p)=\mathcal P_{M,t,q}(p,b).
    \label{e.cavity_increment_canonical_bound}
\end{equation}
Finally, since $b=b_\pi$ by Part~4, Lemma~\ref{l.canonical_normalization_identity} gives $\mathcal P_{M,t,q}(p,b)=-M\mathscr{P}_{t,q}(p)$, which proves~\eqref{e.cavity_increment_lower_bound} and completes the proof.
<!-- end proof-34 -->
<!-- lemma-27: body_md -->
\label{l.q_dependence}
Let $K\in\{N,N+M\}$, $(x,y)\in\mathfrak X$, and $q\in\mathcal Q_\infty^{\mathscr{S}}$, and define the rescaled path
\begin{equation}
    T_{K,y}q:=\left((1+\eta_Ky^s)^2q^s\right)_{s\in\mathscr{S}}\in\mathcal Q_\infty^{\mathscr{S}}.
    \label{e.T_Ky_def}
\end{equation}
Then $H^{x,y,q}_K(\rho,\alpha)$ is the sum of three terms: a term that does not depend on $q$; the cascade field $\sqrt2W_K^{T_{K,y}q}(\rho,\alpha)$, together with its self-overlap correction $-K(T_{K,y}q)(1)\cdot\lambda$; and the deterministic term
\begin{equation}
    K\eta_K^2\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}(y^s)^2\lambda_sq^s(1),
    \label{e.endpoint_term}
\end{equation}
which is affine in $q$. The same holds for $\widetilde H^{x,y,q}_N$, with $K=N$. Consequently, for every direction $\kappa$ admissible at $q$, the functions $\varepsilon\mapsto\widetilde F_N^{x,y}(t,q+\varepsilon\kappa)$ and $\varepsilon\mapsto\overline F_K^{x,y}(t,q+\varepsilon\kappa)$ are twice continuously differentiable in a neighborhood of $0$, and the directional derivatives~\eqref{e.directional_derivative_def} are given by
\begin{align}
    D_\kappa\widetilde F_N^{x,y}(t,q)&=\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}(1+\eta_Ny^s)^2\,\mathbb{E}\left\langle\kappa^s(\alpha\wedge\alpha')R_{N,s}(\sigma,\sigma')\right\rangle_N^{\mathord{\sim},x,y,q}-\eta_N^2\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}(y^s)^2\lambda_s\kappa^s(1),
    \label{e.derivative_tildeF_exact}\\
    D_\kappa\overline F_{K}^{x,y}(t,q)&=\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}(1+\eta_Ky^s)^2\,\mathbb{E}\left\langle\kappa^s(\alpha\wedge\alpha')R_{K,s}(\rho,\rho')\right\rangle_{K}^{x,y,q}-\eta_K^2\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}(y^s)^2\lambda_s\kappa^s(1).
    \label{e.derivative_trueF_exact}
\end{align}
In particular, there exists a constant $C<\infty$, independent of $N$, $x$, $y$, $q$, and $\kappa$, such that
\begin{align}
    \left|D_\kappa\widetilde F_N^{x,y}(t,q)-\mathbb{E}\left\langle\kappa(\alpha\wedge\alpha')\cdot R_N(\sigma,\sigma')\right\rangle_N^{\mathord{\sim},x,y,q}\right|&\leqslant C\eta_N|\kappa|_{L^\infty},
    \label{e.derivative_tildeF}\\
    \left|D_\kappa\overline F_{N+M}^{x,y}(t,q)-\mathbb{E}\left\langle\kappa(\alpha\wedge\alpha')\cdot R_{N+M}(\rho,\rho')\right\rangle_{N+M}^{x,y,q}\right|&\leqslant C\eta_{N}|\kappa|_{L^\infty},
    \label{e.derivative_trueF}
\end{align}
and such that, for every $q,q'\in\mathcal Q_\infty^{\mathscr{S}}$ and $F\in\{\widetilde F_N^{x,y},\overline F_K^{x,y}\}$,
\begin{equation}
    \left|F(t,q)-F(t,q')\right|\leqslant C|q-q'|_{L^1}+C\eta_K^2\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}|q^s(1)-q'^s(1)|.
    \label{e.perturbed_path_lipschitz}
\end{equation}
Moreover, the semi-concavity estimate~\eqref{e.semi_concave_q_spherical} of Proposition~\ref{p.semi-concave} holds for $\widetilde F_N^{x,y}(t,\cdot)$ and $\overline F_{N+M}^{x,y}(t,\cdot)$ in place of $\overline F_N(t,\cdot)$, with a constant $C$ independent of $N,x,y$.
<!-- end lemma-27 -->
<!-- proof-35: body_md -->
By~\eqref{e.full_radially_evaluated_H}--\eqref{e.full_radial_perturbation} and~\eqref{e.WNq_def}, the $q$-dependent part of $H^{x,y,q}_K(\rho,\alpha)$ is
\begin{equation*}
    \sqrt2W_K^q(\rho,\alpha)-\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}q^s(1)|\rho^{(s)}|^2
    +2\eta_K\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}y^s\partial_{r^s}\left(\sqrt2W_K^q(S_r\rho,\alpha)-\sum_{s'\in\mathscr{S}}q^{s'}(1)|(S_r\rho)^{(s')}|^2\right)\Big|_{r=\vec{\mathbf{1}}}.
\end{equation*}
Since $W^q_K(S_r\rho,\alpha)=\sum_{s'}\sqrt{r^{s'}}\sum_{i\in I_{K,s'}}w_i^{q^{s'}}(\alpha)\rho_i$ and $|(S_r\rho)^{(s')}|^2=r^{s'}|\rho^{(s')}|^2$, the radial derivative in $r^s$ at $r=\vec{\mathbf{1}}$ equals $\frac12\sqrt2\sum_{i\in I_{K,s}}w_i^{q^s}(\alpha)\rho_i-q^s(1)|\rho^{(s)}|^2$. Collecting terms and using $|\rho^{(s)}|^2=|I_{K,s}|=K\lambda_s$ on $\Sigma_K$, the $q$-dependent part is
\begin{equation*}
    \sqrt2\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}(1+\eta_Ky^s)\sum_{i\in I_{K,s}}w_i^{q^s}(\alpha)\rho_i-K\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}(1+2\eta_Ky^s)q^s(1)\lambda_s.
\end{equation*}
The first sum is a cascade field with path $T_{K,y}q$, since $(1+\eta_Ky^s)w^{q^s}_i$ has covariance $(1+\eta_Ky^s)^2q^s(\alpha\wedge\alpha')$, and since $(1+2\eta_Ky^s)=(1+\eta_Ky^s)^2-\eta_K^2(y^s)^2$, the second sum is the self-overlap correction for this field plus the term~\eqref{e.endpoint_term}. The argument for $\widetilde H^{x,y,q}_N$ is identical.

We now compute the directional derivatives. Let $\kappa$ be admissible at $q$, and let $\varepsilon_0>0$ be such that $q_\pm:=q\pm\varepsilon_0\kappa\in\mathcal Q_\infty^{\mathscr{S}}$. For $|\varepsilon|<\varepsilon_0$, the path $q+\varepsilon\kappa$ is the convex combination $\frac12(1-\varepsilon/\varepsilon_0)q_-+\frac12(1+\varepsilon/\varepsilon_0)q_+$, and the same is true after applying the linear map $T_{K,y}$. As in the proof of~\cite[Proposition~5.1]{chen2025free}, we realize the cascade fields with paths $T_{K,y}(q+\varepsilon\kappa)$ jointly for all $|\varepsilon|<\varepsilon_0$ as $\sqrt{\tfrac12(1-\varepsilon/\varepsilon_0)}\,w^{T_{K,y}q_-}+\sqrt{\tfrac12(1+\varepsilon/\varepsilon_0)}\,w^{T_{K,y}q_+}$, with $w^{T_{K,y}q_-}$ and $w^{T_{K,y}q_+}$ independent. The Gaussian integration by parts leading to~\eqref{e.def.der.FN} applies without change to a Hamiltonian which is the sum of a cascade field, of its self-overlap correction, and of Gaussian and deterministic terms whose laws do not depend on the path of the cascade field: the derivative in $\varepsilon$ of the free energy, at the path $T_{K,y}(q+\varepsilon\kappa)$ and in the direction $T_{K,y}\kappa$, is $\mathbb{E}\left\langle(T_{K,y}\kappa)(\alpha\wedge\alpha')\cdot R_K(\rho,\rho')\right\rangle_K^{x,y,q+\varepsilon\kappa}$. The deterministic term~\eqref{e.endpoint_term} enters the free energy $-\frac1K\mathbb{E}\log Z$ with a minus sign, and its derivative in $\varepsilon$ is the constant $K\eta_K^2\sum_s(y^s)^2\lambda_s\kappa^s(1)$. Since $(T_{K,y}\kappa)^s=(1+\eta_Ky^s)^2\kappa^s$, we obtain~\eqref{e.derivative_trueF_exact} at $\varepsilon=0$; the same argument gives~\eqref{e.derivative_tildeF_exact}. Moreover, a second Gaussian integration by parts, as in the proof of~\cite[Proposition~5.1]{chen2025free}, shows that the derivative in $\varepsilon$ computed above is itself continuously differentiable on $(-\varepsilon_0,\varepsilon_0)$, so that the free energies are twice continuously differentiable in $\varepsilon$ there.

For~\eqref{e.derivative_tildeF} and~\eqref{e.derivative_trueF}, we use $0\leqslant y^s\leqslant3$, $\eta_{N+M}\leqslant\eta_N\leqslant1$, and $|R_{K,s}|\leqslant1$: the factors $(1+\eta_Ky^s)^2$ differ from $1$ by at most $15\eta_N$, and the endpoint term is bounded by $9\eta_N^2|\kappa|_{L^\infty}$.

For~\eqref{e.perturbed_path_lipschitz}, let $q,q'\in\mathcal Q_\infty^{\mathscr{S}}$ and $\kappa:=q'-q$. The segment $\varepsilon\mapsto q+\varepsilon\kappa$, $\varepsilon\in[0,1]$, stays in $\mathcal Q_\infty^{\mathscr{S}}$, and, realizing the cascade fields along it as in the proof of~\cite[Proposition~5.1]{chen2025free}, the free energy is a continuous function of $\varepsilon\in[0,1]$, continuously differentiable on $(0,1)$, with derivative given by the right-hand side of~\eqref{e.derivative_trueF_exact} (or~\eqref{e.derivative_tildeF_exact}) evaluated at the path $q+\varepsilon\kappa$. By the invariance~\eqref{e.invariance_cascade}, the overlap $\alpha\wedge\alpha'$ is uniformly distributed on $[0,1]$ under $\mathbb{E}\left\langle\cdot\right\rangle_K^{x,y,q+\varepsilon\kappa}$, so that, using $|R_{K,s}|\leqslant\lambda_s$ and $\sum_s\lambda_s|a_s|\leqslant|a|$ for $a\in\mathbb{R}^{\mathscr{S}}$, the first term of~\eqref{e.derivative_trueF_exact} is bounded by $16\sum_s\lambda_s\mathbb{E}\left\langle|\kappa^s(\alpha\wedge\alpha')|\right\rangle_K^{x,y,q+\varepsilon\kappa}\leqslant16|\kappa|_{L^1}$, while the endpoint term is bounded by $9\eta_K^2\sum_s|\kappa^s(1)|$. Integrating over $\varepsilon\in[0,1]$ gives~\eqref{e.perturbed_path_lipschitz}.

Finally, the last assertion of Proposition~\ref{p.semi-concave} allows for the addition of Gaussian fields independent of the cascade field and of affine deterministic terms, such as~\eqref{e.endpoint_term}; applying it with the path $T_{K,y}q$, whose derivative differs from that of $q$ by bounded factors, gives the semi-concavity estimate.
<!-- end proof-35 -->
<!-- lemma-28: body_md -->
\label{l.radial_semiconcavity_directional_bounds}
Fix $c\in(0,1]$. There exists $C_c<\infty$ such that the following holds for every $i\geqslant1$, $N\in\mathbb{N}$, $(x,y)\in\mathfrak X$, $q\in\mathcal Q_{\uparrow,c}^{\mathscr{S}}\cap\mathcal Q_\infty^{\mathscr{S}}$, and $z\in[0,3]^\mathbb{N}$. Define, for $r\in[0,3]$,
\begin{equation*}
    \mathsf f(r):=\widetilde F_N^{x,y}\left(t,q+q_N(z^{i,r})\right),
    \qquad
    \mathsf g(r):=\overline F_{N+M}^{x,y}\left(t,q+q_N(z^{i,r})\right).
\end{equation*}
Then $\mathsf f$ and $\mathsf g$ are twice continuously differentiable on $[0,3]$, with
\begin{equation}
    \mathsf f'(r)=\eta_N^{1/2}a_i\,D_{\kappa_i}\widetilde F_N^{x,y}\left(t,q+q_N(z^{i,r})\right)
    \qquad\text{and}\qquad
    \mathsf g'(r)=\eta_N^{1/2}a_i\,D_{\kappa_i}\overline F_{N+M}^{x,y}\left(t,q+q_N(z^{i,r})\right),
    \label{e.one_dim_chain_rule}
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
    |\mathsf f'|+|\mathsf g'|\leqslant C_c\,\eta_N^{1/2},
    \qquad
    \mathsf f''\leqslant C_c\,\eta_N,
    \qquad
    \mathsf g''\leqslant C_c\,\eta_N
    \label{e.radial_directional_semiconcavity_bounds}
\end{equation}
on $[0,3]$.
<!-- end lemma-28 -->
<!-- proof-36: body_md -->
By~\eqref{e.q_N_y_spherical}, the map $r\mapsto q+q_N(z^{i,r})$ is affine, with derivative $\eta_N^{1/2}a_i\kappa_i$, and it takes values in $\mathcal Q_{\uparrow,c}^{\mathscr{S}}$ because $\kappa_i$ is nonnegative and nondecreasing. Since $q$ has slope at least $c>0$ while $\kappa_i$ vanishes at the origin and is nondecreasing and Lipschitz, the direction $\kappa_i$ is admissible at $q+q_N(z^{i,r})$ for every $r\in[0,3]$, in the sense of Lemma~\ref{l.q_dependence}. For $r\in[0,3]$, the function $\varepsilon\mapsto\widetilde F_N^{x,y}(t,q+q_N(z^{i,r})+\varepsilon\eta_N^{1/2}a_i\kappa_i)$ coincides with $\mathsf f(r+\varepsilon)$ when $r+\varepsilon\in[0,3]$, and it is twice continuously differentiable in a neighborhood of $0$ by Lemma~\ref{l.q_dependence}. Hence $\mathsf f$ is twice continuously differentiable on $[0,3]$, and~\eqref{e.one_dim_chain_rule} follows from the definition~\eqref{e.directional_derivative_def} of the directional derivative; the same applies to $\mathsf g$. By~\eqref{e.derivative_tildeF}, \eqref{e.derivative_trueF}, and $|R_{N,s}|\leqslant1$,
\begin{equation*}
    |\mathsf f'(r)|+|\mathsf g'(r)|\leqslant2\eta_N^{1/2}a_i\left(1+C\eta_N\right)|\kappa_i|_{L^\infty}.
\end{equation*}
The semi-concavity estimate in Lemma~\ref{l.q_dependence}, applied to two points of the segment $r\mapsto q+q_N(z^{i,r})$, says that $r\mapsto\mathsf f(r)-Cc^{-2}\eta_Na_i^2| 
\accentset{\mbox{\large\bfseries .}}{\kappa}_i|_{L^2}^2\,r^2$ is concave on $[0,3]$; since $\mathsf f$ is twice differentiable, $\mathsf f''\leqslant2Cc^{-2}\eta_Na_i^2| 
\accentset{\mbox{\large\bfseries .}}{\kappa}_i|_{L^2}^2$, and the same holds for $\mathsf g''$. Since $a_i|\kappa_i|_{L^\infty}\leqslant1$ and $a_i| 
\accentset{\mbox{\large\bfseries .}}{\kappa}_i|_{L^2}\leqslant a_i| 
\accentset{\mbox{\large\bfseries .}}{\kappa}_i|_{L^\infty}\leqslant1$ by~\eqref{e.a_i_spherical}, the bounds~\eqref{e.radial_directional_semiconcavity_bounds} follow, with a constant that does not depend on $i$.
<!-- end proof-36 -->
<!-- lemma-29: body_md -->
\label{l.semi_concavity_one_dim_spherical}
There exists $C>0$ with the following property. Let $\mathsf f,\mathsf g:[0,3]\to\mathbb{R}$ be twice continuously differentiable, with $|\mathsf f'|,|\mathsf g'|\leqslant a$ and $\mathsf f'',\mathsf g''\leqslant b$ on $[0,3]$, for some $a,b>0$. We have
\begin{equation*}
    \int_1^2|\mathsf f'(r)-\mathsf g'(r)|^2\,\mathrm{d} r\leqslant C(a+b)\|\mathsf f-\mathsf g\|_{L^\infty[0,3]}.
\end{equation*}
<!-- end lemma-29 -->
<!-- proof-37: body_md -->
This is~\cite[Lemma~6.2]{chen2026ising}; we recall the argument. Choose a smooth function $\zeta:[0,3]\to[0,1]$ with compact support in $(0,3)$ and such that $\zeta=1$ on $[1,2]$. Integration by parts gives
\begin{align*}
    \int_1^2|\mathsf f'-\mathsf g'|^2\leqslant\int_0^3\zeta(\mathsf f'-\mathsf g')^2=-\int_0^3\zeta'(\mathsf f-\mathsf g)(\mathsf f'-\mathsf g')-\int_0^3\zeta(\mathsf f-\mathsf g)(\mathsf f''-\mathsf g'').
\end{align*}
The first term on the right-hand side is bounded by $6a|\zeta'|_{L^\infty}\|\mathsf f-\mathsf g\|_{L^\infty}$. Since $b-\mathsf f''\geqslant0$ and $b-\mathsf g''\geqslant0$,
\begin{align*}
    \int_0^3|\mathsf f''-\mathsf g''|\leqslant\int_0^3\left((b-\mathsf f'')+(b-\mathsf g'')\right)=6b-\mathsf f'(3)-\mathsf g'(3)+\mathsf f'(0)+\mathsf g'(0)\leqslant6b+4a,
\end{align*}
which bounds the second term.
<!-- end proof-37 -->
<!-- lemma-30: body_md -->
\label{l.derivative_matching_spherical}
For every $q\in\mathcal Q_{\infty,\uparrow}^{\mathscr{S}}$ and every $i\geqslant1$,
\begin{equation}
    \lim_{N\to\infty}\mathbb{E}_{x,y,z}\mathfrak D_{N,i}(x,y,z)=0.
    \label{e.derivative_matching_average_spherical}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-30 -->
<!-- proof-38: body_md -->
Choose $c\in(0,1]$ such that $q\in\mathcal Q_{\uparrow,c}^{\mathscr{S}}$, and set $Q:=\{q+q_{N}(z):N\in\mathbb{N},\ z\in[0,3]^\mathbb{N}\}$, which is a bounded subset of $\mathcal Q_\infty^{\mathscr{S}}$ by~\eqref{e.q_N_small_spherical}. Fix $i\geqslant1$, $(x,y)\in\mathfrak X$, and $z\in[1,2]^\mathbb{N}$, and let $\mathsf f$ and $\mathsf g$ be as in Lemma~\ref{l.radial_semiconcavity_directional_bounds}. By that lemma, the assumptions of Lemma~\ref{l.semi_concavity_one_dim_spherical} hold with $a=C_c\eta_N^{1/2}$ and $b=C_c\eta_N$, and $\|\mathsf f-\mathsf g\|_{L^\infty[0,3]}\leqslant\varepsilon_N(Q)$ by the definition of $\varepsilon_N(Q)$ in~\eqref{e.eps_N_small}. Lemma~\ref{l.semi_concavity_one_dim_spherical} therefore gives
\begin{equation*}
    \int_1^2|\mathsf f'(r)-\mathsf g'(r)|^2\,\mathrm{d} r\leqslant C_c\left(\eta_N^{1/2}+\eta_N\right)\varepsilon_N(Q).
\end{equation*}
By~\eqref{e.one_dim_chain_rule} and~\eqref{e.D_N,i=}, we have $|\mathsf f'(r)-\mathsf g'(r)|^2=\eta_Na_i^2\,\mathfrak D_{N,i}(x,y,z^{i,r})$, so that the left-hand side equals $\eta_Na_i^2\int_1^2\mathfrak D_{N,i}(x,y,z^{i,r})\,\mathrm{d} r$. Integrating over the remaining coordinates $(z_j)_{j\ne i}\in[1,2]^{\mathbb{N}\setminus\{i\}}$, we obtain
\begin{align*}
    \mathbb{E}_z\mathfrak D_{N,i}(x,y,z)\leqslant C_c\,a_i^{-2}\,\eta_N^{-1/2}\left(1+\eta_N^{1/2}\right)\varepsilon_N(Q),
\end{align*}
uniformly over $(x,y)\in\mathfrak X$. The right-hand side tends to zero by~\eqref{e.eps_N_small}, which proves~\eqref{e.derivative_matching_average_spherical}.
<!-- end proof-38 -->
<!-- lemma-31: body_md -->
\label{l.overlap_identities_radial_spherical}
For every bounded subset $Q\subseteq\mathcal Q_\infty^{\mathscr{S}}$,
\begin{equation*}
    \lim_{N\to\infty}\sup_{q\in Q}\mathbb{E}_{x,y}\Delta_N(x,y,q)=0.
\end{equation*}
<!-- end lemma-31 -->
<!-- proof-39: body_md -->
Fix $\mathsf h\in\mathbb{N}^4$, and set
\begin{equation*}
    H_N^{\mathsf h,y}(\sigma,\alpha):=H_N^{\mathsf h}(\sigma,\alpha)+2\eta_N\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}y^s\partial_{r^s}H_N^{\mathsf h}(S_r\sigma,\alpha)\big|_{r=\vec{\mathbf{1}}}.
\end{equation*}
By~\eqref{e.perturbed_enriched_H}, \eqref{e.radially_evaluated_H}, and~\eqref{e.radial_generic_perturbation}, the dependence of $\widetilde H_N^{x,y,q}$ on the coordinate $x_{\mathsf h}$ is
\begin{equation*}
    \widetilde H_N^{x,y,q}(\sigma,\alpha)=\widetilde H_{N,\mathsf h}^{x,y,q}(\sigma,\alpha)+\eta_Nx_{\mathsf h}c_{\mathsf h}H_N^{\mathsf h,y}(\sigma,\alpha),
\end{equation*}
where $\widetilde H_{N,\mathsf h}^{x,y,q}$ does not depend on $x_{\mathsf h}$ and is independent of $H^{\mathsf h,y}_N$. By Lemma~\ref{l.comput_cov_radial},
\begin{equation*}
    \mathbb{E} H_N^{\mathsf h,y}(\sigma,\alpha)H_N^{\mathsf h,y}(\sigma',\alpha')=N(\mathsf C_{\mathsf h})_{\eta_N,y}\left(R_N(\sigma,\sigma'),\alpha\wedge\alpha'\right),
\end{equation*}
and by~\eqref{e.f_eta_N,y=} and~\eqref{e.Lambda_h_def},
\begin{equation*}
    \sup_{y\in[1,2]^{\mathscr{S}}}\sup_{v\in[-2,2]^{\mathscr{S}},\ u\in[0,1]}\left|(\mathsf C_{\mathsf h})_{\eta_N,y}(v,u)-\mathsf C_{\mathsf h}(v,u)\right|\leqslant C\Lambda_{\mathsf h}(\eta_N+\eta_N^2).
\end{equation*}
The perturbation $\eta_Nx_{\mathsf h}c_{\mathsf h}H_N^{\mathsf h,y}$ is thus of exactly the form treated in the proof of~\cite[Proposition~6.8]{chen2025free}, with the same coefficient $\eta_N=N^{-1/16}$, except that the covariance kernel $\mathsf C_{\mathsf h}$ is replaced by $(\mathsf C_{\mathsf h})_{\eta_N,y}$. That proof uses the differentiation of the free energy in $x_{\mathsf h}$ followed by Gaussian integration by parts, the convexity of $\log Z_N^{\mathord{\sim},x,y,q}$ in $x_{\mathsf h}$, and the concentration of $\log Z_N^{\mathord{\sim},x,y,q}$ around its expectation. The latter is provided by Lemma~\ref{l.cascade_concentration}: the Hamiltonian $\widetilde H^{x,y,q}_N$ is of the form~\eqref{e.linear_cascade_hamiltonian}, see Remark~\ref{r.linear_form_hamiltonians}, and by~\eqref{e.covariance_perturbed_H}, \eqref{e.second_radial_bound}, and~\eqref{e.radial_energy_covariance_bound}, its variance is bounded by $CN$ uniformly over $q\in Q$, $x$, and $y\in[1,2]^{\mathscr{S}}$. Hence $\sup_{x,y,q}\mathbb{E}|\log Z_N^{\mathord{\sim},x,y,q}-\mathbb{E}\log Z_N^{\mathord{\sim},x,y,q}|\leqslant CN^{1/2}$, which is the concentration bound on which the argument of~\cite{chen2025free} rests. That argument then applies verbatim, and the estimates it yields are uniform over $(q,y)$. The Gaussian integration by parts produces the Ghirlanda--Guerra identities for the array $(\mathsf C_{\mathsf h})_{\eta_N,y}(R^{\ell,\ell'}_N,R^{\ell,\ell'}_\alpha)$, and replacing this kernel by $\mathsf C_{\mathsf h}$ changes each term of~\eqref{e.Delta_r_def} by at most $C\Lambda_{\mathsf h}(\eta_N+\eta_N^2)\|\mathbf{f}\|_\infty$. Therefore, for every $j\in\mathbb{N}$,
\begin{equation*}
    \lim_{N\to\infty}\sup_{q\in Q}\mathbb{E}_{x,y}\Delta_N^{x,y,q}(\mathbf{f}_j,n_j,\mathsf h_j)=0.
\end{equation*}
Since $0\leqslant\Delta_N^{x,y,q}(\mathbf{f}_j,n_j,\mathsf h_j)\leqslant1$ by~\eqref{e.Delta<1}, the definition~\eqref{e.Delta_MN_def} and dominated convergence complete the proof.
<!-- end proof-39 -->
<!-- lemma-32: body_md -->
\label{l.choose_perturbations_spherical}
For every $q\in\mathcal Q_{\infty,\uparrow}^{\mathscr{S}}$, there exist $(x_n,y_n)\in\mathfrak X$ and $z_n\in[1,2]^\mathbb{N}$ such that, with $q_n:=q+q_{N_n}(z_n)$,
\begin{gather}
    \lim_{n\to\infty}\Delta_{N_n}(x_n,y_n,z_n)=0,
    \label{e.chosen_Delta_zero}\\
    \lim_{n\to\infty}\operatorname{Rad}_{N_n,L}(x_n,y_n,z_n)=0
    \quad\text{for every }L\in\mathbb{N},
    \label{e.chosen_Rad_zero}\\
    \lim_{n\to\infty}\left(D_{\kappa_i}\widetilde F_{N_n}^{x_n,y_n}(t,q_n)-D_{\kappa_i}\overline F_{N_n+M}^{x_n,y_n}(t,q_n)\right)=0
    \quad\text{for every }i\geqslant1,
    \label{e.chosen_derivative_match}\\
    \limsup_{n\to\infty}\overline F_{N_n}(t,q)\leqslant\limsup_{n\to\infty}\left(-\frac1M A_{N_n}(x_n,y_n,z_n)\right).
    \label{e.upper_selected_A}
\end{gather}
<!-- end lemma-32 -->
<!-- proof-40: body_md -->
Set $Q:=\{q+q_N(z):N\in\mathbb{N},\ z\in[0,3]^\mathbb{N}\}$, a bounded subset of $\mathcal Q_\infty^{\mathscr{S}}$ by~\eqref{e.q_N_small_spherical}. All the constants and the sets in~\eqref{e.xyqbR_uniform} are understood with this $Q$.

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{Step 1: Averaged bounds.}\par
Lemma~\ref{l.overlap_identities_radial_spherical} gives $\lim_{N\to\infty}\mathbb{E}_{x,y,z}\Delta_N(x,y,z)=0$. Lemma~\ref{l.radial_self_average}, applied with the set $Q$, gives $\lim_{N\to\infty}\mathbb{E}_{x,y,z}\operatorname{Rad}_{N,L}(x,y,z)=0$ for every $L\in\mathbb{N}$. Moreover, by Lemma~\ref{l.fixed_tilt_uniform_bounds} and Jensen's inequality, for every $L\in\mathbb{N}$ there is $K_L<\infty$ such that $\sup_{N,x,y,z}\operatorname{Rad}_{N,L}(x,y,z)\leqslant K_L$. Since $0\leqslant\frac{2^{-L}}{1+K_L}\operatorname{Rad}_{N,L}\leqslant2^{-L}$, dominated convergence gives
\begin{equation*}
    \lim_{N\to\infty}\mathbb{E}_{x,y,z}\sum_{L=1}^\infty \frac{2^{-L}}{1+K_L} \operatorname{Rad}_{N,L}(x,y,z)=0.
\end{equation*}
Finally, \eqref{e.derivative_tildeF}, \eqref{e.derivative_trueF}, and $0\leqslant\kappa_i\leqslant1$ give $\mathfrak D_{N,i}\leqslant C$ uniformly in $i,N,x,y,z$; Lemma~\ref{l.derivative_matching_spherical} and dominated convergence therefore yield $\lim_{N\to\infty}\mathbb{E}_{x,y,z}\mathfrak D_{N}(x,y,z)=0$.

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{Step 2: Selection of the parameters.}\par
Set
\begin{equation*}
    \mathfrak E_N(x,y,z):=\Delta_N(x,y,z)+\mathfrak D_N(x,y,z)+\sum_{L=1}^\infty\frac{2^{-L}}{1+K_L}\operatorname{Rad}_{N,L}(x,y,z),
\end{equation*}
a nonnegative quantity with $\lim_{N\to\infty}\mathbb{E}_{x,y,z}\mathfrak E_N(x,y,z)=0$ by Step~1. By Lemma~\ref{l.fixed_block_increment_bound}, there is $C_A<\infty$ such that $|A_{N}(x,y,z)|\leqslant C_A$ for every sufficiently large $N$ and every $(x,y,z)\in\mathfrak X\times[1,2]^\mathbb{N}$. For $\varepsilon\in(0,C_A]$, consider the event
\begin{equation*}
    \Omega_{\varepsilon,N}:=\{(x,y,z):A_{N}(x,y,z)\leqslant\mathbb{E}_{x,y,z}A_{N}(x,y,z)+\varepsilon\}.
\end{equation*}
Since $A_N-\mathbb{E}_{x,y,z}A_N$ is centered, bounded below by $-2C_A$, and larger than $\varepsilon$ on the complement of $\Omega_{\varepsilon,N}$, we have $0\geqslant\varepsilon\,\mathbb{P}_{x,y,z}(\Omega_{\varepsilon,N}^c)-2C_A\mathbb{P}_{x,y,z}(\Omega_{\varepsilon,N})$, hence
\begin{equation*}
    \mathbb{P}_{x,y,z}(\Omega_{\varepsilon,N})\geqslant\frac{\varepsilon}{2C_A+\varepsilon}\geqslant\frac{\varepsilon}{3C_A},
\end{equation*}
which is the averaging argument of~\cite[Lemma~3.3]{pan}. On the other hand, Markov's inequality gives $\mathbb{P}_{x,y,z}(\mathfrak E_N\leqslant\varepsilon)\geqslant1-\varepsilon^{-1}\mathbb{E}_{x,y,z}\mathfrak E_N$. Take $\varepsilon_N:=2\left(C_A\left(\mathbb{E}_{x,y,z}\mathfrak E_N+N^{-1}\right)\right)^{1/2}$, so that $\varepsilon_N\to0$ and $\varepsilon_N^2>3C_A\mathbb{E}_{x,y,z}\mathfrak E_N$. For every sufficiently large $N$, we have $\varepsilon_N\leqslant C_A$, and the sum of the two probabilities above exceeds one, so that $\Omega_{\varepsilon_N,N}\cap\{\mathfrak E_N\leqslant\varepsilon_N\}\ne\emptyset$. We choose $(x_n,y_n,z_n)$ in this intersection for $N=N_n$. Then
\begin{equation*}
    \lim_{n\to\infty}\mathfrak E_{N_n}(x_n,y_n,z_n)=0
    \qquad\text{and}\qquad
    A_{N_n}(x_n,y_n,z_n)\leqslant\mathbb{E}_{x,y,z}A_{N_n}(x,y,z)+\varepsilon_{N_n}.
\end{equation*}
Since all the terms in $\mathfrak E_N$ are nonnegative with positive weights, the first limit gives~\eqref{e.chosen_Delta_zero}, \eqref{e.chosen_Rad_zero}, and $\lim_n\mathfrak D_{N_n}(x_n,y_n,z_n)=0$; the latter implies $\lim_n\mathfrak D_{N_n,i}(x_n,y_n,z_n)=0$ for every $i$, which is~\eqref{e.chosen_derivative_match}.

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{Step 3: Free energy as an average of cavity increments.}\par
By~\eqref{e.ASS_increment_def} and the definition of $A_N(x,y,z)$,
\begin{multline*}
    -N_{j+1}\overline F_{N_{j+1}}^{x,y}(t,q+q_{N_{j+1}}(z))+N_j\overline F_{N_j}^{x,y}(t,q+q_{N_j}(z))
    \\
    =A_{N_j}(x,y,z)-N_{j+1}\left(\overline F_{N_{j+1}}^{x,y}(t,q+q_{N_{j+1}}(z))-\overline F_{N_{j+1}}^{x,y}(t,q+q_{N_j}(z))\right).
\end{multline*}
By~\eqref{e.q_N_y_spherical}, we have $q_{N_{j+1}}(z)-q_{N_j}(z)=(\eta_{N_{j+1}}^{1/2}-\eta_{N_j}^{1/2})\sum_ia_iz_i\kappa_i$, and the path $\sum_ia_iz_i\kappa_i$ is bounded by $1$ in $L^\infty$ by~\eqref{e.a_i_spherical}. Since $\eta_{N_j}^{1/2}=(jM)^{-1/32}$, both $|q_{N_{j+1}}(z)-q_{N_j}(z)|_{L^1}$ and $\sum_s|q^s_{N_{j+1}}(z)(1)-q^s_{N_j}(z)(1)|$ are bounded by $Cj^{-1-1/32}$. The Lipschitz estimate~\eqref{e.perturbed_path_lipschitz}, which applies to the perturbed free energy and accounts for the endpoint term in Lemma~\ref{l.q_dependence}, therefore bounds the last term by $CN_{j+1}j^{-1-1/32}\leqslant Cj^{-1/32}$. Summing over $1\leqslant j<n$ and dividing by $N_n=nM$, we obtain, uniformly over $(x,y,z)\in\mathfrak X\times[1,2]^\mathbb{N}$,
\begin{equation}
    \overline F_{N_n}^{x,y}(t,q+q_{N_n}(z))=-\frac1{nM}\sum_{j=1}^{n-1}A_{N_j}(x,y,z)+o(1),
    \label{e.telescoping_identity}
\end{equation}
where we also used that the term $N_1\overline F^{x,y}_{N_1}(t,q+q_{N_1}(z))$ is bounded. Moreover, removing the perturbations at the path $q+q_{N_n}(z)$ costs at most $C\eta_{N_n}$ by~\eqref{e.full_radial_free_energy_cost} and~\eqref{e.GG_free_energy_cost}, and then~\eqref{e.F_N_Lipschitz} and~\eqref{e.q_N_small_spherical} give $|\overline F_{N_n}(t,q+q_{N_n}(z))-\overline F_{N_n}(t,q)|\leqslant C\eta_{N_n}^{1/2}$; hence
\begin{equation*}
    \sup_{(x,y,z)\in\mathfrak X\times[1,2]^\mathbb{N}}\left|\overline F_{N_n}^{x,y}(t,q+q_{N_n}(z))-\overline F_{N_n}(t,q)\right|=o(1).
\end{equation*}
Averaging~\eqref{e.telescoping_identity} over $(x,y,z)$ therefore gives
\begin{equation}
    \overline F_{N_n}(t,q)=-\frac1{nM}\sum_{j=1}^{n-1}\mathbb{E}_{x,y,z}A_{N_j}(x,y,z)+o(1).
    \label{e.average_telescoping_identity}
\end{equation}
Since $\limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac1n\sum_{j=1}^{n-1}v_j\leqslant\limsup_{j\to\infty}v_j$ for every bounded sequence $(v_j)$ of real numbers, we deduce from~\eqref{e.average_telescoping_identity} and the choice of $(x_n,y_n,z_n)$ in Step~2 that
\begin{equation*}
    \limsup_{n\to\infty}\overline F_{N_n}(t,q)\leqslant\limsup_{n\to\infty}\left(-\frac1M\mathbb{E}_{x,y,z}A_{N_n}(x,y,z)\right)\leqslant\limsup_{n\to\infty}\left(-\frac1M A_{N_n}(x_n,y_n,z_n)\right),
\end{equation*}
which is~\eqref{e.upper_selected_A}.
<!-- end proof-40 -->
<!-- proof-41: body_md -->
\smallskip
\noindent\emph{Step 1: The upper bound.}\par
Let $(x_n,y_n,z_n,q_n)$ be given by Lemma~\ref{l.choose_perturbations_spherical}. By~\eqref{e.q_N_small_spherical}, the paths $q_n$ are uniformly bounded and converge to $q$ uniformly on $[0,1]$, so that~\eqref{e.cavity_theorem_path_convergence} holds. Pass to a subsequence along which $-\frac1MA_{N_n}(x_n,y_n,z_n)$ converges to its $\limsup$. By~\eqref{e.chosen_Delta_zero} and~\eqref{e.chosen_Rad_zero}, Theorem~\ref{t.spherical_cavity_lim} applies along this subsequence, and provides a further subsequence, a path $p\in\mathcal Q_{\infty,\leqslant\lambda}^{\mathscr{S}}$, and a vector $b$ admissible for $\pi:=q+t\nabla\xi(p)$ such that, by~\eqref{e.cavity_increment_lower_bound},
\begin{equation}
    \limsup_{n\to\infty}\left(-\frac1M A_{N_n}(x_n,y_n,z_n)\right)\leqslant\mathscr{P}_{t,q}(p).
    \label{e.critical_A_limit}
\end{equation}
Combining~\eqref{e.upper_selected_A} and~\eqref{e.critical_A_limit} gives~\eqref{e.spherical_critical_bounds}.

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{Step 2: The critical relation.}\par
We keep the subsequence, the path $p$, and the vector $b$ of Step~1, and we show that $p$ satisfies~\eqref{e.spherical_critical_relation}. Fix $i\geqslant1$. As observed in the proof of Lemma~\ref{l.radial_semiconcavity_directional_bounds}, the direction $\kappa_i$ is admissible at $q_n$, and by~\eqref{e.derivative_tildeF} with $\kappa=\kappa_i$, the directional derivative $D_{\kappa_i}\widetilde F_{N_n}^{x_n,y_n}(t,q_n)$ differs from $\mathbb{E}\left\langle\kappa_i(\alpha\wedge\alpha')\cdot R_{N_n}(\sigma,\sigma')\right\rangle_{N_n}^{\mathord{\sim},x_n,y_n,q_n}$ by at most $C\eta_{N_n}$. By part~\eqref{i.cav_overlaps} of Theorem~\ref{t.spherical_cavity_lim}, the continuity and boundedness of $\kappa_i$, and the fact that $\alpha\wedge\alpha'$ is uniformly distributed on $[0,1]$ under $\mathbb{E}\left\langle\cdot\right\rangle_\mathfrak{R}$, we deduce that
\begin{equation}
    \lim_{n\to\infty}D_{\kappa_i}\widetilde F_{N_n}^{x_n,y_n}(t,q_n)=\mathbb{E}\left\langle\kappa_i(\alpha\wedge\alpha')\cdot p(\alpha\wedge\alpha')\right\rangle_\mathfrak{R}=\left\langle\kappa_i,p\right\rangle_{L^2}.
    \label{e.tilde_derivative_limit}
\end{equation}
For the $(N+M)$-spin system, we first use the exchangeability of the coordinates within each species. By~\eqref{e.mean_perturbed_H} and~\eqref{e.covariance_perturbed_H}, the law of $H^{x,y,q}_{N+M}$ is invariant under permutations of the coordinates in $I_{N+M,s}$; so is the reference measure $P_{N+M}$, and therefore so is $\mathbb{E}\left\langle\cdot\right\rangle_{N+M}^{x,y,q}$. Hence, for $j_0\in\mathsf M_s$, using $|I_{N_n+M,s}|/(N_n+M)=\lambda_s=M_s/M$ by~\eqref{e.compatible_sequence} and~\eqref{e.lambda_compatible_block},
\begin{align}
    \mathbb{E}\left\langle\kappa_i^s(\alpha\wedge\alpha')R_{N_n+M,s}(\rho,\rho')\right\rangle_{N_n+M}^{x_n,y_n,q_n}
    &=\frac{|I_{N_n+M,s}|}{N_n+M}\mathbb{E}\left\langle\kappa_i^s(\alpha\wedge\alpha')\rho_{N_n+j_0}\rho'_{N_n+j_0}\right\rangle_{N_n+M}^{x_n,y_n,q_n}\notag\\
    &=\frac{M_s}{M}\mathbb{E}\left\langle\kappa_i^s(\alpha\wedge\alpha')\tau_{j_0}\tau'_{j_0}\right\rangle_{N_n+M}^{x_n,y_n,q_n}\notag\\
    &=\mathbb{E}\left\langle\kappa_i^s(\alpha\wedge\alpha')\widetilde R_{M,s}(\tau,\tau')\right\rangle_{N_n+M}^{x_n,y_n,q_n}.
    \label{e.permutation_replace_overlap}
\end{align}
Now apply part~\eqref{i.cav_marginal} of Theorem~\ref{t.spherical_cavity_lim} with two replicas and $g((a^{\ell,\ell'},r^{\ell,\ell'})_{\ell,\ell'\leqslant2}):=\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}\kappa_i^s(r^{1,2})a_s^{1,2}$, which is continuous with linear growth. Together with~\eqref{e.derivative_trueF}, \eqref{e.permutation_replace_overlap}, the identity $b=b_\pi$ from part~\eqref{i.cav_normalization}, and Lemma~\ref{l.derivative_initial} applied with $\kappa=\kappa_i\in\mathcal Q_\infty^{\mathscr{S}}$, this gives
\begin{equation}
    \lim_{n\to\infty}D_{\kappa_i}\overline F_{N_n+M}^{x_n,y_n}(t,q_n)=\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}\mathbb{E}\left\langle\kappa_i^s(\alpha\wedge\alpha')\widetilde R_{M,s}(\tau,\tau')\right\rangle^{\pi,\mathfrak{R}}_{M,b_\pi}=\left\langle\kappa_i,\partial_q\psi(\pi)\right\rangle_{L^2}.
    \label{e.true_derivative_limit}
\end{equation}
Combining~\eqref{e.chosen_derivative_match}, \eqref{e.tilde_derivative_limit}, and~\eqref{e.true_derivative_limit}, we obtain
\begin{equation*}
    \left\langle\kappa_i,p\right\rangle_{L^2}=\left\langle\kappa_i,\partial_q\psi\left(q+t\nabla\xi(p)\right)\right\rangle_{L^2},
    \qquad i\geqslant1.
\end{equation*}
Since both $p$ and $\partial_q\psi(q+t\nabla\xi(p))$ belong to $\mathcal Q_{\infty,\leqslant\lambda}^{\mathscr{S}}$, by~\eqref{e.derivative_psi_lambda}, the separating property~\eqref{e.separating_family} yields $p=\partial_q\psi(q+t\nabla\xi(p))$, which is~\eqref{e.spherical_critical_relation}.
<!-- end proof-41 -->
<!-- lemma-33: body_md -->
\label{l.dual_cone_monotone}
For every probability vector $\lambda$ with positive entries, the function $\psi_\lambda$ is $(\mathcal Q_2^{\mathscr{S}})^*$-increasing on $\mathcal Q_2^{\mathscr{S}}$; in particular, so is $\psi$.
<!-- end lemma-33 -->
<!-- proof-42: body_md -->
Let $q,q'\in\mathcal Q_2^{\mathscr{S}}$ be such that $q'-q\in(\mathcal Q_2^{\mathscr{S}})^*$. Since $\mathcal Q_2^{\mathscr{S}}$ is convex, the segment $q_u:=q+u(q'-q)$, $u\in[0,1]$, stays in $\mathcal Q_2^{\mathscr{S}}$. By~\eqref{e.psi_quadratic_remainder}, the function $u\mapsto\psi_\lambda(q_u)$ is differentiable on $[0,1]$, with derivative $\left\langle q'-q,\partial_q\psi_\lambda(q_u)\right\rangle_{L^2}$. By~\eqref{e.derivative_psi_lambda}, $\partial_q\psi_\lambda(q_u)$ is a path in $\mathcal Q_\infty^{\mathscr{S}}\subseteq\mathcal Q_2^{\mathscr{S}}$, so this derivative is nonnegative, by the definition~\eqref{e.Cstar} of the dual cone. Hence $u\mapsto\psi_\lambda(q_u)$ is nondecreasing, and $\psi_\lambda(q')\geqslant\psi_\lambda(q)$.
<!-- end proof-42 -->
<!-- definition-1: body_md -->
\label{d.regularization}
A function $\overline\xi:\mathbb{R}_+^{\mathscr{S}}\to\mathbb{R}$ is called a regularization of $\xi$ if the following conditions hold.
\begin{enumerate}
    \item The function $\overline\xi$ agrees with $\xi$ on $\{a\in\mathbb{R}_+^{\mathscr{S}}:|a|\leqslant1\}$.
    \item The function $\overline\xi$ is Lipschitz and proper, in the sense that $\overline\xi$ is $\mathbb{R}_+^{\mathscr{S}}$-increasing and, for every $b\in\mathbb{R}_+^{\mathscr{S}}$, the map $\mathbb{R}_+^{\mathscr{S}}\ni a\mapsto\overline\xi(a+b)-\overline\xi(a)$ is also $\mathbb{R}_+^{\mathscr{S}}$-increasing.
    \item If $\xi$ is convex on $\mathbb{R}_+^{\mathscr{S}}$, then $\overline\xi$ is convex.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end definition-1 -->
<!-- definition-2: body_md -->
\label{d.vs}
Let $\overline\xi$ be a regularization of $\xi$, and let $\mathsf{H}$ be defined by~\eqref{e.def_H_spin_glass}. Consider the equation
\begin{equation}
\label{e.hj_H}
\partial_t f-\mathsf{H}(\partial_q f)=0
\qquad\text{on }\mathbb{R}_+\times\mathcal Q_2^{\mathscr{S}}.
\end{equation}
\begin{enumerate}
    \item A continuous function $f:\mathbb{R}_+\times\mathcal Q_2^{\mathscr{S}}\to\mathbb{R}$ is a viscosity subsolution of~\eqref{e.hj_H} if, for every $(t,q)\in(0,\infty)\times\mathcal Q_2^{\mathscr{S}}$ and every smooth function $\phi$ such that $f-\phi$ has a local maximum at $(t,q)$, relative to $(0,\infty)\times\mathcal Q_2^{\mathscr{S}}$, we have
    \begin{equation*}
        \left(\partial_t\phi-\mathsf{H}(\partial_q\phi)\right)(t,q)\leqslant0.
    \end{equation*}
    \item A continuous function $f:\mathbb{R}_+\times\mathcal Q_2^{\mathscr{S}}\to\mathbb{R}$ is a viscosity supersolution of~\eqref{e.hj_H} if, for every $(t,q)\in(0,\infty)\times\mathcal Q_2^{\mathscr{S}}$ and every smooth function $\phi$ such that $f-\phi$ has a local minimum at $(t,q)$, relative to $(0,\infty)\times\mathcal Q_2^{\mathscr{S}}$, we have
    \begin{equation*}
        \left(\partial_t\phi-\mathsf{H}(\partial_q\phi)\right)(t,q)\geqslant0.
    \end{equation*}
    \item A continuous function $f:\mathbb{R}_+\times\mathcal Q_2^{\mathscr{S}}\to\mathbb{R}$ is a viscosity solution of~\eqref{e.hj_H} if it is both a viscosity subsolution and a viscosity supersolution.
\end{enumerate}
Finally, a continuous function $f:\mathbb{R}_+\times\mathcal Q_2^{\mathscr{S}}\to\mathbb{R}$ is called a viscosity solution of the equation in~\eqref{e.main.hj} if it is a viscosity solution of~\eqref{e.hj_H} for some regularization $\overline\xi$ of $\xi$.
<!-- end definition-2 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
\label{t.vis_sol}
Let $\psi$ be the spherical initial condition defined in~\eqref{e.multi_species_initial}, restricted to $\mathcal Q_2^{\mathscr{S}}$.
\begin{enumerate}
    \item \label{i.vis_sol_existence} For every regularization $\overline\xi$ of $\xi$, there exists a viscosity solution $f$ of~\eqref{e.hj_H} with $f(0,\cdot)=\psi$, unique in the class of Lipschitz functions on $\mathbb{R}_+\times\mathcal Q_2^{\mathscr{S}}$, and $f$ does not depend on the choice of $\overline\xi$. In particular, $f$ is the unique Lipschitz viscosity solution of~\eqref{e.main.hj}.
    \item \label{i.vis_sol_hopf} For every $(t,q)\in\mathbb{R}_+\times\mathcal Q_2^{\mathscr{S}}$,
    \begin{equation}
    \label{e.Hopf_spin_glass}
        f(t,q)=\sup_{p\in\mathcal Q_\infty^{\mathscr{S}}}\ \inf_{q'\in\mathcal Q_\infty^{\mathscr{S}}}\ \mathcal J_{t,q}(q',p)=\sup_{p\in\mathcal Q_{\infty,\leqslant\lambda_\infty}^{\mathscr{S}}}\ \inf_{q'\in\mathcal Q_\infty^{\mathscr{S}}}\ \mathcal J_{t,q}(q',p).
    \end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- proof-43: body_md -->
We verify the hypotheses of~\cite[Theorem~4.7]{chen2022hamilton}. The function $\xi$ is locally Lipschitz, and it is proper on $\mathbb{R}_+^{\mathscr{S}}$, as shown after Definition~\ref{d.regularization}. By Lemma~\ref{l.dual_cone_monotone} and Corollary~\ref{c.psi_multi_species}, the function $\psi$ is $(\mathcal Q_2^{\mathscr{S}})^*$-increasing on $\mathcal Q_2^{\mathscr{S}}$ and satisfies
\begin{equation*}
    |\psi(q)-\psi(q')|\leqslant|q-q'|_{L^1},
    \qquad q,q'\in\mathcal Q_2^{\mathscr{S}},
\end{equation*}
and $\psi$ is convex by Lemma~\ref{l.psi_convex}. Part~\eqref{i.vis_sol_existence} is therefore~\cite[Theorem~4.7]{chen2022hamilton}, in the diagonal setting discussed after Definition~\ref{d.vs}, together with~\cite[Remark~4.10]{chen2022hamilton} for the independence of $f$ from the choice of $\overline\xi$; the last sentence of part~\eqref{i.vis_sol_existence} is a rephrasing, since a viscosity solution of the equation in~\eqref{e.main.hj} is by definition a viscosity solution of~\eqref{e.hj_H} for some regularization. Since $\psi$ is convex, \cite[Theorem~4.7]{chen2022hamilton} also gives the Hopf formula, which is the first equality in~\eqref{e.Hopf_spin_glass}: the supremum and the infimum there are over bounded paths in the cone, that is, over $\mathcal Q_\infty^{\mathscr{S}}$.

It remains to show that the supremum can be restricted to $\mathcal Q_{\infty,\leqslant\lambda_\infty}^{\mathscr{S}}$, and for this it suffices to show that, for $p\in\mathcal Q_\infty^{\mathscr{S}}\setminus\mathcal Q_{\infty,\leqslant\lambda_\infty}^{\mathscr{S}}$, the infimum over $q'$ in~\eqref{e.Hopf_spin_glass} equals $-\infty$. By the endpoint convention~\eqref{e.continuous_endpoint_convention}, such a path has a coordinate $s\in\mathscr{S}$ and a point $r_0\in[0,1)$ with $p^s(r_0)>\lambda_{\infty,s}$, so that, by monotonicity,
\begin{equation*}
    \int_{r_0}^1\left(p^s(v)-\lambda_{\infty,s}\right)\mathrm{d} v>0.
\end{equation*}
For $a>0$, let $q'_a\in\mathcal Q_\infty^{\mathscr{S}}$ have $s$-component $a\mathds{1}_{[r_0,1)}$ and all other components equal to zero. Since $\psi$ is convex, with derivative $\partial_q\psi(q'_a)$ at $q'_a$ by~\eqref{e.psi_quadratic_remainder}, we have $\psi(0)\geqslant\psi(q'_a)-\left\langle q'_a,\partial_q\psi(q'_a)\right\rangle_{L^2}$, and the bound $\partial_q\psi(q'_a)\in\mathcal Q^{\mathscr{S}}_{\infty,\leqslant\lambda_\infty}$ in~\eqref{e.bound_derivative_spherical_psi} gives $\left\langle q'_a,\partial_q\psi(q'_a)\right\rangle_{L^2}\leqslant a\lambda_{\infty,s}(1-r_0)$. Therefore
\begin{equation*}
    \mathcal J_{t,q}(q'_a,p)\leqslant\psi(0)-a\int_{r_0}^1\left(p^s(v)-\lambda_{\infty,s}\right)\mathrm{d} v+\left\langle q,p\right\rangle_{L^2}+t\int_0^1\xi(p(r))\mathrm{d} r
    \xrightarrow[a\to\infty]{}-\infty.
\end{equation*}
Hence such paths $p$ do not contribute to the supremum, and the second equality in~\eqref{e.Hopf_spin_glass} follows.
<!-- end proof-43 -->
<!-- proposition-8: body_md -->
\label{p.HJ_bdd_spherical}
Let $f$ be the viscosity solution of Theorem~\ref{t.vis_sol}. Then, for every $(t,q)\in\mathbb{R}_+\times\mathcal Q_2^{\mathscr{S}}$,
\begin{equation}
\label{e.HJ_lower_spherical}
    f(t,q)\leqslant\liminf_{N\to\infty}\overline F_N(t,q).
\end{equation}
<!-- end proposition-8 -->
<!-- proof-44: body_md -->
The lower bound is an application of~\cite[Theorem~4.14]{chen2022hamilton}, which is a restatement of~\cite[Theorem~3.4]{mourrat2023free}. This result concerns vector spin glasses in which the reference measure is an arbitrary probability measure supported in the closed ball of radius $\sqrt N$ of $(\mathbb{R}^N)^D$, for some $D\in\mathbb{N}$; in particular, no product structure of the reference measure is required, so that the spherical constraint is allowed. We first embed the spherical model into this setting, then verify the hypotheses of the theorem, and finally identify the solution of the matrix-valued equation appearing in its conclusion with $f$ along diagonal paths.

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{Step 1: Embedding.}\par
Let $D:=|\mathscr{S}|$, and, as in~\cite[Section~6.2]{mourrat2023free}, associate with $\sigma\in\Sigma_N$ the vector-spin configuration $\widehat\sigma=(\widehat\sigma^s)_{s\in\mathscr{S}}\in(\mathbb{R}^N)^{\mathscr{S}}$ defined by
\begin{equation*}
    \widehat\sigma^s_i:=\sigma_i\mathds{1}_{\{i\in I_{N,s}\}},
    \qquad i\in[N],\quad s\in\mathscr{S}.
\end{equation*}
Then, for $\sigma,\sigma'\in\Sigma_N$,
\begin{equation*}
    \frac1N\widehat\sigma^s\cdot\widehat\sigma'^{s'}=R_{N,s}(\sigma,\sigma')\mathds{1}_{\{s=s'\}},
    \qquad\text{and}\qquad
    \sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}|\widehat\sigma^s|^2=N.
\end{equation*}
In other words, the overlap matrix $(\frac1N\widehat\sigma^s\cdot\widehat\sigma'^{s'})_{s,s'\in\mathscr{S}}$ is the diagonal matrix with diagonal $R_N(\sigma,\sigma')$, and the embedded configurations lie on the sphere of radius $\sqrt N$ of $(\mathbb{R}^N)^{\mathscr{S}}$. We absorb the external field into the reference measure: let $P_N^h$ be the probability measure on $\Sigma_N$ defined by
\begin{equation*}
    \mathrm{d} P_N^h(\sigma):=\exp\left(N\overline F_N(0,0)+\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}h^s\sum_{i\in I_{N,s}}\sigma_i\right)\mathrm{d} P_N(\sigma),
\end{equation*}
which is indeed a probability measure by~\eqref{e.def.FN.delta0} at $t=0$. The reference measure of the vector-spin model is the image of $P_N^h$ under the embedding.

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{Step 2: Covariance function and free energy.}\par
For a matrix $A\in\mathbb{R}^{\mathscr{S}\times\mathscr{S}}$, we set $\Xi(A):=\xi((A_{ss})_{s\in\mathscr{S}})$, which is well defined since the series~\eqref{e.xi_power_series_def} converges on all of $\mathbb{R}^{\mathscr{S}}$. The function $\Xi$ is smooth, hence locally Lipschitz, and it is proper on the cone of positive semidefinite matrices in the sense of~\cite[Definition~4.2]{chen2022hamilton}: the diagonal entries of a positive semidefinite matrix are nonnegative, and if $B-A$ is positive semidefinite, then $A_{ss}\leqslant B_{ss}$ for every $s\in\mathscr{S}$, so that the properness of $\xi$ on $\mathbb{R}_+^{\mathscr{S}}$, shown after Definition~\ref{d.regularization}, transfers to $\Xi$. The setting of~\cite{chen2022hamilton} requires a centered Gaussian field indexed by all of $(\mathbb{R}^N)^{\mathscr{S}}$, with covariance $N\Xi$ evaluated at the overlap matrix, that is, $N\xi((\frac1N\widehat\sigma^s\cdot\widehat\sigma'^s)_{s\in\mathscr{S}})$. Such a field exists: each kernel $(\widehat\sigma,\widehat\sigma')\mapsto\widehat\sigma^s\cdot\widehat\sigma'^s$ is nonnegative definite, hence so is every monomial $\prod_s(\widehat\sigma^s\cdot\widehat\sigma'^s)^{k_s}$ by the Schur product theorem, and the covariance is a convergent sum of such monomials with the nonnegative coefficients of~\eqref{e.xi_power_series_def}. On the embedded configurations, this field has the same law as $H_N$, by~\eqref{e.def_H_N}. Likewise, the external field of~\cite{chen2022hamilton} associated with a bounded matrix-valued path $\boldsymbol q$, nondecreasing for the positive semidefinite order, has covariance $\sum_{s,s'\in\mathscr{S}}\boldsymbol q_{ss'}(\alpha\wedge\alpha')\,\widehat\sigma^s\cdot\widehat\sigma'^{s'}$; on the embedded configurations, only the diagonal $\operatorname{\mathsf{diag}}\boldsymbol q:=(\boldsymbol q_{ss})_{s\in\mathscr{S}}$ contributes, and the field has the law of $W_N^{\operatorname{\mathsf{diag}}\boldsymbol q}$ in~\eqref{e.WNq_covariance}. Note that $\operatorname{\mathsf{diag}}\boldsymbol q\in\mathcal Q_\infty^{\mathscr{S}}$, since the diagonal entries of a nondecreasing path of positive semidefinite matrices are nonnegative and nondecreasing. Conversely, for an $\mathbb{R}^{\mathscr{S}}$-valued path $p$, we write $\operatorname{\mathsf{diag}}(p)$ for the path of diagonal matrices with diagonal $p$. Finally, the deterministic centerings of~\cite{chen2022hamilton} are $Nt\,\Xi$ evaluated at the self-overlap matrix, which is $Nt\xi(\lambda_N)$ since $R_N(\sigma,\sigma)=\lambda_N$, and $\sum_{s,s'}\boldsymbol q_{ss'}(1)\widehat\sigma^s\cdot\widehat\sigma^{s'}=N\,\operatorname{\mathsf{diag}}\boldsymbol q(1)\cdot\lambda_N$. Comparing with~\eqref{e.enriched_H}, we conclude that the free energy of~\cite{chen2022hamilton} for the embedded model, with reference measure $P_N^h$, at time $t$ and path $\boldsymbol q$, is
\begin{equation}
\label{e.matrix_free_energy_diagonal}
    \overline F_N(t,\operatorname{\mathsf{diag}}\boldsymbol q)-\overline F_N(0,0).
\end{equation}
This identity extends from bounded to square-integrable matrix paths, since both sides are continuous for the $L^1$ norm; see~\eqref{e.F_N_Lipschitz} for the right-hand side.

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{Step 3: Initial condition and matrix-valued solution.}\par
By~\eqref{e.matrix_free_energy_diagonal} and Proposition~\ref{l.initial_condition}, the initial condition of the embedded model converges: for every square-integrable matrix path $\boldsymbol q$ as above,
\begin{equation*}
    \lim_{N\to\infty}\left(\overline F_N(0,\operatorname{\mathsf{diag}}\boldsymbol q)-\overline F_N(0,0)\right)=\boldsymbol\psi(\boldsymbol q):=\psi(\operatorname{\mathsf{diag}}\boldsymbol q)-\psi(0).
\end{equation*}
The function $\boldsymbol\psi$ is convex, since $\psi$ is convex and $\boldsymbol q\mapsto\operatorname{\mathsf{diag}}\boldsymbol q$ is linear.
