It also satisfies the hypotheses of~\cite[Theorem~4.7]{chen2022hamilton}: it is $1$-Lipschitz for the $L^1$ norm, by~\eqref{e.psi_lambda_lipschitz} and since $\left|\operatorname{\mathsf{diag}} A\right|\leqslant|A|$ for the Frobenius norm; and it is increasing for the dual of the matrix cone, since if $\boldsymbol q-\boldsymbol q'$ belongs to this dual cone, then testing against the diagonal paths $\operatorname{\mathsf{diag}}(p)$ with $p\in\mathcal Q_2^{\mathscr{S}}$, which belong to the matrix cone, shows that $\operatorname{\mathsf{diag}}\boldsymbol q-\operatorname{\mathsf{diag}}\boldsymbol q'\in(\mathcal Q_2^{\mathscr{S}})^*$, and Lemma~\ref{l.dual_cone_monotone} gives $\psi(\operatorname{\mathsf{diag}}\boldsymbol q)\geqslant\psi(\operatorname{\mathsf{diag}}\boldsymbol q')$. Let $\boldsymbol f$ be the unique Lipschitz viscosity solution of the matrix-valued Hamilton--Jacobi equation with nonlinearity $\Xi$ and initial condition $\boldsymbol\psi$, given by~\cite[Theorem~4.7]{chen2022hamilton}. Since $\boldsymbol\psi$ is convex, the same theorem gives the Hopf formula
\begin{equation}
\label{e.matrix_Hopf}
    \boldsymbol f(t,\boldsymbol q)=\sup_{\boldsymbol p}\inf_{\boldsymbol q'}\left\{\boldsymbol\psi(\boldsymbol q')+\left\langle\boldsymbol q-\boldsymbol q',\boldsymbol p\right\rangle+t\int_0^1\Xi(\boldsymbol p(r))\mathrm{d} r\right\},
\end{equation}
where $\boldsymbol p$ and $\boldsymbol q'$ range over bounded paths that are nondecreasing for the positive semidefinite order, and $\left\langle\cdot,\cdot\right\rangle$ is the $L^2$ pairing associated with the Frobenius inner product.

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{Step 4: Identification along diagonal paths.}\par
We claim that, for every $q\in\mathcal Q_\infty^{\mathscr{S}}$,
\begin{equation}
\label{e.matrix_diagonal_identification}
    \boldsymbol f(t,\operatorname{\mathsf{diag}}(q))=f(t,q)-\psi(0).
\end{equation}
The restriction of a viscosity solution to a subcone is not, in general, a viscosity solution of the restricted equation, so we argue through the two Hopf formulas. Let $\boldsymbol q:=\operatorname{\mathsf{diag}}(q)$. For every admissible $\boldsymbol p$, the path $p:=\operatorname{\mathsf{diag}}\boldsymbol p$ belongs to $\mathcal Q_\infty^{\mathscr{S}}$, and restricting the infimum in~\eqref{e.matrix_Hopf} to the diagonal paths $\boldsymbol q'=\operatorname{\mathsf{diag}}(q')$ with $q'\in\mathcal Q_\infty^{\mathscr{S}}$, for which $\left\langle\boldsymbol q-\boldsymbol q',\boldsymbol p\right\rangle=\left\langle q-q',p\right\rangle_{L^2}$ and $\Xi(\boldsymbol p)=\xi(p)$, gives
\begin{equation*}
    \inf_{\boldsymbol q'}\left\{\boldsymbol\psi(\boldsymbol q')+\left\langle\boldsymbol q-\boldsymbol q',\boldsymbol p\right\rangle+t\int_0^1\Xi(\boldsymbol p(r))\mathrm{d} r\right\}\leqslant\inf_{q'\in\mathcal Q_\infty^{\mathscr{S}}}\mathcal J_{t,q}(q',p)-\psi(0)\leqslant f(t,q)-\psi(0),
\end{equation*}
by~\eqref{e.Hopf_spin_glass}. Taking the supremum over $\boldsymbol p$ proves that $\boldsymbol f(t,\operatorname{\mathsf{diag}}(q))\leqslant f(t,q)-\psi(0)$. Conversely, we restrict the supremum in~\eqref{e.matrix_Hopf} to the diagonal paths $\boldsymbol p=\operatorname{\mathsf{diag}}(p)$ with $p\in\mathcal Q_\infty^{\mathscr{S}}$. For such paths, $\left\langle\boldsymbol q-\boldsymbol q',\boldsymbol p\right\rangle=\left\langle q-\operatorname{\mathsf{diag}}\boldsymbol q',p\right\rangle_{L^2}$ and $\Xi(\boldsymbol p)=\xi(p)$, so that every term in the braces depends on $\boldsymbol q'$ only through $\operatorname{\mathsf{diag}}\boldsymbol q'$, which ranges over all of $\mathcal Q_\infty^{\mathscr{S}}$ as $\boldsymbol q'$ varies. The infimum over $\boldsymbol q'$ is therefore $\inf_{q'\in\mathcal Q_\infty^{\mathscr{S}}}\mathcal J_{t,q}(q',p)-\psi(0)$, and taking the supremum over $p$ gives $\boldsymbol f(t,\operatorname{\mathsf{diag}}(q))\geqslant f(t,q)-\psi(0)$, again by~\eqref{e.Hopf_spin_glass}. This proves~\eqref{e.matrix_diagonal_identification}.

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{Step 5: Conclusion.}\par
Let $q\in\mathcal Q_\infty^{\mathscr{S}}$. By Steps~1 to~3, the embedded model satisfies the hypotheses of~\cite[Theorem~4.14]{chen2022hamilton}, and the conclusion of this theorem at the path $\operatorname{\mathsf{diag}}(q)$ reads, by~\eqref{e.matrix_free_energy_diagonal} and~\eqref{e.matrix_diagonal_identification},
\begin{equation*}
    f(t,q)-\psi(0)=\boldsymbol f(t,\operatorname{\mathsf{diag}}(q))\leqslant\liminf_{N\to\infty}\left(\overline F_N(t,q)-\overline F_N(0,0)\right)=\liminf_{N\to\infty}\overline F_N(t,q)-\psi(0),
\end{equation*}
where we used~\eqref{e.initial_condition_limit} at $q=0$ in the last step. This proves~\eqref{e.HJ_lower_spherical} for bounded $q$. For $q\in\mathcal Q_2^{\mathscr{S}}$, set $q_m^s:=q^s\wedge m$ for every $s\in\mathscr{S}$ and $m\in\mathbb{N}$. Then $q_m\in\mathcal Q_\infty^{\mathscr{S}}$ and $|q_m-q|_{L^1}\to0$ as $m\to\infty$. The estimates~\eqref{e.f_L1_lipschitz} and~\eqref{e.F_N_Lipschitz} give
\begin{equation*}
    f(t,q)\leqslant f(t,q_m)+|q_m-q|_{L^1}\leqslant\liminf_{N\to\infty}\overline F_N(t,q)+2|q_m-q|_{L^1},
\end{equation*}
and letting $m\to\infty$ proves~\eqref{e.HJ_lower_spherical}.
<!-- end proof-44 -->
<!-- corollary-2: body_md -->
\label{c.rational_identification}
Assume that $\lambda_\infty\in\mathbb{Q}^{\mathscr{S}}$, and let $M$ and the sequence of sizes~\eqref{e.compatible_sequence} be as in Proposition~\ref{p.crit_pt_bdd_spherical}. Let $f$ be the viscosity solution of Theorem~\ref{t.vis_sol}. For every $t>0$ and $q\in\mathcal Q_\infty^{\mathscr{S}}$, we have
\begin{equation}
\label{e.rational_identification}
    \lim_{n\to\infty}\overline F_{N_n}(t,q)=f(t,q).
\end{equation}
<!-- end corollary-2 -->
<!-- proof-45: body_md -->
\noindent\emph{Step 1: Regular paths.}\par
Let $q\in\mathcal Q_{\infty,\uparrow}^{\mathscr{S}}$. Propositions~\ref{p.HJ_bdd_spherical} and~\ref{p.crit_pt_bdd_spherical} being now proved, the chain~\eqref{e.identification_chain} holds, with $f(t,q)$ equal to the right-hand side of~\eqref{e.main.1} by the Hopf formula~\eqref{e.Hopf_spin_glass}. This proves~\eqref{e.rational_identification} for $q\in\mathcal Q_{\infty,\uparrow}^{\mathscr{S}}$.

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{Step 2: Bounded paths.}\par
Let $q\in\mathcal Q_\infty^{\mathscr{S}}$, and, for every integer $m\geqslant1$, define $q_m$ by
\begin{equation*}
    q_m^s(u):=q^s(u)\wedge(mu)+\frac um,
    \qquad u\in[0,1),\quad s\in\mathscr{S}.
\end{equation*}
Each component of $q_m$ is right-continuous, bounded by $|q|_{L^\infty}+1$, vanishes at $0$, and satisfies $q_m^s(v)-q_m^s(u)\geqslant(v-u)/m$ for $0\leqslant u\leqslant v<1$, so $q_m\in\mathcal Q_{\infty,\uparrow}^{\mathscr{S}}$. Moreover, $q^s(u)\wedge(mu)$ and $q^s(u)$ both belong to $[0,|q|_{L^\infty}]$, and they coincide for $u\geqslant|q|_{L^\infty}/m$, so that
\begin{equation*}
    |q_m-q|_{L^1}\leqslant\frac{|\mathscr{S}|}{m}\left(|q|_{L^\infty}^2+1\right)\xrightarrow[m\to\infty]{}0.
\end{equation*}
Both $\overline F_{N_n}(t,\cdot)$ and $f(t,\cdot)$ are $1$-Lipschitz for the $L^1$ norm, by~\eqref{e.F_N_Lipschitz} and~\eqref{e.f_L1_lipschitz}. Hence, by Step~1,
\begin{equation*}
    \limsup_{n\to\infty}\left|\overline F_{N_n}(t,q)-f(t,q)\right|\leqslant2|q_m-q|_{L^1}+\limsup_{n\to\infty}\left|\overline F_{N_n}(t,q_m)-f(t,q_m)\right|=2|q_m-q|_{L^1},
\end{equation*}
and letting $m\to\infty$ proves~\eqref{e.rational_identification}.
<!-- end proof-45 -->
<!-- lemma-34: body_md -->
\label{l.one_coordinate_comparison}
There exists a constant $C<\infty$, depending only on $\xi$ and~$h$, such that, for every integer vector $\mathbf n$ with positive entries, $s\in\mathscr{S}$, $t\geqslant0$, and $q\in\mathcal Q_\infty^{\mathscr{S}}$,
\begin{gather}
\label{e.log_partition_uniform_bound}
    \left|\mathbb{E}\log Z_{\mathbf n}(t,q)\right|\leqslant C|\mathbf n|_1\left(1+t+|q|_{L^\infty}\right),\\
\label{e.one_coordinate_log_partition}
    \left|\mathbb{E}\log Z_{\mathbf n+e_s}(t,q)-\mathbb{E}\log Z_{\mathbf n}(t,q)\right|\leqslant C\left(1+t+|q|_{L^\infty}\right).
\end{gather}
<!-- end lemma-34 -->
<!-- proof-46: body_md -->
Write $K:=|\mathbf n|_1$ and $\lambda:=\mathbf n/K$, and let $(I_{K,u})_{u\in\mathscr{S}}$ denote the species partition of the system with $n_u$ coordinates in species $u$. We first prove~\eqref{e.log_partition_uniform_bound}. By~\eqref{e.F_N_Lipschitz}, we have $|\overline F_{\mathbf n}(t,q)-\overline F_{\mathbf n}(0,0)|\leqslant|q|_{L^1}+t\sup_{[-1,1]^{\mathscr{S}}}|\xi|$. Moreover, $|\overline F_{\mathbf n}(0,0)|\leqslant\max_u|h^u|$, since $|\sum_uh^u\sum_{i\in I_{K,u}}\sigma_i|\leqslant K\max_u|h^u|$ on $\Sigma_K$, by the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality. Since $\mathbb{E}\log Z_{\mathbf n}=-K\overline F_{\mathbf n}$ and $|q|_{L^1}\leqslant|q|_{L^\infty}$, this proves~\eqref{e.log_partition_uniform_bound}.

We now turn to~\eqref{e.one_coordinate_log_partition}. The larger system has size $K+1$ and proportions $\lambda':=(\mathbf n+e_s)/(K+1)$. We apply the disintegration~\eqref{e.block_disintegration} with $m=1$ and $n=n_s$ to the species-$s$ sphere of the larger system, leaving the spheres of the other species unchanged: writing $\tau\in\mathcal B_{1,n_s}$ for the added coordinate, $r^s(\tau):=1+(1-\tau^2)/n_s$, and $r^u(\tau):=1$ for $u\ne s$, a configuration of the larger system is $(S_{r(\tau)}\sigma,\tau)$ with $\sigma\in\Sigma_K$, and its reference measure is $p_{1,n_s}(\tau)\mathrm{d}\tau\,P_K(\mathrm{d}\sigma)$. This is the chart of Subsection~\ref{s.spherical_chart} for a cavity block consisting of one coordinate of species $s$, and we follow Steps~1 and~2 of the proof of Lemma~\ref{l.fixed_block_increment_bound}, with $x=y=0$. By~\eqref{e.overlap_dilation}, the analogue of~\eqref{e.full_and_bulk_overlap_identity} holds, and since $n_s|r^s(\tau)-1|\leqslant1+\tau^2$ and $K|R_{K,s}(\sigma,\sigma')|\leqslant n_s$, the analogue of~\eqref{e.full_and_bulk_overlap_bound} reads
\begin{equation*}
    (K+1)\left|R_{K+1}\left((S_{r(\tau)}\sigma,\tau),(S_{r(\tau')}\sigma',\tau')\right)-R_K(\sigma,\sigma')\right|\leqslant C\left(1+\tau^2+\tau'^2\right),
\end{equation*}
for a constant $C$ depending only on $|\mathscr{S}|$. We compare the enriched Hamiltonians~\eqref{e.enriched_H} of the two systems, viewed as Gaussian fields indexed by $(\sigma,\alpha,\tau)$; recall that their means and covariances depend on the configurations only through the overlaps and the sums $\sum_{i\in I_{K,u}}\sigma_i$. Both overlap vectors lie in the overlap domain $[-1,1]^{\mathscr{S}}$, on which $\xi$ is Lipschitz, so the covariance $(K+1)\xi(R_{K+1})$ of the interaction field of the larger system differs from the covariance $K\xi(R_K)$ of the smaller one by at most $C(1+\tau^2+\tau'^2)$; and the deterministic centerings $-(K+1)t\xi(\lambda')$ and $-Kt\xi(\lambda)$ differ by at most $Ct$, since $|\lambda'-\lambda|\leqslant2/K$ and $\xi$ is Lipschitz on $[0,1]^{\mathscr{S}}$. For the cascade field, the covariance of $\sqrt2W^q_{K+1}$ in~\eqref{e.WNq_covariance} is $2\sum_{u\in\mathscr{S}}q^u(\alpha\wedge\alpha')(K+1)R_{K+1,u}$, which differs from the covariance of $\sqrt2W_K^q$ by at most $2|q|_{L^\infty}\sum_u|(K+1)R_{K+1,u}-KR_{K,u}|\leqslant C|q|_{L^\infty}(1+\tau^2+\tau'^2)$, while the self-overlap corrections $-(K+1)q(1)\cdot\lambda'$ and $-Kq(1)\cdot\lambda$ differ by the constant $q^s(1)$. The external-field terms differ by at most $C(1+\tau^2)$, as in~\eqref{e.frozen_chart_mean_bound}. Altogether, the means and covariances of the two Hamiltonians differ by at most $C(1+t+|q|_{L^\infty})(1+\tau^2+\tau'^2)$.

We now apply Lemma~\ref{l.quadratically_confined_Gaussian_comparison} with $M=1$, $\mathbb X^0:=\Sigma_K\times\mathfrak U$, $\mu^0:=P_K\otimes\mathfrak{R}$, $B:=\mathcal B_{1,n_s}$, $\nu:=p_{1,n_s}(\tau)\mathrm{d}\tau$, and $C_0:=C(1+t+|q|_{L^\infty})$. The set $\mathcal B_{1,n_s}$ is bounded, $\nu$ is a probability measure on it, and $\int\tau^2p_{1,n_s}(\tau)\mathrm{d}\tau=1$ by~\eqref{e.block_disintegration}, since each coordinate of a point of $\mathbb{S}_{n_s+1}$ has second moment $1$ under the uniform measure. The condition~\eqref{e.quadratic_comparison_second_moments} holds for the same reason as in the proof of Lemma~\ref{l.fixed_block_increment_bound}: the law of the Hamiltonian of the larger system is invariant under permutations of the coordinates within species $s$, and $\sum_{i\in I_{K+1,s}}\rho_i^2=n_s+1$ on its configuration space, so that $\mathbb{E}\left\langle\tau^2\right\rangle_{\mathbf n+e_s}=1$, where $\left\langle\cdot\right\rangle_{\mathbf n+e_s}$ denotes the Gibbs bracket associated with $Z_{\mathbf n+e_s}(t,q)$. The lemma yields~\eqref{e.one_coordinate_log_partition}.
<!-- end proof-46 -->
<!-- lemma-35: body_md -->
\label{l.finite_size_comparison}
There exists a constant $C<\infty$, depending only on $\xi$ and $h$, such that the following holds. Let $N,N'\in\mathbb{N}$ satisfy $N\leqslant N'\leqslant2N$, and let $\lambda,\lambda'$ be probability vectors such that $N\lambda_s,N'\lambda'_s\in\mathbb{N}$ for every $s\in\mathscr{S}$. For every $t\geqslant0$ and $q\in\mathcal Q_\infty^{\mathscr{S}}$, we have
\begin{equation}
    \left|\overline F_{N,\lambda}(t,q)-\overline F_{N',\lambda'}(t,q)\right|\leqslant C\left(1+t+|q|_{L^\infty}\right)\left(|\lambda-\lambda'|+\frac{N'-N}{N}\right).
    \label{e.finite_size_comparison}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-35 -->
<!-- proof-47: body_md -->
We first translate the comparison of $\mathbb{E}\log Z_{\mathbf n}$ in Lemma~\ref{l.one_coordinate_comparison} into a comparison of free energies. Let $\mathbf n$ be an integer vector with positive entries, and let $s\in\mathscr{S}$. Since $\overline F_{\mathbf n}(t,q)=-|\mathbf n|_1^{-1}\mathbb{E}\log Z_{\mathbf n}(t,q)$, we can write
\begin{equation*}
    \overline F_{\mathbf n+e_s}(t,q)-\overline F_{\mathbf n}(t,q)=\left(\frac1{|\mathbf n|_1}-\frac1{|\mathbf n|_1+1}\right)\mathbb{E}\log Z_{\mathbf n+e_s}(t,q)-\frac{1}{|\mathbf n|_1}\left(\mathbb{E}\log Z_{\mathbf n+e_s}(t,q)-\mathbb{E}\log Z_{\mathbf n}(t,q)\right).
\end{equation*}
By the two estimates of Lemma~\ref{l.one_coordinate_comparison}, the first term is bounded by $C(1+t+|q|_{L^\infty})/|\mathbf n|_1$ in absolute value, and so is the second. Hence
\begin{equation}
    \left|\overline F_{\mathbf n+e_s}(t,q)-\overline F_{\mathbf n}(t,q)\right|\leqslant\frac{C}{|\mathbf n|_1}\left(1+t+|q|_{L^\infty}\right),
    \qquad t\geqslant0,\quad q\in\mathcal Q_\infty^{\mathscr{S}},
    \label{e.one_coordinate_free_energy_comparison}
\end{equation}
for a constant $C$ depending only on $\xi$ and $h$.

We now prove~\eqref{e.finite_size_comparison}. Put $\mathbf n:=(N\lambda_s)_{s\in\mathscr{S}}$ and $\mathbf n':=(N'\lambda'_s)_{s\in\mathscr{S}}$, and choose integer vectors $\mathbf m_0,\ldots,\mathbf m_d$ with $\mathbf m_0=\mathbf n$, $\mathbf m_d=\mathbf n'$, and $\mathbf m_{j+1}-\mathbf m_j\in\{e_s,-e_s:s\in\mathscr{S}\}$ for every $j<d$, such that each coordinate moves monotonically from $n_s$ to $n'_s$ along the path, and such that all the increments $+e_s$ come before all the decrements $-e_s$. Then
\begin{equation*}
    d=\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}|N'\lambda'_s-N\lambda_s|\leqslant N'\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}|\lambda'_s-\lambda_s|+(N'-N)\leqslant CN\left(|\lambda-\lambda'|+\frac{N'-N}{N}\right).
\end{equation*}
Moreover, for every $j$ and $s$, the coordinate $(\mathbf m_j)_s$ lies between $n_s$ and $n'_s$, and is therefore positive; and since $|\mathbf m_j|_1$ first increases from $N$ and then decreases to $N'\geqslant N$, we have $|\mathbf m_j|_1\geqslant N$ for every $j$. The estimate~\eqref{e.one_coordinate_free_energy_comparison} applies to each pair $(\mathbf m_j,\mathbf m_{j+1})$, possibly after exchanging the roles of $\mathbf n$ and $\mathbf n+e_s$ there. Summing over $j\in\{0,\ldots,d-1\}$ gives
\begin{equation*}
    \left|\overline F_{\mathbf n'}(t,q)-\overline F_{\mathbf n}(t,q)\right|\leqslant\frac{Cd}{N}\left(1+t+|q|_{L^\infty}\right),
\end{equation*}
and the bound on $d$ proves~\eqref{e.finite_size_comparison}.
<!-- end proof-47 -->
<!-- lemma-36: body_md -->
\label{l.hopf_normalized}
For every probability vector $\lambda$ with positive entries, $t\geqslant0$, and $q\in\mathcal Q_2^{\mathscr{S}}$, we have
\begin{equation}
\label{e.hopf_normalized}
\begin{gathered}
    f_\lambda(t,q)=\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}\lambda_s\psi_s(0)+\sup_{a\in(\mathcal Q_{\infty,\leqslant1})^{\mathscr{S}}}\left\{A_\lambda(a)-\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}\lambda_sc_s(a_s)\right\},\\
    \text{where}\qquad
    A_\lambda(a):=\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}\lambda_s\left\langle q^s,a_s\right\rangle_{L^2}+t\int_0^1\xi\left((\lambda_sa_s(r))_{s\in\mathscr{S}}\right)\mathrm{d} r.
\end{gathered}
\end{equation}
Moreover, for every $a\in(\mathcal Q_{\infty,\leqslant1})^{\mathscr{S}}$,
\begin{equation}
\label{e.A_lambda_bounds}
    0\leqslant A_\lambda(a)\leqslant C_{t,q}:=\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}|q^s|_{L^1}+t\sup_{v\in[0,1]^{\mathscr{S}}}\xi(v),
\end{equation}
and thus the supremum in~\eqref{e.hopf_normalized} belongs to $[0,C_{t,q}]$.
<!-- end lemma-36 -->
<!-- proof-48: body_md -->
The map $p\mapsto a:=(p^s/\lambda_s)_{s\in\mathscr{S}}$ is a bijection from $\mathcal Q^{\mathscr{S}}_{\infty,\leqslant\lambda}$ onto $(\mathcal Q_{\infty,\leqslant1})^{\mathscr{S}}$, and $\left\langle q',p\right\rangle_{L^2}=\sum_s\lambda_s\left\langle q'^s,a_s\right\rangle_{L^2}$ for every $q'\in\mathcal Q_\infty^{\mathscr{S}}$, while $\psi_\lambda(q')=\sum_s\lambda_s\psi_s(q'^s)$ by~\eqref{e.psi_lambda_def}. Since the components $q'^s$ of $q'\in\mathcal Q_\infty^{\mathscr{S}}$ vary independently in $\mathcal Q_\infty$, we have
\begin{equation*}
    \sup_{q'\in\mathcal Q_\infty^{\mathscr{S}}}\left\{\left\langle q',p\right\rangle_{L^2}-\psi_\lambda(q')\right\}=\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}\lambda_s\psi_s^*(a_s),
\end{equation*}
and therefore $\inf_{q'}\mathcal J^\lambda_{t,q}(q',p)=A_\lambda(a)-\sum_s\lambda_s\psi_s^*(a_s)$, so that, by~\eqref{e.f_lambda_def},
\begin{equation}
\label{e.hopf_inner_inf_computed}
    f_\lambda(t,q)=\sup_{a\in(\mathcal Q_{\infty,\leqslant1})^{\mathscr{S}}}\left\{A_\lambda(a)-\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}\lambda_s\psi_s^*(a_s)\right\};
\end{equation}
the conjugates are bounded below and $A_\lambda(a)$ is finite, so that no indeterminate expression appears. Inserting $\psi_s^*=c_s-\psi_s(0)$ gives~\eqref{e.hopf_normalized}. The bounds~\eqref{e.A_lambda_bounds} follow from $0\leqslant a_s\leqslant1$, $q^s\geqslant0$, $0\leqslant\lambda_s\leqslant1$, and the nonnegativity of $\xi$ on $[0,1]^{\mathscr{S}}$, which holds since its coefficients are nonnegative. Finally, since $c_s\geqslant0$, the expression in braces is at most $C_{t,q}$; and it vanishes at $a=0$, since $c_s(0)=0$ and $A_\lambda(0)=t\xi(0)=0$.
<!-- end proof-48 -->
<!-- lemma-37: body_md -->
\label{l.hopf_continuity_lambda}
Fix $\eta\in(0,1]$. There exists $C<\infty$, depending only on $\xi$, $h$, and $\eta$, such that, for every $\lambda,\lambda'\in\Lambda_\eta$, $t\geqslant0$, and $q\in\mathcal Q_2^{\mathscr{S}}$,
\begin{equation}
\label{e.hopf_continuity_lambda}
    |f_\lambda(t,q)-f_{\lambda'}(t,q)|\leqslant C\left(1+t+|q|_{L^1}\right)|\lambda-\lambda'|.
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-37 -->
<!-- proof-49: body_md -->
Fix $t$ and $q$, and let $\mathsf V_\lambda$ denote the supremum in~\eqref{e.hopf_normalized}. Let $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, and let $a\in(\mathcal Q_{\infty,\leqslant1})^{\mathscr{S}}$ satisfy $A_\lambda(a)-\sum_s\lambda_sc_s(a_s)\geqslant\mathsf V_\lambda-\varepsilon$. Since $\mathsf V_\lambda\geqslant0$ and $A_\lambda(a)\leqslant C_{t,q}$, we get $\sum_s\lambda_sc_s(a_s)\leqslant C_{t,q}+1$, hence $c_s(a_s)\leqslant(C_{t,q}+1)/\eta$ for every $s\in\mathscr{S}$, as $\lambda_s\geqslant\eta$. We now evaluate the same $a$ at $\lambda'$. Since $\xi$ is Lipschitz on $[0,1]^{\mathscr{S}}$, with a constant $L_\xi$ depending only on $\xi$, and since $|(\lambda_sa_s(r))_s-(\lambda'_sa_s(r))_s|\leqslant|\lambda-\lambda'|$ for every $r$, we have
\begin{equation*}
    |A_\lambda(a)-A_{\lambda'}(a)|\leqslant\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}|\lambda_s-\lambda'_s|\,|q^s|_{L^1}+tL_\xi|\lambda-\lambda'|
    \quad\text{and}\quad
    \Big|\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}(\lambda_s-\lambda'_s)c_s(a_s)\Big|\leqslant\frac{C_{t,q}+1}{\eta}\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}|\lambda_s-\lambda'_s|.
\end{equation*}
Using $\sum_s|x_s|\leqslant|\mathscr{S}|^{1/2}|x|$ for $x\in\mathbb{R}^{\mathscr{S}}$, and $\sum_s|q^s|_{L^1}\leqslant|\mathscr{S}|^{1/2}|q|_{L^1}$, we deduce that
\begin{equation*}
    \mathsf V_{\lambda'}\geqslant A_{\lambda'}(a)-\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}\lambda'_sc_s(a_s)\geqslant\mathsf V_\lambda-\varepsilon-C\left(1+t+|q|_{L^1}\right)|\lambda-\lambda'|,
\end{equation*}
for a constant $C$ depending only on $\xi$ and $\eta$. Exchanging the roles of $\lambda$ and $\lambda'$ and letting $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ bounds $|\mathsf V_\lambda-\mathsf V_{\lambda'}|$ by the last term. The first term in~\eqref{e.hopf_normalized} is Lipschitz in $\lambda$ with constant $\max_s|\psi_s(0)|$, and $\psi_s(0)=\psi^\circ_{h^s}(0)$ depends only on $h^s$. This proves~\eqref{e.hopf_continuity_lambda}.
<!-- end proof-49 -->
<!-- proof-50: body_md -->
Let $f=f_{\lambda_\infty}$ be the Lipschitz viscosity solution of~\eqref{e.main.hj} given by Theorem~\ref{t.vis_sol}. By~\eqref{e.Hopf_spin_glass}, $f(t,q)$ is the right-hand side of~\eqref{e.main.1}, so it remains to prove that $\overline F_N(t,q)$ converges to $f(t,q)$ for every $t\geqslant0$ and $q\in\mathcal Q_2^{\mathscr{S}}$. At $t=0$, this is the convergence of the initial condition in Proposition~\ref{l.initial_condition}: $\overline F_N(0,q)\to\psi(q)=f(0,q)$ for every $q\in\mathcal Q_2^{\mathscr{S}}$. We fix $t>0$ from now on.

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{Step 1: Bounded paths.}\par
Let $q\in\mathcal Q_\infty^{\mathscr{S}}$. Set $\eta:=\frac12\min_{s\in\mathscr{S}}\lambda_{\infty,s}>0$, and choose rational probability vectors $\lambda^{(m)}\in\Lambda_\eta\cap\mathbb{Q}^{\mathscr{S}}$, $m\in\mathbb{N}$, such that $\lambda^{(m)}\to\lambda_\infty$ as $m\to\infty$, together with integers $M_m\in\mathbb{N}$ such that $M_m\lambda^{(m)}_s\in\mathbb{N}$ for every $s\in\mathscr{S}$. Fix $m$. The systems of sizes $N\in M_m\mathbb{N}$ with proportions $\lambda^{(m)}$ form a model of the type considered in Section~\ref{s.introduction}, with the same $\xi$ and $h$, whose limiting proportions $\lambda^{(m)}$ are rational, and whose initial condition is $\psi_{\lambda^{(m)}}$; the sizes $N\notin M_m\mathbb{N}$ play no role, and can be assigned arbitrary proportions converging to $\lambda^{(m)}$. Corollary~\ref{c.rational_identification} applies to this model and gives
\begin{equation}
\label{e.rational_limit_m}
    \lim_{k\to\infty}\overline F_{kM_m,\lambda^{(m)}}(t,q)=f_{\lambda^{(m)}}(t,q).
\end{equation}
For $N\geqslant M_m$, let $K_N:=M_m\lfloor N/M_m\rfloor$, so that $N-M_m<K_N\leqslant N\leqslant2K_N$ and $K_N\lambda^{(m)}_s\in\mathbb{N}$ for every $s$. Lemma~\ref{l.finite_size_comparison}, applied with the sizes $K_N\leqslant N$ and the proportions $\lambda^{(m)}$ and $\lambda_N$, gives
\begin{equation*}
    \left|\overline F_N(t,q)-\overline F_{K_N,\lambda^{(m)}}(t,q)\right|\leqslant C\left(1+t+|q|_{L^\infty}\right)\left(|\lambda_N-\lambda^{(m)}|+\frac{M_m}{K_N}\right),
\end{equation*}
with $C$ depending only on $\xi$ and $h$. Letting $N\to\infty$ at fixed $m$, using~\eqref{e.rational_limit_m} and $\lambda_N\to\lambda_\infty$, and then applying Lemma~\ref{l.hopf_continuity_lambda} to $\lambda^{(m)},\lambda_\infty\in\Lambda_\eta$, we obtain, since $|q|_{L^1}\leqslant|q|_{L^\infty}$,
\begin{equation*}
    \limsup_{N\to\infty}\left|\overline F_N(t,q)-f(t,q)\right|\leqslant C\left(1+t+|q|_{L^\infty}\right)|\lambda^{(m)}-\lambda_\infty|,
\end{equation*}
with $C$ depending only on $\xi$, $h$, and $\eta$.
Letting $m\to\infty$ proves that $\overline F_N(t,q)\to f(t,q)$.

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{Step 2: General paths.}\par
Let $q\in\mathcal Q_2^{\mathscr{S}}$, and set $q_j^s:=q^s\wedge j$ for $j\in\mathbb{N}$ and $s\in\mathscr{S}$, so that $q_j\in\mathcal Q_\infty^{\mathscr{S}}$ and $|q_j-q|_{L^1}\to0$ as $j\to\infty$, by monotone convergence. By~\eqref{e.F_N_Lipschitz}, \eqref{e.f_L1_lipschitz}, and Step~1,
\begin{equation*}
    \limsup_{N\to\infty}\left|\overline F_N(t,q)-f(t,q)\right|\leqslant2|q_j-q|_{L^1}+\limsup_{N\to\infty}\left|\overline F_N(t,q_j)-f(t,q_j)\right|=2|q_j-q|_{L^1}.
\end{equation*}
Letting $j\to\infty$ completes the proof.
<!-- end proof-50 -->
<!-- definition-3: body_md -->
\label{d.balanced_comparison_structure}
We say that $\xi$ is balanced with respect to $\lambda$ if
\begin{equation}
\label{e.balanced_inequality}
    \xi\left((\lambda_sx_s)_{s\in\mathscr{S}}\right)\leqslant\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}\lambda_s\,\xi_\star(x_s),
    \qquad x=(x_s)_{s\in\mathscr{S}}\in[0,1]^{\mathscr{S}}.
\end{equation}
<!-- end definition-3 -->
<!-- proposition-9: body_md -->
\label{p.balanced_reduction}
Assume that $h^s=h_\star$ for every $s\in\mathscr{S}$ and that $\xi$ is balanced with respect to $\lambda$. Let $f$ be the limit free energy in Theorem~\ref{t.main}. For every $t\geqslant0$ and $q\in\mathcal Q_2^{\mathscr{S}}$, we have
\begin{equation}
\label{e.balanced_comparison}
    u(t,\overline q)\leqslant f(t,q)\leqslant\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}\lambda_su(t,q^s).
\end{equation}
In particular, if $q^s=\rho$ for every $s\in\mathscr{S}$, for some $\rho\in\mathcal Q_2$, then $f(t,q)=u(t,\rho)$. Moreover, the first inequality in~\eqref{e.balanced_comparison} holds even if $\xi$ is not balanced.
<!-- end proposition-9 -->
<!-- proof-51: body_md -->
Since $h^s=h_\star$ for every $s\in\mathscr{S}$, the conjugate $\psi_s^*$ in~\eqref{e.psi_conjugate_def} does not depend on $s$: it is the conjugate of $\psi^\circ_\star$, and we denote it by $\psi_\star^*$. By Theorem~\ref{t.main} and~\eqref{e.hopf_inner_inf_computed} with $\lambda=\lambda_\infty$, and by the definition~\eqref{e.balanced_u_def} of $u$, we have, for every $\rho\in\mathcal Q_2$,
\begin{align}
\label{e.balanced_f_hopf}
    f(t,q)&=\sup_{a\in(\mathcal Q_{\infty,\leqslant1})^{\mathscr{S}}}\left\{\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}\lambda_s\left\langle q^s,a_s\right\rangle_{L^2}-\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}\lambda_s\psi_\star^*(a_s)+t\int_0^1\xi\left((\lambda_sa_s(v))_{s\in\mathscr{S}}\right)\mathrm{d} v\right\},
    \\
\label{e.balanced_u_hopf}
    u(t,\rho)&=\sup_{a\in\mathcal Q_{\infty,\leqslant1}}\left\{\left\langle\rho,a\right\rangle_{L^2}-\psi_\star^*(a)+t\int_0^1\xi_\star(a(v))\mathrm{d} v\right\}.
\end{align}
For the lower bound, we restrict the supremum in~\eqref{e.balanced_f_hopf} to the families with $a_s=a$ for every $s\in\mathscr{S}$, for some $a\in\mathcal Q_{\infty,\leqslant1}$. For such a family, the expression in braces in~\eqref{e.balanced_f_hopf} is that in~\eqref{e.balanced_u_hopf} with $\rho=\overline q$, since $\sum_s\lambda_s=1$ and $\xi(a(v)\lambda)=\xi_\star(a(v))$ by~\eqref{e.xi_star_def}. We thus have $f(t,q)\geqslant u(t,\overline q)$.

For the upper bound, let $a\in(\mathcal Q_{\infty,\leqslant1})^{\mathscr{S}}$. For every $v\in[0,1)$, the vector $(a_s(v))_{s\in\mathscr{S}}$ belongs to $[0,1]^{\mathscr{S}}$, so that~\eqref{e.balanced_inequality} gives $\xi((\lambda_sa_s(v))_{s\in\mathscr{S}})\leqslant\sum_s\lambda_s\xi_\star(a_s(v))$. The expression in braces in~\eqref{e.balanced_f_hopf} is therefore at most
\begin{equation*}
    \sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}\lambda_s\left\{\left\langle q^s,a_s\right\rangle_{L^2}-\psi_\star^*(a_s)+t\int_0^1\xi_\star(a_s(v))\mathrm{d} v\right\}\leqslant\sum_{s\in\mathscr{S}}\lambda_su(t,q^s),
\end{equation*}
by~\eqref{e.balanced_u_hopf}. Taking the supremum over $a$ proves the upper bound in~\eqref{e.balanced_comparison}.

Finally, if $q^s=\rho$ for every $s\in\mathscr{S}$, then $\overline q=\rho$ and $\sum_s\lambda_su(t,q^s)=u(t,\rho)$, so that both sides of~\eqref{e.balanced_comparison} are equal to $u(t,\rho)$.
<!-- end proof-51 -->
<!-- corollary-3: body_md -->
\label{c.balanced_one_species_formula}
Assume that $h^s=h_\star$ for every $s\in\mathscr{S}$ and that $\xi$ is balanced with respect to $\lambda$. Let $(H^\star_N(\sigma))_{\sigma\in\mathbb{R}^N}$ be a centered Gaussian field with covariance
\begin{equation*}
    \mathbb{E}\left[H^\star_N(\sigma)H^\star_N(\sigma')\right]=N\xi_\star\left(\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N\sigma_i\sigma_i'\right),
    \qquad\sigma,\sigma'\in\mathbb{R}^N,
\end{equation*}
and let
\begin{equation*}
    \overline F^\star_N(t):=-\frac1N\mathbb{E}\log\int_{\mathbb{S}_N}\exp\left(\sqrt{2t}\,H^\star_N(\sigma)-Nt\xi_\star(1)+h_\star\sum_{i=1}^N\sigma_i\right)\mu_N(\mathrm{d}\sigma)
\end{equation*}
be the free energy~\eqref{e.def.FN.delta0} of the one-species spherical model with covariance function $\xi_\star$ and external field $h_\star$. For every $t\geqslant0$, we have
\begin{equation}
\label{e.balanced_simple_formula}
    \lim_{N\to\infty}\overline F_N(t,0)=\lim_{N\to\infty}\overline F_N^\star(t)=\sup_{a\in\mathcal Q_{\infty,\leqslant1}}\ \inf_{\rho'\in\mathcal Q_\infty}\left\{\psi_\star^\circ(\rho')-\left\langle\rho',a\right\rangle_{L^2}+t\int_0^1\xi_\star(a(v))\mathrm{d} v\right\}.
\end{equation}
<!-- end corollary-3 -->
<!-- proof-52: body_md -->
The right-hand side of~\eqref{e.balanced_simple_formula} is $u(t,0)$, which is equal to $f(t,0)=\lim_N\overline F_N(t,0)$ by Proposition~\ref{p.balanced_reduction} applied with $q=0$ and Theorem~\ref{t.main}. As observed below~\eqref{e.balanced_u_def}, Theorem~\ref{t.main} applied to the one-species model shows that $\lim_N\overline F^\star_N(t)$ is also equal to $u(t,0)$.
<!-- end proof-52 -->
<!-- lemma-38: body_md -->
\label{l.tilted_invariance}
Let $X$ be admissible. Conditionally on $z_\emptyset$, the point processes
\begin{equation}
\label{e.tilted_invariance}
    \left(u_{\alpha_{|1}}e_{\alpha_{|1}},\ldots,u_{\alpha_{|k}}e_{\alpha_{|k}},\Omega_\alpha\right)_{\alpha\in\mathbb{N}^k}
    \qquad\text{and}\qquad
    \left(u_{\alpha_{|1}},\ldots,u_{\alpha_{|k}},\Omega'_\alpha\right)_{\alpha\in\mathbb{N}^k}
\end{equation}
on $(0,\infty)^k\times(\mathbb{R}^n)^{k+1}$ have the same law, the marks $(z'_\beta)_{\beta\in\mathcal A}$ in the second process being generated by~\eqref{e.tilted_node_law} independently of the weights. In particular, by~\eqref{e.tilt_factor_def}, conditionally on $z_\emptyset$,
\begin{equation}
\label{e.tilted_invariance_weights}
    \left(w_\alpha\exp\left(X(\Omega_\alpha)-X_0(z_\emptyset)\right),\Omega_\alpha\right)_{\alpha\in\mathbb{N}^k}
    \stackrel{\mathrm{d}}{=}
    \left(w_\alpha,\Omega'_\alpha\right)_{\alpha\in\mathbb{N}^k}
\end{equation}
as point processes on $(0,\infty)\times(\mathbb{R}^n)^{k+1}$, and $\sum_{\alpha\in\mathbb{N}^k}w_\alpha\exp(X(\Omega_\alpha))$ is almost surely finite.
<!-- end lemma-38 -->
<!-- proof-53: body_md -->
This is~\cite[Lemma~3]{pantal07}, for independent standard Gaussian marks and with the root mark $z_\emptyset$ frozen: the recursion~\eqref{e.tilted_recursion}, the laws~\eqref{e.tilted_node_law}, and the factors~\eqref{e.tilt_factor_def} are respectively (3.4), (3.6), and (3.7) there. The result is stated in~\cite{pantal07} under the assumption $\mathbb{E}\exp X(\Omega_\alpha)<\infty$, but its proof is an induction on the depth of the tree, in which the invariance of Poisson--Dirichlet point processes with i.i.d.\ marks, \cite[Lemma~2]{pantal07} or~\cite[Theorem~5.19]{HJbook}, is applied to the children of each node $\beta$ of depth $j-1$, conditionally on the marks of depth at most $j-1$, with the function $z\mapsto\exp(X_j(\Omega_\beta,z))$, whose moment of order $m_j$ is $\exp(m_jX_{j-1}(\Omega_\beta))$. It therefore only uses the finiteness of the conditional expectations in~\eqref{e.tilted_recursion}, that is, the admissibility of $X$. The last assertion follows from~\eqref{e.tilt_factor_def} and from the almost sure finiteness of $\sum_\alpha w_\alpha$, \cite[Lemma~5.23]{HJbook}.
<!-- end proof-53 -->
<!-- corollary-4: body_md -->
\label{c.tilted_consequences}
Let $X$ be admissible. We have
\begin{equation}
\label{e.recursive_formula}
    \mathbb{E}\log\sum_{\alpha\in\mathbb{N}^k}v_\alpha\exp\left(X(\Omega_\alpha)\right)=X_{-1},
\end{equation}
and, for every bounded measurable $\Phi$ on $(\mathbb{R}^n)^{k+1}$,
\begin{equation}
\label{e.tilted_marks_one}
    \mathbb{E}\left\langle\Phi(\Omega_\alpha)\right\rangle_X=\int\Phi\,\mathrm{d}\mu_X.
\end{equation}
If moreover $k\geqslant1$ and $X_0(z_\emptyset)$ is square integrable, and if $S$ denotes the sum of the points of a Poisson--Dirichlet point process with parameter $m_1$, then $\operatorname{Var}(\log S)<\infty$ and
\begin{equation}
\label{e.variance_bound_general}
    \operatorname{Var}\left(\log\sum_{\alpha\in\mathbb{N}^k}v_\alpha\exp\left(X(\Omega_\alpha)\right)\right)\leqslant2\operatorname{Var}\left(X_0(z_\emptyset)\right)+4\operatorname{Var}(\log S).
\end{equation}
In words, under $\mathbb{E}\left\langle\cdot\right\rangle_X$, the marks along the sampled leaf have law $\mu_X$; and, apart from the contribution of the untilted root mark, the fluctuations of the tilted free energy are those of the weights at the first level, whatever the tilt.
<!-- end corollary-4 -->
<!-- proof-54: body_md -->
When $k=0$, the tree is reduced to its root, $v_\emptyset=1$, $\left\langle\Phi\right\rangle_X=\Phi(z_\emptyset)$, $\mu_X$ is the law of $z_\emptyset$, and $X_{-1}=\mathbb{E} X(z_\emptyset)$, so that~\eqref{e.recursive_formula} and~\eqref{e.tilted_marks_one} are immediate. Let $k\geqslant1$, and let $T:=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathbb{N}^k}w_\alpha$, which is independent of $z_\emptyset$. We first check that $T$ has the law of $cS$ for some constant $c\in(0,\infty)$, and that $\log S$ is square integrable. For $k=1$, $T=S$. For $k\geqslant2$, we write $T=\sum_{i\geqslant1}u_iT_i$, where $T_i:=\sum_{\alpha:\alpha_{|1}=i}w_\alpha/u_i$ is the sum of the weights of the subtree rooted at the node $i$ of depth one. The random variables $(T_i)_{i\geqslant1}$ are i.i.d., independent of $(u_i)_{i\geqslant1}$, and distributed as the sum of the weights of the cascade of depth $k-1$ with parameters $(m_2,\ldots,m_k)$, which by induction has the law of $c'S'$, with $S'$ the sum of a Poisson--Dirichlet point process with parameter $m_2>m_1$; hence $\mathbb{E} T_1^{m_1}<\infty$ by~\cite[Proposition~5.18]{HJbook}, and~\cite[Theorem~5.19]{HJbook} gives $T\stackrel{\mathrm{d}}{=}(\mathbb{E} T_1^{m_1})^{1/m_1}S$. Moreover, $S$ is at least the largest point $u_1$ of the process, whose law is $\mathbb{P}(u_1\leqslant x)=\exp(-x^{-m_1})$, so that $S$ has finite negative moments, and $S$ has finite positive moments of order $p<m_1$ by~\cite[Proposition~5.18]{HJbook}; hence $\log S$ is square integrable, and so is $\log T$, with $\operatorname{Var}(\log T)=\operatorname{Var}(\log S)$.

Set $A:=\log\sum_\alpha w_\alpha\exp(X(\Omega_\alpha))$, so that $\log\sum_\alpha v_\alpha\exp(X(\Omega_\alpha))=A-\log T$. By~\eqref{e.tilted_invariance_weights}, conditionally on $z_\emptyset$, the random variable $\sum_\alpha w_\alpha\exp(X(\Omega_\alpha)-X_0(z_\emptyset))$ has the same law as $T$; since $T$ is independent of $z_\emptyset$, the pair $(z_\emptyset,A)$ therefore has the same law as $(z_\emptyset,X_0(z_\emptyset)+\log T')$, with $T'\stackrel{\mathrm{d}}{=}T$ independent of $z_\emptyset$. Since $X_0(z_\emptyset)$ and $\log T$ are integrable, taking expectations gives $\mathbb{E} A=X_{-1}+\mathbb{E}\log T$, which is~\eqref{e.recursive_formula}. If $X_0(z_\emptyset)$ is square integrable, then $\operatorname{Var}(A)=\operatorname{Var}(X_0(z_\emptyset))+\operatorname{Var}(\log T)$ by independence, and $\operatorname{Var}(A-\log T)\leqslant2\operatorname{Var}(A)+2\operatorname{Var}(\log T)$ gives~\eqref{e.variance_bound_general}. Finally, for~\eqref{e.tilted_marks_one}, conditionally on $z_\emptyset$, \eqref{e.tilted_invariance_weights} gives
\begin{equation*}
    \left\langle\Phi(\Omega_\alpha)\right\rangle_X=\frac{\sum_\alpha w_\alpha\exp\left(X(\Omega_\alpha)-X_0(z_\emptyset)\right)\Phi(\Omega_\alpha)}{\sum_\alpha w_\alpha\exp\left(X(\Omega_\alpha)-X_0(z_\emptyset)\right)}
    \stackrel{\mathrm{d}}{=}\frac{\sum_\alpha w_\alpha\Phi(\Omega'_\alpha)}{\sum_\alpha w_\alpha}=\sum_\alpha v_\alpha\Phi(\Omega'_\alpha).
\end{equation*}
Conditionally on $z_\emptyset$ and on the weights, each $\Omega'_\alpha$ has the conditional law of $\mu_X$ given that its first coordinate is $z_\emptyset$, and $\sum_\alpha v_\alpha=1$; taking expectations, first over the marks, then over the weights, and finally over $z_\emptyset$, gives~\eqref{e.tilted_marks_one}.
<!-- end proof-54 -->
<!-- lemma-39: body_md -->
\label{l.log_S_variance}
There exists $C<\infty$ such that, for every $m\in(0,\frac12]$, the sum $S$ of the points of a Poisson--Dirichlet point process with parameter $m$ satisfies $\operatorname{Var}(\log S)\leqslant Cm^{-2}$.
<!-- end lemma-39 -->
<!-- proof-55: body_md -->
Let $u_1>u_2>\cdots$ be the points of the process, ordered decreasingly, and write $\log S=\log u_1+\log(S/u_1)$. The random variable $E:=u_1^{-m}$ is exponentially distributed with parameter one, so $\operatorname{Var}(\log u_1)=m^{-2}\operatorname{Var}(\log E)$. Conditionally on $u_1$, the remaining points form a Poisson point process on $(0,u_1)$ with intensity $mx^{-m-1}\mathrm{d} x$, so that
\begin{align*}
    \mathbb{E}\left[\frac{S}{u_1}-1\,\Big|\,u_1\right] & =\int_0^{u_1}\frac{x}{u_1}\,mx^{-m-1}\mathrm{d} x=\frac{m}{1-m}E, \\
    \operatorname{Var}\left(\frac S{u_1}\,\Big|\,u_1\right) & =\int_0^{u_1}\frac{x^2}{u_1^2}\,mx^{-m-1}\mathrm{d} x=\frac{m}{2-m}E.
\end{align*}
Since $0\leqslant\log(S/u_1)\leqslant S/u_1-1$, we get $\mathbb{E}[\log(S/u_1)^2]\leqslant\mathbb{E}[(S/u_1-1)^2]\leqslant Cm$ for $m\leqslant\frac12$, and $\operatorname{Var}(\log S)\leqslant2\operatorname{Var}(\log u_1)+2\mathbb{E}[\log(S/u_1)^2]\leqslant Cm^{-2}$.
<!-- end proof-55 -->
<!-- lemma-40: body_md -->
\label{l.tilted_cascade}
Let $\{1,\ldots,n\}=\bigsqcup_{g\in\mathcal G}I_g$ be a partition of the coordinates into groups, and for a leaf $\alpha$ and $g\in\mathcal G$, let $\Omega_{\alpha,g}:=(\Omega_{\alpha,i})_{i\in I_g}$ denote the marks of the coordinates of the group $g$. For every $g\in\mathcal G$, let $X^{(g)}$ be a measurable function of the marks of the group $g$ which is admissible for the cascade with $|I_g|$ marks per node, and set $X(\Omega_\alpha):=\sum_{g\in\mathcal G}X^{(g)}(\Omega_{\alpha,g})$.
\begin{enumerate}
    \item \label{i.tilted_additivity} The function $X$ is admissible, the recursion~\eqref{e.tilted_recursion} is additive: $X_j=\sum_gX^{(g)}_j$ for every $j$, the tilted path law is the product $\mu_X=\bigotimes_{g\in\mathcal G}\mu_{X^{(g)}}$, and
    \begin{equation}
    \label{e.additive_recursion}
        \mathbb{E}\log\sum_{\alpha\in\mathbb{N}^k}v_\alpha\exp\left(X(\Omega_\alpha)\right)=\sum_{g\in\mathcal G}X^{(g)}_{-1}.
    \end{equation}
    \item \label{i.tilted_marks} For every bounded measurable $\Phi$,
    \begin{equation*}
        \mathbb{E}\left\langle\Phi\left((\Omega_{\alpha,g})_{g\in\mathcal G}\right)\right\rangle_X=\int\Phi\,\mathrm{d}\bigotimes_{g\in\mathcal G}\mu_{X^{(g)}}.
    \end{equation*}
    In words, under $\mathbb{E}\left\langle\cdot\right\rangle_X$, the marks of the groups along the sampled leaf are independent, with laws $\mu_{X^{(g)}}$.
    \item \label{i.tilted_variance} Assume moreover that $X^{(g)}_0(z_0)$ is square integrable for every $g$, and let $S$ be as in Corollary~\ref{c.tilted_consequences} if $k\geqslant1$, with the convention $\operatorname{Var}(\log S):=0$ if $k=0$. Then
    \begin{equation*}
        \operatorname{Var}\left(\log\sum_{\alpha\in\mathbb{N}^k}v_\alpha\exp\left(X(\Omega_\alpha)\right)\right)\leqslant2\sum_{g\in\mathcal G}\operatorname{Var}\left(X^{(g)}_0(z_0)\right)+4\operatorname{Var}(\log S).
    \end{equation*}
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-40 -->
<!-- proof-56: body_md -->
Since the marks of different groups are independent at every level, the expectation in~\eqref{e.tilted_recursion} factorizes over the groups, and an induction from $j=k$ down to $j=0$ gives $X_j=\sum_gX^{(g)}_j$, each term being finite by assumption; in particular $X$ is admissible, $X_{-1}=\sum_gX^{(g)}_{-1}$, and the density in~\eqref{e.tilted_path_law} is the product of the corresponding densities of the groups. Part~\eqref{i.tilted_additivity} then follows from~\eqref{e.recursive_formula}, and part~\eqref{i.tilted_marks} from~\eqref{e.tilted_marks_one}. This is the additivity of~\cite[Corollary~5.26]{HJbook}, under the conditional integrability assumption. For part~\eqref{i.tilted_variance}, the case $k=0$ is immediate, since then $\log\sum_\alpha v_\alpha\exp(X(\Omega_\alpha))=X(z_\emptyset)=\sum_gX^{(g)}_0(z_{\emptyset,g})$, whose variance is $\sum_g\operatorname{Var}(X^{(g)}_0(z_0))$ by independence. When $k\geqslant1$, it follows from~\eqref{e.variance_bound_general} and from $\operatorname{Var}(X_0(z_\emptyset))=\sum_g\operatorname{Var}(X^{(g)}_0(z_0))$, again by independence.
<!-- end proof-56 -->
<!-- lemma-41: body_md -->
\label{l.cascade_concentration}
There exists a universal constant $C<\infty$ such that, under the assumptions above,
\begin{equation}
\label{e.cascade_concentration}
    \mathbb{E}\left|\log Z-\mathbb{E}\log Z\right|\leqslant C\,(1+\mathsf V)^{1/2}.
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-41 -->
<!-- proof-57: body_md -->
Throughout the proof, $C$ denotes a universal constant.

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{Step 1: Integrability, and reduction to a finite family.}\par
By Jensen's inequality under $P_N\otimes\mathfrak{R}$, we have $\log Z\geqslant\iint G\,\mathrm{d} P_N\,\mathrm{d}\mathfrak{R}$, and, conditionally on $\mathfrak{R}$, the right-hand side is a Gaussian random variable with mean in $[-\|\mathsf m\|_\infty,\|\mathsf m\|_\infty]$ and variance at most $\mathsf V$; moreover, $\mathbb{E}[Z\mid\mathfrak{R}]=\iint\exp(\mathsf m(\sigma)+\frac12\operatorname{Var} G(\sigma,\alpha))\,\mathrm{d} P_N\,\mathrm{d}\mathfrak{R}\leqslant\exp(\|\mathsf m\|_\infty+\mathsf V/2)$. Hence $\log Z$ is integrable, and, almost surely,
\begin{equation}
\label{e.log_Z_mean_bounds}
    -\|\mathsf m\|_\infty\leqslant\mathbb{E}\left[\log Z\,\Big|\,\mathfrak{R}\right]\leqslant\|\mathsf m\|_\infty+\frac{\mathsf V}2,
\end{equation}
with the same bounds for $\mathbb{E}\log Z$. When $J$ is finite, conditionally on $\mathfrak{R}$, the random variable $\log Z$ is the free energy of the Gaussian field $G$ on $\Sigma_N\times\mathfrak U$, whose variance is at most $\mathsf V$ by~\eqref{e.linear_cascade_variance}, and the Gaussian concentration inequality, in the form used for free energies, see~\cite[Theorem~1.2]{pan} and~\cite[Theorem~4.7]{HJbook}, gives Gaussian tails for $\log Z-\mathbb{E}[\log Z\mid\mathfrak{R}]$, uniformly over the realization of $\mathfrak{R}$; in particular,
\begin{equation}
\label{e.conditional_gaussian_concentration}
    \mathbb{E}\left[\left(\log Z-\mathbb{E}[\log Z\mid\mathfrak{R}]\right)^2\,\Big|\,\mathfrak{R}\right]\leqslant C\mathsf V
\end{equation}
almost surely, and, in view of the paragraph preceding~\eqref{e.log_Z_mean_bounds}, $\log Z$ has finite moments of all orders.

We now reduce to the case of a finite family. Let $Z^{(n)}$ be the partition function of the Hamiltonian $G^{(n)}$ obtained by restricting the sum in~\eqref{e.linear_cascade_hamiltonian} to $J_n$, with Gibbs bracket $\left\langle\cdot\right\rangle_{(n)}$, and let $T_n:=G-G^{(n)}=\sum_{j\notin J_n}w_j(\alpha)\phi_j(\sigma)$, so that
\begin{equation*}
    \log Z-\log Z^{(n)}=\log\left\langle\exp(T_n)\right\rangle_{(n)}.
\end{equation*}
Conditionally on $\mathfrak{R}$, the field $T_n$ is centered Gaussian, independent of $G^{(n)}$, with variance at most $\varepsilon_n:=\sup_\sigma\sum_{j\notin J_n}\rho_j(1)\phi_j(\sigma)^2$, which tends to zero by~\eqref{e.linear_cascade_tail}. By Jensen's inequality and the inequality $\log u\leqslant u-1$, we have $\left\langle T_n\right\rangle_{(n)}\leqslant\log Z-\log Z^{(n)}\leqslant\left\langle\exp(T_n)\right\rangle_{(n)}-1$. Averaging first over $T_n$, with the bracket $\left\langle\cdot\right\rangle_{(n)}$ frozen, we get $\mathbb{E}\left\langle T_n\right\rangle_{(n)}^2\leqslant\mathbb{E}\left\langle T_n^2\right\rangle_{(n)}\leqslant\varepsilon_n$ and
\begin{equation*}
    \mathbb{E}\left[\left(\left\langle\exp(T_n)\right\rangle_{(n)}-1\right)^2\right]=\mathbb{E}\left\langle\exp\left(T_n(z)+T_n(z')\right)\right\rangle_{(n)}-2\,\mathbb{E}\left\langle\exp(T_n)\right\rangle_{(n)}+1\leqslant e^{2\varepsilon_n}-1,
\end{equation*}
where $z=(\sigma,\alpha)$ and $z'=(\sigma',\alpha')$ denote two replicas. Hence $\mathbb{E}|\log Z-\log Z^{(n)}|\leqslant\varepsilon_n^{1/2}+(e^{2\varepsilon_n}-1)^{1/2}$, which tends to zero as $n\to\infty$, and
\begin{equation*}
    \mathbb{E}|\log Z-\mathbb{E}\log Z|\leqslant2\,\mathbb{E}\left|\log Z-\log Z^{(n)}\right|+\mathbb{E}\left|\log Z^{(n)}-\mathbb{E}\log Z^{(n)}\right|.
\end{equation*}
Since $G^{(n)}$ is again of the form~\eqref{e.linear_cascade_hamiltonian} and satisfies~\eqref{e.linear_cascade_variance} with the same $\mathsf V$, it therefore suffices to prove the lemma when $J$ is finite, which we assume from now on. We also fix $\delta\in(0,\frac12]$, to be chosen at the end.

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{Step 2: Flattening of the paths on $[0,\delta)$.}\par
For $j\in J$, let $\tilde\rho_j(u):=\rho_j(u\vee\delta)$, which belongs to $\mathcal Q_\infty$, coincides with $\rho_j$ on $[\delta,1]$, and satisfies $0\leqslant\tilde\rho_j-\rho_j\leqslant\rho_j(1)\mathds{1}_{[0,\delta)}$. Let $(\tilde w_j)_{j\in J}$ be independent cascade fields with covariances $\tilde\rho_j(\alpha\wedge\alpha')$, independent of $(w_j)_{j\in J}$ and of $G_0$ conditionally on $\mathfrak{R}$, and, for $a\in[0,1]$, let $G^a$ be defined by~\eqref{e.linear_cascade_hamiltonian} with $w^a_j:=\sqrt{1-a}\,w_j+\sqrt a\,\tilde w_j$ in place of $w_j$, with partition function $Z_a$ and bracket $\left\langle\cdot\right\rangle_a$. The field $w^a_j$ has covariance $((1-a)\rho_j+a\tilde\rho_j)(\alpha\wedge\alpha')$, so that $G^a$ is again of the form~\eqref{e.linear_cascade_hamiltonian}, with the same~$\mathsf V$, and $Z_0=Z$, while $\widetilde Z:=Z_1$ is the partition function of the flattened model. The derivative in~$a$ of the covariance of $G^a$ is
\begin{equation*}
    \Delta(\sigma,\alpha;\sigma',\alpha'):=\sum_{j\in J}\left(\tilde\rho_j-\rho_j\right)(\alpha\wedge\alpha')\,\phi_j(\sigma)\phi_j(\sigma'),
\end{equation*}
which vanishes when $\alpha=\alpha'$, since $\tilde\rho_j(1)=\rho_j(1)$, and satisfies $|\Delta(\sigma,\alpha;\sigma',\alpha')|\leqslant\mathsf V\mathds{1}_{\{\alpha\wedge\alpha'<\delta\}}$ by the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality and~\eqref{e.linear_cascade_variance}. We compare the conditional expectations
\begin{equation*}
    \mu:=\mathbb{E}\left[\log Z\,\Big|\,\mathfrak{R}\right]
    \qquad\text{and}\qquad
    \tilde\mu:=\mathbb{E}\left[\log\widetilde Z\,\Big|\,\mathfrak{R}\right],
\end{equation*}
which integrate the Gaussian fields with the cascade frozen. Conditionally on $\mathfrak{R}$, the family $(G^a)_{a\in[0,1]}$ is a Gaussian interpolation, and Gaussian integration by parts, as in the proof of Lemma~\ref{l.gaussian_comparison_covariance_norm}, gives
\begin{equation}
\label{e.conditional_interpolation}
    \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d} a}\mathbb{E}\left[\log Z_a\,\Big|\,\mathfrak{R}\right]=-\frac12\mathbb{E}\left[\left\langle\Delta(z,z')\right\rangle_a\,\Big|\,\mathfrak{R}\right],
\end{equation}
where $z=(\sigma,\alpha)$ and $z'=(\sigma',\alpha')$ denote two replicas, the diagonal term of the integration by parts vanishing since $\Delta(z,z)=0$. By the invariance~\eqref{e.invariance_cascade}, applied conditionally on $G_0$, the overlap $\alpha\wedge\alpha'$ is uniformly distributed on $[0,1]$ under $\mathbb{E}\left\langle\cdot\right\rangle_a$, so that $\mathbb{E}\left\langle|\Delta(z,z')|\right\rangle_a\leqslant\mathsf V\delta$ for every $a\in[0,1]$. Integrating~\eqref{e.conditional_interpolation} over $a\in[0,1]$ and taking expectations, we obtain
\begin{equation}
\label{e.coarsening_interpolation}
    \mathbb{E}|\mu-\tilde\mu|\leqslant\frac12\mathsf V\delta.
\end{equation}
Since $\mathbb{E}\mu=\mathbb{E}\log Z$ and $\mathbb{E}\tilde\mu=\mathbb{E}\log\widetilde Z$, the triangle inequality gives
\begin{equation*}
    \mathbb{E}|\log Z-\mathbb{E}\log Z|\leqslant\mathbb{E}|\log Z-\mu|+2\,\mathbb{E}|\mu-\tilde\mu|+\mathbb{E}|\tilde\mu-\mathbb{E}\tilde\mu|.
\end{equation*}
We bound the first term by~\eqref{e.conditional_gaussian_concentration}, the second one by~\eqref{e.coarsening_interpolation}, and the last one by the conditional Jensen inequality $\mathbb{E}|\tilde\mu-\mathbb{E}\tilde\mu|\leqslant\mathbb{E}|\log\widetilde Z-\mathbb{E}\log\widetilde Z|\leqslant \operatorname{Var}(\log\widetilde Z)^{1/2}$, and we get
\begin{equation}
\label{e.coarsening_reduction}
    \mathbb{E}|\log Z-\mathbb{E}\log Z|\leqslant C\mathsf V^{1/2}+\mathsf V\delta+\operatorname{Var}\left(\log\widetilde Z\right)^{1/2}.
\end{equation}
It remains to bound the variance of the free energy of the flattened model.

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{Step 3: Discrete approximation of the flattened model.}\par
The flattened Hamiltonian depends on the cascade only through $(\alpha\wedge\alpha')\vee\delta$, since $\tilde\rho_j(u)=\tilde\rho_j(u\vee\delta)$. For $K\in\mathbb{N}$, consider the discrete cascade of depth $K$ with parameters $m_1:=\delta$ and $m_{l+1}:=\delta+l(1-\delta)/K$ for $1\leqslant l\leqslant K$, so that $m_{K+1}=1$, and and let $\hat\rho_j$ be such that $\hat\rho_j=\rho_j(\delta)$ on $[0,\delta)$ and $\hat\rho_j=\rho_j(m_l)$ on $[m_l,m_{l+1})$ for $l\geqslant1$. Let $\widetilde Z^{(K)}$ be the partition sum obtained by replacing, in the flattened model, the cascade $\mathfrak{R}$ by this discrete cascade and the fields $\tilde w_j$ by the discrete fields $\mathsf w^{\hat\rho_j}_j$ of~\eqref{e.discrete_field}, built from independent families of marks. As $K\to\infty$, the array $(m_{\alpha^\ell\wedge\alpha^{\ell'}}\vee\delta)_{\ell,\ell'\leqslant n'}$ of the discrete cascade converges in law to $((\alpha^\ell\wedge\alpha^{\ell'})\vee\delta)_{\ell,\ell'\leqslant n'}$ under $\mathbb{E}\left\langle\cdot\right\rangle_\mathfrak{R}$, for every $n'$, by~\cite[Corollary~5.32]{HJbook}, and since the off-diagonal overlaps are uniformly distributed while the paths $\tilde\rho_j$ have countably many discontinuities, the arrays $(\hat\rho_j(m_{\alpha^\ell\wedge\alpha^{\ell'}}))_{j,\ell,\ell'}$ converge in law to $(\tilde\rho_j(\alpha^\ell\wedge\alpha^{\ell'}))_{j,\ell,\ell'}$. Let $A>\|\mathsf m\|_\infty+\mathsf V$, and let $\log_A:=(-A)\vee(\log\wedge A)$. The argument of the proof of~\cite[Proposition~4.8]{chen2025free}, based on~\cite[Propositions~4.4 and~4.6]{chen2025free}, shows that $\mathbb{E}\log_A\widetilde Z$ and $\mathbb{E}(\log_A\widetilde Z)^2$ are, up to an error which can be made arbitrarily small uniformly over the cascades under consideration, expectations of bounded continuous functions of these arrays: one truncates the Gaussian fields, using their Gaussian tails, approximates the bounded continuous functions $\log_A$ and $(\log_A)^2$ by polynomials on the compact range of the truncated partition function, and observes that the expectation of a polynomial in the partition function is, after integrating the Gaussian fields, a continuous function of the overlap array of finitely many replicas. Consequently, $\operatorname{Var}(\log_A\widetilde Z)=\lim_{K\to\infty}\operatorname{Var}(\log_A\widetilde Z^{(K)})$. Since $\log_A$ is the projection of $\log$ onto $[-A,A]$, and since $\mathbb{E}\log\widetilde Z^{(K)}$ lies in $[-\|\mathsf m\|_\infty,\|\mathsf m\|_\infty+\mathsf V/2]\subseteq[-A,A]$, by~\eqref{e.log_Z_mean_bounds}, whose proof applies verbatim to the discrete model, we have $\operatorname{Var}(\log_A\widetilde Z^{(K)})\leqslant\mathbb{E}[(\log_A\widetilde Z^{(K)}-\mathbb{E}\log\widetilde Z^{(K)})^2]\leqslant \operatorname{Var}(\log\widetilde Z^{(K)})$. Letting $A\to\infty$, and using that $\log\widetilde Z$ is square integrable, by Step~1 applied to the flattened model, we conclude that
\begin{equation}
\label{e.coarsened_discrete_variance}
    \operatorname{Var}(\log\widetilde Z)\leqslant\liminf_{K\to\infty}\operatorname{Var}\left(\log\widetilde Z^{(K)}\right).
\end{equation}

\smallskip

\noindent\emph{Step 4: The discrete bound.}\par
We fix $K$. In the notation of Appendix~\ref{s.app_cascade}, with $n=|J|$ marks per node, we have 
\begin{equation*}
\log\widetilde Z^{(K)}=\log\sum_{\alpha\in\mathbb{N}^K}v_\alpha\exp(X(\Omega_\alpha)),
\end{equation*}
where
\begin{align*}
    X(\Omega_\alpha)&:=\log\int\exp\Big(G_0(\sigma)+\mathsf m(\sigma)+\sum_{j\in J}\mathsf w^{\hat\rho_j}_j(\alpha)\phi_j(\sigma)\Big)P_N(\mathrm{d}\sigma),
    \\
    \mathsf w^{\hat\rho_j}_j(\alpha)&=\sum_{l=0}^K\left(\hat\rho_{j,l}-\hat\rho_{j,l-1}\right)^{1/2}z_{\alpha_{|l},j},
\end{align*}
The gradient of $X$ with respect to the marks is a Gibbs average of $((\hat\rho_{j,l}-\hat\rho_{j,l-1})^{1/2}\phi_j(\sigma))_{j,l}$, whose norm is at most $(\sum_j\hat\rho_j(1)\phi_j(\sigma)^2)^{1/2}\leqslant\mathsf V^{1/2}$; hence $X$ is Lipschitz with respect to these variables, and admissible. Conditionally on $G_0$, the variance bound~\eqref{e.variance_bound_general} and the recursive formula~\eqref{e.recursive_formula} give
\begin{align*}
    \operatorname{Var}\left(\log\widetilde Z^{(K)}\,\Big|\,G_0\right)&\leqslant2\operatorname{Var}\left(X_0(z_\emptyset)\,\Big|\,G_0\right)+4\operatorname{Var}(\log S)
    \\
    \text{and}\qquad
    \mathbb{E}\left[\log\widetilde Z^{(K)}\,\Big|\,G_0\right]&=\mathbb{E}\left[X_0(z_\emptyset)\,\Big|\,G_0\right],
\end{align*}
where $S$ is the sum of the points of a Poisson--Dirichlet point process with parameter $m_1=\delta$, so that $\operatorname{Var}(\log S)\leqslant C\delta^{-2}$ by Lemma~\ref{l.log_S_variance}. Combining the two identities through the decomposition of the variance into conditional variance and variance of the conditional expectation, we obtain
\begin{equation*}
    \operatorname{Var}\left(\log\widetilde Z^{(K)}\right)\leqslant2\operatorname{Var}\left(X_0(z_\emptyset)\right)+C\delta^{-2},
\end{equation*}
where the variance of $X_0(z_\emptyset)$ is now taken over $G_0$ and $z_\emptyset$ jointly. The random variable $X_0(z_\emptyset)$ depends on $G_0$ and $z_\emptyset$ only through the centered Gaussian field $\mathsf G(\sigma):=G_0(\sigma)+\sum_{j\in J}\hat\rho_{j,0}^{1/2}z_{\emptyset,j}\phi_j(\sigma)$ on $\Sigma_N$, whose variance is at most $\mathsf V$ by~\eqref{e.linear_cascade_variance}, since $\hat\rho_{j,0}=\rho_j(\delta)\leqslant\rho_j(1)$. Moreover, $X_K$ is of the form $\log\int\exp(\mathsf G(\sigma)+\cdots)P_N(\mathrm{d}\sigma)$, whose derivative with respect to a bounded perturbation $h$ of the field is $\int h\,\mathrm{d}\nu$ for a probability measure $\nu$ on $\Sigma_N$, and the recursion~\eqref{e.tilted_recursion} averages such derivatives with nonnegative weights summing to one; the same is therefore true of $X_0$. The Gaussian concentration inequality, in the form used for free energies, see~\cite[Theorem~1.2]{pan} and~\cite[Theorem~4.7]{HJbook}, thus applies to $X_0$ as a functional of $\mathsf G$, and gives $\operatorname{Var}(X_0(z_\emptyset))\leqslant C\mathsf V$. Hence $\operatorname{Var}(\log\widetilde Z^{(K)})\leqslant C\mathsf V+C\delta^{-2}$, uniformly in $K$.

\smallskip

\noindent\emph{Step 5: Conclusion.}\par
By~\eqref{e.coarsening_reduction}, \eqref{e.coarsened_discrete_variance}, and Step~4,
\begin{equation*}
    \mathbb{E}|\log Z-\mathbb{E}\log Z|\leqslant C\mathsf V^{1/2}+\mathsf V\delta+C\delta^{-1}.
\end{equation*}
Choosing $\delta:=\min\{\frac12,(1+\mathsf V)^{-1/2}\}$ gives~\eqref{e.cascade_concentration}.
<!-- end proof-57 -->
